items.quote: record crude runs despite the disruptions in Strait of Hormuz. I mentioned about how the crude sourcing has kind of changed between different regions

items.quote: We operate the largest network of store. See, if you look at our competition, the next guy is somewhere around two-and-a-half thousand after dark stores, we look at as an omni channel network, right? We have presence across 5000 plus stores.

items.statement: New energy revenues expected from FY2028

items.statement: Three ethane vessels ordered; one delivered and operating, second en route to US, third delivery imminent
items.quote: Also we have out of the three new ethane vessels that we had ordered we have got delivery of one which has started operating, the second delivery has also happened, the second vessel is now on its way to US for the first load and very shortly we will be getting the delivery of the third vessel also

items.statement: Solar module capacity 6+ GW now, targeting 20 GW early next year; solar cell nearing 5 GW, targeting 20 GW H1 next year

items.statement: BESS facility (pack and container) up to 40 GWh commissioning in next half year; cell capacity 35-40 GWh late next year

items.statement: Domestic oil demand strong at 57 million tonnes; gasoline up 8.5% YoY, diesel up 7.5% YoY

Diesel growth is 7.5%

items.statement: Polymer demand down 3% due to supply constraints; PET demand strong from beverage sector, filament and staple weaker

items.statement: Petrochemicals had fantastic quarter/half-year due to feedstock advantage; ethane-naphtha cracking differential widened to $557 in Q2, up 2.3x YoY
items.quote: ethane and naphtha cracking differential therefore widened to $557 in Q2, and this was up 2.3 times from a year-on-year basis.

items.quote: if you look at diesel, I think it is almost $2.8 a barrel higher sequentially. So even diesel, which is a large production from a refinery has been quite significant.

items.quote: the absolute numbers are naphtha AG to Japan freight increased from $86 in July to $186 a tonne in September of this year almost like 100% increase during the quarter and our quarterly average number was $122 a tonne, which was like three times higher compared to the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Naphtha flows from Middle East dropped from 12.5 to 6.5 million tonnes in quarter; Russian material disappeared from Asian markets
items.quote: naphtha flows from Middle East as I said, dropped from almost 12.5 million tonnes to 6.5 million tonnes in the quarter, which meant that there was a serious shortage of material all across the region.

items.statement: US ethane feedstock steady at $24.3 vs $23.2 last quarter; provided stable supply during Middle East crisis
items.quote: Ethane prices, as I said, were quite steady during the quarter 24.3 versus 23.2 in the last one.

items.statement: Retail online growth 42% YoY; focusing on mindful customer acquisition leveraging 400M existing customers for sustainable LTV/CAC

items.statement: Online retail competition intense with steep discounting; quick commerce players investing heavily in customer acquisition

items.quote: Global oil demand, while it is declining by 2.6 that is the projection of IEA in 2026, next, of course, three months to go and then it is expected to rebound by almost 2 million barrels in next year that is the projection from IEA.

items.statement: IPL media rights renewal early 2027; committed to disciplined bidding and profitable growth philosophy
items.quote: IPL and marquee properties like this are a very core part of our strategic agenda, but we will address this objectively once the tender comes out, keeping the group's philosophy in mind of profitable growth.

items.statement: Jio-bp retail outlets added 85-90; charge points, CNG stations, convenience stores all increased
items.quote: retail outlets added abou t 85 to 90, retail outlets are added, charge points have been added, e-mobility and CBG of course significant growth on a low base

items.statement: Inventory gain expected for the year; channel inventories kept at minimum levels
items.quote: There will be some inventory gain. We anticipate as to there will be inventory gain in this year.

items.quote: We will continue to fund these investments through healthy cash flows and internal accruals while maintaining financial discipline.

items.quote: 9.1 million user additions for the quarter, industry beating numbers, taking the total base to 542.4 million users and like Pankaj said we added 66 million 5G users, 36 million overall net adds

items.quote: 44.2 GB per user per month that is the kind of metric. See how it has moved consistently every quarter since the last one year from 38.7 GB per user per month.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of ₹30,188 crores received; added to cash position making company net debt positive.

items.statement: Aim to grow revenue faster than market (e.g., 10% if market grows 8%) and reach double-digit EBITDA margin over time, but timing depends on inflation and investment choices

items.statement: Consumer Products grew 2.4% YoY; Lighting Solutions declined 1.3% YoY; overall revenue growth modest at 1.5%
items.quote: We delivered modest revenue growth of hardly 1.5%.

items.quote: BLDC fans for us have grown more than 56% and is now close to 17% of our portfolio.

items.quote: So to answer your question, we have taken one round of price increase in lighting in October. And we are evaluating if we need to take a price increase in Consumer Products, which at this stage seems to be the case, yes.

items.quote: From a channel perspective, our e-commerce has grown in double digits this quarter and focus on exports are also yielding results with growth -- with very strong growth.

items.statement: Commodity costs remain elevated; geopolitical uncertainty persists; inflation on metals and plastics emerging; fan portfolio transition risk if BLDC ramp delayed

items.statement: Order book INR 731 cr as of 30 Sep 2026 (INR 632 cr domestic, INR 99 cr export); Power Cable & specialized conductors INR 575 cr; HTLS order book INR 200 cr+ as of date
items.quote: Our order book as of 30th September '26 stood at INR 731 crores, comprising INR 632 crores of domestic orders and INR 99 crores of export orders.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 operating margin 7.3% vs 6.6% Q1 FY27 and 1.3% Q2 FY26; target to exceed FY25 operating margins by Q4 FY27 and reach ~8% operating margin by Q4 FY27
items.quote: Operating profit for the quarter was INR 40.9 crores with an operating margin of 7.3% as against 6.6% in Q1 FY27 and 1.3% in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: HTLS product carries double-digit margins; INR 200 cr+ HTLS order book to aid margin improvement; HTLS to help exceed FY25 margins more comfortably
items.quote: HTLS by itself could give us double-digit margins. But then HTLS order book is roughly INR200 crores as of now.

items.statement: Structural drivers strong: grid strengthening, renewables, railways/metro, data centers; multiyear programs reflected in inquiries and order flow
items.quote: Transmission and distribution investments, renewable capacity addition, railways and metro electrification, and the buildout of large data centers all remain supportive throughout the quarter.

items.statement: HTLS (carbon-core and gap-type up to 765 kV), EHV cables up to 220 kV, e-beam cables, rubber cables identified as margin-accretive growth segments; Narmadapuram to house these
items.quote: Narmadapuram is what allows us to move up the value chain with EHV cables up to 220 kV, specialized conductors, including HTLS and e-beam cables.

items.statement: Data center approvals established with leading developers representing substantial share of hyperscale/colocation capex; approvals with others progressing
items.quote: We have established approvals with leading data center developers and the customers where we are approved, represent a substantial share of the hyperscale and colocation capex being planned in the country.

items.statement: U.S. tariff framework stabilized post Supreme Court ruling; Indian cables at par with Asian/European competitors; U.S. distributors regaining confidence
items.quote: Today, Indian cables are at par with the competing exporting countries in Asia and Europe. One expects that the tariff framework in the U.S. now rests on a more stable footing than sudden changes that we lived through last year.

items.statement: Net working capital 108 days (vs 101 days end FY26) due to accelerated supplier payments post equity raise; receivables improved 79 to 66 days; target 90-100 days in H2 FY27
items.quote: Our net working capital stood at 108 days versus 101 days at the end of FY26. This reflects basically the accelerated supplier payments post our equity raise.

items.statement: Net worth INR 920 cr; debt-equity 0.14x; long-term loans to be tied up for Narmadapuram; debt-equity expected ~0.3x post commissioning, not exceeding 0.6-0.7x
items.quote: Our net worth stood at INR 920 crores as of 30th September '26, and our debt-equity ratio remains comfortable at 0.14x.

items.statement: National Electricity Plan projects INR 5 lakh cr investment in EHV transmission lines 2027-2032; management estimates HTLS reconductoring market ~INR 50,000 cr over next 5 years
items.quote: As per our internal assessment of the tenders announced by multiple utilities, state governments and central government authorities, the management projects the market size for reconductoring projects of HTLS to be approximately INR 50,000 crores in the next 5 years.

items.statement: No ambition to enter high-advertising B2C house wire segment (~INR 100 cr of ~INR 2,000 cr revenue); B2B strength from 70-year footprint and approvals; new Narmadapuram products face less competition
items.quote: We do not have any ambitions to jump into that extra competitive, high advertising cost and high distribution cost segment. We have a very limited exposure to B2C business, and that is quite steady.

items.statement: U.S. IEEPA tariffs struck down by Supreme Court in Feb 2026; tariff framework now stable; customers carry tariff changes to their account
items.quote: As you know, the IEEPA tariffs was shut down by the U.S. Supreme Court in February. Today, Indian cables are at par with the competing exporting countries in Asia and Europe.

items.statement: Metal booking discipline: firm-price orders booked next working day; no firm-price orders beyond 3-4 months delivery; aluminum >75% of metal value consumption; aluminum softened in quarter
items.quote: The day we receive a firm-price order, the next working day we book the metal, and mostly, we do not accept firm-price orders beyond 3 to 4 months delivery.

items.statement: Metal price volatility and global trade environment remain key challenges; HTLS execution involves EPC/installation with potentially longer deliveries; 220 kV approvals take 1-1.5 years
items.quote: The wires and cable industry continued to navigate two familiar challenges this quarter- metal price volatility and the global trade environment that is still settling down.

items.statement: Consolidated FY27 capex increased to about INR150 crores across fasteners, DC contactors and MCUs
items.quote: We are also increasing our overall FY27 capex to about INR150 crores across all our businesses of fasteners, DC contactors and MCUs.

items.statement: Fastener capex plan raised from INR80 crores to about INR110 crores; INR25 crores already incurred
items.quote: Against our earlier capex plan of INR80 crores for fasteners business, we have already incurred about INR25 crores and our total fastener capex plans within the range of about INR110 crores now.

items.statement: Stand-alone fastener capex ramped up to INR120 crores for FY27; expected to add roughly INR150 crores revenue capacity
items.quote: Our -- on our stand-alone fasteners business, the initial capex plan was INR80 crores, which has been ramped up to maybe close to more like INR130 crores this year -- sorry, INR120 crores this year.

items.statement: SEM capex INR20 crores and STML capex INR10 crores included in consolidated INR150 crores
items.value: INR20 crores SEM, INR10 crores STML
items.quote: So our overall capex at a consolidated level will be about INR150 crores. INR20 crores is going to happen at SEM and about INR10-odd crores at STML.

items.statement: Stand-alone revenue grew 32% YoY in Q2 FY27 vs industry 18%; H1 grew 28% vs industry 20%
items.quote: While industry sales grew by approximately 18% in Q2 FY27, our stand-alone revenue increased by around 32% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: CV segment strong traction, particularly high volumes from a marquee customer driving outperformance
items.quote: A key driver has been strong traction in the CV segment, particularly high volumes from a marquee customer.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA up 17% YoY to INR58.7 crores; Q2 EBITDA up 8% YoY to INR27.7 crores; PAT lower due to exceptional gain in prior year
items.quote: Our H1 EBITDA increased by 17% year-on-year to INR58.7 crores, whereas for Q2 FY27, EBITDA increased to INR27.7 crores, reflecting a growth of around 8% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Near-term margin pressure from input cost inflation; low-cost inventory exhausted in Q1; pass-through with time lag
items.quote: As discussed on our previous earnings calls, we exhausted most of our earlier low-cost inventory in Q1. At the same time, commodity and non-commodity input costs have increased significantly amid the ongoing West Asia conflict.

items.statement: Expect margins to improve over coming quarters as higher costs progressively recovered, subject to input prices
items.quote: As the higher costs are progressively recovered, we expect margins to improve over the coming quarters, subject to input price movements and broader operating environment.

items.statement: Fastener EBITDA margin historically 15-16%; hope to maintain but exceptional inflation may cause marginal pressure this year
items.quote: On the fasteners business, we've been hovering between 15% and 16% EBITDA. Like I said a little while ago, we hope to maintain that. But this year is an exceptional year.

items.statement: Target to reach 15% EBITDA margin by Q4 FY27 on quarterly basis
items.quote: We are hoping that. That's correct.

items.statement: Input costs up dramatically: some commodities up 300%, others 30-50%; tungsten carbide up over 300% in 12 months
items.quote: We have seen where input costs have gone up by some commodities as much as 300%, some by 30%, 40%, 50%. So the inflationary impact has been substantial.

items.statement: Price pass-through negotiations ongoing with OEMs; some agreed, some under negotiation, some retrospective; expect substantial compensation in H2
items.quote: We are negotiating with our customers for price increases, not only on account of steel, which is a normal practice running for years, but this year exceptional item is inflation and cost increases.

items.statement: Price recovery expected in Q3 and Q4 with retrospective effect
items.quote: Correct. And some of those price increases will have a retrospective effect as well.

items.statement: SEM revenue INR23 crores in Q2, INR37 crores H1; 80% QoQ growth driven by higher-value CV/LCV applications
items.quote: Revenue from this business stood at approximately INR23 crores in Q2 FY27, taking H1FY27 revenue to around INR37 crores.

items.statement: SEM targeting INR150 crores annual revenue for breakeven; expect to outperform in FY28
items.quote: Once we reach a revenue of INR150 crores plus, we'll probably achieve breakeven point at that time.

items.statement: SEM production lines for onboard chargers and multifunction units commissioned in Q2; revenue ramp from Q3/Q4 as customer SOPs start
items.quote: The production lines for onboard chargers and multifunction units scheduled for commissioning in Q2 has been commissioned as planned.

items.statement: SEM has 42 active programs, 23 business contracts; 5 new contracts entering production by year-end
items.quote: We've got 5 new contracts that are coming into production by the end of this year.

items.statement: STML commercial supplies of high-voltage DC contactors and relays commenced in Q2 FY27 as scheduled
items.quote: Commercial supplies, which were scheduled to begin in Q2 FY27, have now commenced.

items.statement: CV growth driven by existing OEMs (Tata, Leyland, Volvo, Mahindra, Daimler Benz, Swaraj Mazda); no new customers in fasteners
items.quote: All -- these are all incumbents. There have been no really new customers or new operators in that segment. So it's existing customers like Tata, Leyland, V olvo, Mahindra, Daimler Benz

items.statement: Fastener business has all major OEMs onboarded; focus on increasing share of wallet and new product development
items.quote: We are already working with pretty much all the customers. There are no major customers to be acquired in that fasteners space.

items.statement: No pricing or volume pressure from competitor acquisition by Italian company; strong position due to quality, service, capacity, 4-decade relationships
items.quote: Despite that acquisition of that competitor by an Italian company, we don't feel any pressure coming to us on account of that. There is no pricing pressure. There is no volume pressure.

items.statement: Debt increased due to INR40 crores subsidiary investment, higher capex funding, higher working capital from 30% revenue growth, and strategic raw material inventory build-up
items.quote: I think the debt has gone up by 2, 3 reasons. One, we have done a INR40 crores investment in our subsidiaries this year, SEM and STML, which was announced in the last quarter's results.

items.statement: New CFO Amit Dhadda appointed with nearly 3 decades experience across finance, taxation, audit, corporate reporting, financial control
items.quote: I would like to introduce our newly appointed CFO, Mr. Amit Dhadda. Mr. Dhadda brings nearly 3 decades of experience across finance, taxation, audit, corporate reporting and financial control.

items.statement: Industry Q2 FY27 domestic sales grew ~18% YoY to 83.88 lakh units; H2 expected positive momentum from festive demand, new launches, infra spending, fleet replacement
items.quote: The Indian automobile industry recorded its highest ever second quarter sales across major vehicle segments in Q2 FY27. Domestic sales grew approximately 18% year-on-year to 83.88 lakh units.

items.statement: Inflation, potential interest rate increases, geopolitical uncertainties remain key factors to watch for industry
items.quote: However, inflation, potential interest rate increases and geopolitical uncertainties remain important factors to watch.

items.statement: AEM advanced motor PoC delayed; one PoC expected by end-November, second put on hold by customer due to inflationary pressure
items.quote: One PoC is delayed, but expected to be completed by the end of November. The second PoC has been put on hold by the customer because of the inflationary pressure that they were facing.

items.statement: Credit growth target 2-3% above industry level
items.quote: We are very conscious with improving our credit growth through secured lending while venturing into other avenues to achieve the credit growth of 2%, 3% above the industry.

items.statement: NIM guidance 3.85-3.95% for Q3 and Q4 FY27
items.quote: Hence, we project NIM in the range of 3.85% to 3.95% for Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: ROA expected above 1.6% for FY27
items.quote: ROA is expected to move above 1.6% plus range.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio guidance 45-47% for FY27
items.quote: Our cost-to-income will largely be in the range of 45% to 47% for FY27.

items.statement: Advances grew 26% YoY to INR 72,442 crores in 2QFY27
items.quote: We had registered 26% advance growth in 2QFY27 year-on-year, and our advance have increased to INR 72,442 crores from INR 57,561 crores in 2QFY26.

items.statement: MSME advances increased by INR 2,600 crores to INR 42,862 crores
items.quote: Our core strength, MSME, has increased by INR 2,600 crores, that is, from INR 40,262 crores to INR 42,862 crores.

items.statement: Secured retail loans grew by INR 1,134 crores to INR 7,802 crores
items.quote: And the new segment, secured retail loans, increased by INR 1,134 crores, that is, from INR 6,668 crores to INR 7,802 crores.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio increased by INR 1,062 crores to INR 21,777 crores
items.quote: The gold loan has also increased by INR 1,062 crores during the quarter, from INR 20,715 crores to INR 21,777 crores.

items.statement: Deposits grew 21% YoY to INR 83,893 crores in 2QFY27
items.quote: Our deposits grew 21% to INR 83,893 crores in 2QFY27, up from INR 69,486 crores in 2QFY26.

items.statement: CASA ratio remained constant at 27% of total deposits
items.quote: The CASA percentage of the total deposits remained constant at 27% this quarter.

items.statement: NIM increased to 3.87% in 2QFY27 from 3.78% in 1QFY27
items.quote: Thus, our NIM has increased from 3.78% in 1QFY27 to 3.87% in 2QFY27.

items.statement: Yield on advances improved to 9.85% in 2QFY27 from 9.79% in 1QFY27
items.quote: Our yield on advances improved to 9.85% in 2QFY27 from 9.79% in 1QFY27.

items.statement: Cost of deposits remained stagnant at 5.56% in 2QFY27
items.quote: At the same time, the cost of deposits remained stagnant at 5.56% for 2QFY27 when compared to 1QFY27.

items.statement: 55% of loan portfolio linked to EBLR, 33% fixed rate, 12% MCLR
items.quote: We have around 55% of the loan portfolio linked to the EBLR. However, deposit rates have not witnessed any immediate change as ample liquidity continues to be available in the banking system, supported by inflows under the FCNR deposit scheme.

items.statement: Gross NPA reduced to 1.44% in 2QFY27 from 1.73% in 1QFY27
items.quote: Our Gross NPA percentage has reduced to 1.44% in 2QFY27 from 1.73% in 1QFY27 which is 29 bps reduction.

items.statement: Net NPA reduced to 0.48% in 2QFY27 from 0.9% in 2QFY26
items.quote: Similarly, our Net NPA have reduced to 0.48%, which is less than 0.5% now from 0.9% of the last quarter.

items.statement: Slippages INR 175 crores vs recoveries INR 317 crores in 2QFY27
items.quote: For Q2 FY27, the total slippages are INR 175 crores, while the total recoveries for Q2 stood at INR 317 crores, consisting of INR 180 crores from live NPA accounts and INR 137 crores from technically written-off accounts, resulting in negative credit cost.

items.statement: Sold INR 803 crores to ARC for INR 131 crores consideration
items.quote: During the quarter, the bank sold a ccounts to the tune of INR 803 crores, comprising live and technical write-off accounts, against which the provision of INR 792 crores has been made against the INR 803 crores of bank accounts sold to an ARC for a consideration price of INR 131

items.statement: Gold loan SMA accounts INR 173 crores (0.24% of gold advances) as of 30/9/2026
items.quote: As of 30/9/2026, the outstanding SMA accounts under the gold loan portfolio is around INR 173 crores, representing 0.24% of the gold advances.

items.statement: Gold loan Gross NPA INR 9.5 crores, only INR 20 lakhs went for auction
items.quote: The Gross NPA stood at INR 9.5 crores. Since the percentage is immaterial, I have not given it as a percentage. So the Gross NPA is around INR 9.5 crores. Out of INR 9.5 crores, at the moment it became NPA, the auction has gone only for INR 20 lakhs.

items.statement: SMA-2 to gross advances 0.67% in 2QFY27 vs 0.94% in 1QFY27
items.quote: Overall, SMA-2 to total advance stood at 0.67% in 2QFY27, versus 0.94% in 1QFY27.

items.statement: PCR with technical write-off 82%, without technical write-off improved to 67%
items.quote: For 2QFY27, PCR with technical written-off stood at 82% and the PCR without technical written-off has improved to 67% from 63% last year corresponding period.

items.statement: ECL incremental provision requirement INR 299.42 crores as of 30th September 2026
items.quote: So 30th September '26, incremental ECL provision requirement is INR 299.42 crores. The variation is minus 5.36. When we started with 31st March 2025, our incremental ECL provision requirement was INR 445 crores. That has come down to INR 299 crores.

items.statement: Deposit cost expected to increase by 10 bps next quarter
items.quote: We foresee 10 bps increase there, sir.

items.statement: Branch network expanded to 1,000+ branches from 800, new branches delivering consistently
items.quote: We were at 800 branches. Now, as of today, we are at 1,000-plus branches. The newly opened branches have started delivering quite consistently.

items.statement: MSME line utilization improved to 71-72% from 69% in previous quarter
items.quote: We would be around 71% to 72%. We were at 69%, if you recall, in the last call, we did. From 69%, we have moved to 71%, 72% as we speak today.

items.statement: Operating expenses run rate expected at INR 275-280 crores per quarter going forward
items.quote: And you can roughly imagine or roughly assume it's around INR 275 crores going forward.

items.statement: Gold loan LTV norms aligned with RBI revised directions effective 1st April 2026
items.quote: This is aligned with RBI's revised lending against gold and silver collateral directions effective 1st April 2026.

items.statement: Contingent provision of INR 50 crores made for unseen economic uncertainties
items.quote: The bank has made a contingent provision of INR 50 crores during this quarter, specifically designed for unseen economic uncertainties in future.

items.statement: CD ratio average 86% for 2QFY27
items.quote: Our average CD ratio for 2QFY27 stood at 86%.

items.statement: Recurring revenue AUM reached INR 26,737 crores in H1 FY27, up from INR 23,230 crores at end of FY26
items.quote: Recurring revenue AUM reached INR 26,737 crores in H1, which is split across mutual fund, overseas AUM, Smartfolio, PMS, and AIF. This is compared to INR 23,230 in the end of FY26.

items.statement: Lending book stood at INR 780 crores as of end of Q2 FY27 compared to INR 735 crores year back
items.quote: Our lending book stood at INR 780 crores as of end of quarter two compared to INR 735 crores year back.

items.statement: Recurring income in H1 FY27 is 40% of total income, up from 25% in FY23
items.quote: Recurring income in H1 is 40% of the total income, which has grown consistently over the last few years. Just for comparison, recurring income was 25% of the total income in FY23; now it is 40%.

items.statement: Customer assets stood at INR 1.12 lakh crores as of September end, broadly stable sequentially despite healthy gross inflows offset by market correction
items.quote: Customer assets stood at INR1.12 lakhs crores as of September end. Sequentially, reported customer assets were broadly stable. Healthy gross inflows continued during the quarter, but market correction, especially in the month of September, offset some of the underlying inflows.

items.statement: Mutual fund SIP book reached INR 156 crores with approximately 1.78 lakh SIP clients
items.quote: In the mutual fund distribution business, our SIP book reached INR 156 crores, and the number of SIP clients is approximately INR1.78 lakhs.

items.statement: Wealth management annual ARR net flow stood at INR 583 crores in Q2 and INR 1,189 crores in H1 FY27
items.quote: For the wealth management business, annual ARR net flow, which comprises of net flows in mutual fund, third-party products, and insurance, stood at INR 583 crores in quarter two. For H1, it stood at INR1,189 crores.

items.statement: Mutual fund AUM stood at INR 18,449 crores excluding JV
items.quote: Mutual fund AUM stood at INR18,449 crores, excluding the JV.

items.statement: PMS and AIF AUM stood at INR 2,018 crores as of September end, up 39% from INR 1,449 crores at end of March
items.quote: PMS, AIF AUM stood at INR 2,018 crores as of September end, compared to INR 1,449 crores end of March, which is a growth of 39% over March.

items.statement: Asset management net inflows increased to INR 322 crores in Q2 from INR 71 crores same period last year; H1 inflows at INR 408 crores
items.quote: Asset management net inflows increased to INR 322 crores in quarter two compared to INR 71 crores in the same period last year. For the half year, asset management inflows stood at INR 408 crores.

items.statement: Geojit Yield Plus Category III AIF AUM reached INR 248 crores as of September end, up from INR 22 crores a year back
items.quote: Within our alternative investment offering, Geojit Yield Plus, Category III AIF, wit h an absolute return strategy, had an AUM of INR 248 crores as of September end, compared to INR 22 crores a year back

items.statement: Insurance gross premium recorded at INR 175 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: In insurance business, we recorded a gross premium of INR 175 crores in quarter two.

items.statement: GCC business seeing wait-and-watch mode due to geopolitical situation and currency depreciation; no major redemptions observed
items.quote: We have observed that attractive FCNR deposit offering and market conditions were influencing the allocation of investment across prod ucts. Rupee movement and global investment opportunities have also shaped client preferences, including interest rates in the US. We have not noticed any major redemptions in our overseas

items.statement: Investing in technology platforms, IT capabilities, digital onboarding, analytics and operational efficiency; employee benefit expense increased by INR 8.17 crores Y-o-Y due to higher sales headcount, DIFC recruitment, IT team expansion and
items.quote: Employee benefit expense increased by INR 8.17 crores Y-o-Y. This increase was mainly attributable to a higher sales personal headcount, recruitment for our DIFC subsidiary, and expansion of the IT team to support the technology transformation program, and of course, higher incentive in line with the growth of distribution business.

items.statement: Q2 revenue INR 165.82 crores up 2.5% Y-o-Y and 3.38% sequentially; EBITDA INR 36.7 crores; H1 revenue up 6.72%, EBITDA INR 78.23 crores; margins pressured by higher operating costs and lower transaction-linked activity
items.quote: For H1, revenue from operation increased by 6.72%, and EBITDA stood at INR78.23 crores. The half-year performance reflects top-line resilience alongside higher operating cost and lower transaction-linked activity in the cash market.

items.statement: Hiring in technology and field force to be cautious going forward; focus on improving productivity of existing employees rather than aggressive headcount expansion
items.quote: we'll be very cautious in terms of in terms of aggressively increasing the employee count. Our main focus right now is to improve the productivity of the existing employees and having a close look at the cost incurred on these employees

items.statement: Cross-selling focus: only 20% clients hold more than one product; less than 5% penetrated for life insurance and less than 3% for health insurance; mutual fund penetration priority
items.quote: We have close to 20% of our clients who have invested through us in more than one product. And primarily that is brokerage and mutual fund, which is the overlapping one. We have right now penetrated less than 5% of our clients for life insurance and less than 3% for health insurance.

items.statement: No forward-looking statements given for DIFC and Barjeel AMC AUM expectations for H2 FY27
items.quote: We do not give any forward-looking statement. DIFC is still in a very nascent stage, so it may take time. Nonetheless, we don't give any forward-looking statement, sir.

items.statement: Plan to significantly increase recurring revenue income over next 3-5 years to reduce cyclicality risk; long-term strategy not dependent on geopolitical trends
items.quote: No, our plan is to significantly increase the recurring revenue income. This will eventually take care of the cyclicality risk as far as our cash flows are concerned. So, this is part of a long-term strategy that we have built in.

items.statement: FCNR deposits competed with equity investments; post-August closure seeing some inflows; geopolitical situation and currency depreciation keeping NRI clients in wait-and-watch mode; preference for dollar-denominated investments
items.quote: the FCNR, most of the Indian banks did a fantastic job in raising funds from NRIs. And the investment returns were very lucrative such that the equity returns or the level of risk for equity was not comparable. So, we had a lo t of challenge in being able to compete with the FCNR product. But subsequent to the closure in August, we have started seeing some bit of

items.statement: H2 FY27 priorities: increase productivity of existing people, expand cross-selling opportunities aggressively; no numerical guidance given
items.quote: So second half, we will focus on increase in productivity. As I told in the beginning of the conference, and Mr. Menon had told you, that the cross-selling opportunity that we are taking advantage is only minimum at this stage. We intend to expand aggressively and increase the focus on cross-selling so that the productivity increase can come within the customer base itself if there are challenges.

items.statement: Transaction-based income outlook: 80% from cash market (90% delivery), 20% from derivatives; focus on long-term wealth creation not day trading/F&O; delivery volumes 50%+ of cash market
items.quote: When we look at Geojit capital market business, of our cash market volumes, 50% or plus is delivery business. And if you look at the split between equities and derivatives, in terms of income, derivatives constitutes around 20% of the total income, 80% comes from cash, of which 90% comes from delivery business.

items.statement: SIP book at INR 156 crores with 1.78 lakh clients; huge untapped segment for SIP penetration; focus on increasing recurring inflows through mutual fund SIPs
items.quote: So it has grown to INR156 crores. And from what I understand, we are growing quite fast compared to the industry. And like I said in my remark, we have 1.78 lakh clients who have SIP running with us. We still have a huge segment to be still tapped for SIP.

items.statement: Insurance penetration less than 5% for life and 3% for health; cross-selling focus continues; insurance not directly affected by capital market sentiments
items.quote: In terms of life and health, we have not even penetrated 5% or 3% respectively in terms of number of clients. We continue our cross-selling objective. So in terms of the products available to our employees to sell, fortunately, insurance is a product which doesn't have a direct bearing on the capital market.

items.statement: Technology investments are imperative for competitive edge; legacy systems being replaced; branch expansion not aggressive in current market; branches predominantly in Tier 2/3 with lower cost
items.quote: Technology investments are must investments that we are undertaking at this stage. In order to gain market edge in terms of the technology platform as well as the features and products that we have, we need to make investments, and some of the legacy investments are being replaced to gain competitive edge in the market.

items.statement: Buyback/dividend decision deferred; waiting for strategic opportunities; strong balance sheet allows patience
items.quote: To answer your next question with regard to returning to shareholders, etcetera, at the appropriate moment. depending on some of these strategic opportunities that we are seeing, particularly in this market. We will wait in terms of taking a decision, or rather jumping into a decision of giving ca sh back to shareholders

items.statement: No international ventures planned except small announced investment in Bahrain; focus on domestic opportunities
items.quote: No, not at the moment. Vansh Rathod: Not as of now. C. J. George: Not at the moment, except for except for -- we had we had planned a small investment in Bahrain, which was announced, and this was -- which is not a very big investment. Other than that, there is no international investment planned at this stage

items.statement: Asset management business highly profitable (90-95% inflows from group, low distribution cost); plan to grow aggressively and empanel third-party distributors which may slightly reduce EBITDA percentage
items.quote: Since more than 90%, 95% of the inflows come from the group itself, it is a highly profitable business for us. As of now, we are at INR 2,000 crores. On INR 2,000 crores and INR18 crores of top line for the half with a direct cost which is not so significant. So, profitability you are already seeing as a part of the consolidated accounts. But going ahead, we intend to grow this aggressively. Going

items.statement: Recurring income less sensitive to market levels vs transaction income: 6% market drop leads to ~6% AUM/income drop vs 30-40% volume drop in broking; H1 ARR net flows strong led by mutual funds (~INR 400 crores asset management, balance mut
items.quote: Unlike the transaction-led brokerage business, a subdued market doesn't impact the recurring income so much. So, when I compared the mutual fund AUM, end August or beginning of September, it was INR 20,000 crores, and we ended September close to INR 18,500 crores, you would see that the income is not much affected. Unless and until you see you a 20%, 30% drop in the total market, you might not see

items.statement: FY28 overall revenue ambition intact; US $375M target now expected a little beyond FY28
items.quote: Our overall revenue ambition for FY28 is firmly in place. What will change is the regional mix, with Ex -US now contributing more than the US. Our goal was for Ex-US revenue to match the US by FY28, and we have achieved that in Q2 FY27 itself.

items.statement: Ex-US revenue expected upwards of $375M in FY28, mirroring US aspiration
items.quote: With the latest trends that is coming in the non-U.S. markets, it should be upwards of that.

items.statement: H2 FY27 expected stronger than H1 for US business
items.quote: Overall, we expect a better H2 for the US business.

items.statement: Capex around INR300 crores for FY27, slightly lower for FY28
items.quote: Yes. I mean it should be around the INR300 crores mark. If you look at our spends have reduced from Q1 into Q2, and we expect it to be more closer around the INR300 crores mark by the end of the year.

items.statement: Net finance cost expected INR40-45 crores range for H2 FY27
items.quote: It will be within a range between that INR40 crores to INR45 crores.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle expected to improve back to historic levels by next quarter
items.quote: We believe that the cash cycle engines should be back in the next quarter itself.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA ratio expected to stabilize and improve by end of FY27
items.quote: As inventory normalizes and H2 launches and business wins begins to contribute, we remain focused on growth and improving our cash-to-cash cycle. With this, we expect our net debt -to-EBITDA ratio to stabilize and improve by the end of the year.

items.statement: Ex-US demand and order books across key markets remain healthy
items.quote: demand and order books across our key Ex-US markets remain healthy.

items.statement: US B2B partner business saw strong order book and meaningful new business wins
items.quote: Our B2B partner business saw a strong order book, and we secured meaningful new business wins during the quarter, from a partnered product, our recent launches and other key molecules in our portfolio.

items.statement: Gross margin 56% in Q2 FY27, H1 at 58.3%; confident of sustaining H1 gross margins going forward
items.quote: Our material costs rose to 44% of revenues in Q2 from 42.2% last year, reflecting the increase in raw material costs that Badree described. This moderated our gross margins to 56% for Q2. Importantly, for the first half, gross margins stood at a healthy 58.3%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 17.6% in Q2 FY27, compressed by higher material, freight and supply chain costs
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter was INR251 crores, our highest ever at a margin of 17.6%. Higher material, freight and supply chain costs linked to the geopolitical situation compressed our margins and tempered the flow-through of a very strong revenue growth, but it did not hold back the growth in our absolute profitability.

items.statement: Ex-US margins slightly higher than company average EBITDA
items.quote: It should be slightly higher than the company average in terms of the EBITDA because it depends on the B2B as well as the B2C markets. Overall, I think the gross margins and the EBITDA are good in these markets.

items.statement: Ex-US revenue reached INR6,963M in Q2 FY27, up 31% YoY; H1 up 24% YoY to INR12,838M
items.quote: Ex -US revenue for Q2 reached ₹6,963 million, an outstanding 31% growth year -on-year. For H1, revenue was ₹12,838 million, up 24% year -on-year.

items.statement: US revenue INR6,855M ($73M) in Q2 FY27, up 9% YoY and QoQ; H1 up 7% YoY to INR13,137M
items.quote: Revenue for Q2 stood at ₹6,855 million, or $73 million, growing 9% year -on-year and 9% quarter -on-quarter. For H1, US revenue was ₹13,137 million, up 7% year-on-year.

items.statement: Capex and intangibles INR208 crores deployed in H1 FY27 for differentiated pipeline including nasal spray, transdermal patch, controlled substances
items.quote: At the same time, we continue to invest in our future, deploying INR208 crores in capex and intangibles to support our growth platforms. Including our nasal spray and transdermal patch programs, these investments are directed at the differentiated pipeline Badree outlined, including our controlled substances opportunity, which will broaden our addressable market and support margin accretive growth

items.statement: Chestnut Ridge facility has capacity and expertise for US-manufactured controlled substance products including nasal sprays, patches and films
items.quote: Regulations require these products to be manufactured in the US, and our Chestnut Ridge facility already has the capacity and expertise to do exactly that.

items.statement: Material costs rose to 44% of revenue in Q2 from 42.2% last year due to geopolitical situation; alternate sourcing and procurement initiatives underway
items.quote: Our material costs rose to 44% of revenues in Q2 from 42.2% last year, reflecting the increase in raw material costs that Badree described.

items.statement: US portfolio shifting to higher-margin differentiated products; 40+ value-accretive products in active pipeline with filings through FY30
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier, our US portfolio is steadily shifting toward higher-margin, differentiated products. We have more than 40 value-accretive products in our active pipeline, with filings and approvals planned in a phased manner and commercialisation through FY30.

items.statement: Controlled substances portfolio: 5 commercialized products (6% of US revenue, $750M market); 10+ pipeline products across nasal sprays, patches, films expanding addressable market to $4.5B
items.quote: Today, our five commercialised CS products, all oral solid tablets, contribute about 6% of our US revenue an d address a market of around $750 million. While this portfolio is constrained by quota allocations, we have more than 10 CS products in our pipeline across multiple domains, including nasal sprays, patches and films, which will expand our addressable mark et to around $4.5 billion, about s

items.statement: Industry-leading service levels central to winning/retaining business with largest US customers and partners
items.quote: We continue to deliver industry -leading service levels to all our customers. This is a real competitive advantage, and it is central to winning and retaining business with some of the largest customers and partners in the market.

items.statement: Sandoz deal awaiting antitrust approval in few countries, expected to close in Q3 FY27
items.quote: Our deal with Sandoz is now awaiting antitrust approval in only a few countries, and we expect it to close in Q3.

items.statement: Cash-to-cash cycle 137 days in H1 FY27, up 13 days from March 2026; absolute working capital increased INR307 crores (INR174 crores inventory, INR133 crores growth)
items.quote: Our cash -to-cash cycle stood at 137 days. This is up 13 days from March 2026 with absolute working capital increasing by INR307 crores during the first half.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA 1.72x in H1 FY27, up from working capital increase of INR211 crores; OneSource investment valued ~INR290 crores not adjusted
items.quote: On net debt, as we had earlier indicated, the inventory build over the last 2 quarters was expected to lift our net debt -to-EBITDA ratio temporarily. The ratio now stands at 1.72x, reflecting the INR211 crores increase in net debt during H1, driven by working capital.

items.statement: US ANDA portfolio: 230 filed, 212 approved covering 154 products; 75 commercialized products; top-3 market position in 38 products contributing ~70% of US revenue
items.quote: As of October 2026, we have filed 230 ANDAs, of which 212 have been approved, covering 154 products. We also have a basket of approved ANDAs yet to be launched, and we will commercialise these at the opportune ti me. During the quarter, we launched three products, taking our commercialised portfolio to 75 products, up from 72 at the end of Q1. We now hold top -three market positions in 38 products

items.statement: H1 FY27: Revenue INR2,695 crores (+15.1% YoY), EBITDA INR481 crores (+6.9% YoY, 17.8% margin), Operational PAT INR259 crores (+9.8% YoY, EPS INR28.1)
items.quote: H1 FY '27 revenues grew 15.1% to INR2,695 crores. EBITDA grew 6.9% to INR481 crores with a 17.8% EBITDA margin and operational PAT grew 9.8% to INR259 crores with operational of INR28.1 per share.

items.statement: Mr. Biren Gabhawala appointed as Independent Director; Independent Directors now 6 of 10 Board members
items.quote: We are very pleased to welcome Mr. Biren Gabhawala to our Board as an Independent Director. Biren is a Chartered Accountant with more than three decades of experience in financial reporting, audit, taxation and corporate governance, and has chaired the Audit Committees of eClerx Services and 3M India.

items.statement: Ash & Coal Handling revenue growth target 20-25% YoY for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: As we have spoken in the earlier call also, we'll have 20% to 25% of the revenue growth in the years to come.

items.statement: Wind energy EBITDA margin 4-5% and PAT margin 2.5-3% for FY27 and H1 FY28
items.quote: we have EBITDA margin of 4% to 5%, PAT margin of 2.5% to 3% over there. For in the current financial year and the coming financial year till half year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 15-18% for FY27
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin in the stand-alone basis will be between 15% to 18%, which we have spoken during all all the previous call.

items.statement: Ash handling volume target 90,000 metric tonnes per month by Q4 FY27

items.statement: Ash & Coal Handling order book INR 1,700 crore with tenders opening in 1-2 months
items.quote: currently, it's about INR1,700 crores. So can you throw something? Dinesh Agarwal: Yes. I mean, it is more of a tender based compared to wind. We have already participated in large tenders. We expect all that tenders to open in the coming , next 1 months to 2 months

items.statement: Large wind energy order in final price negotiation, expected closure in 30-45 days
items.quote: We are in the final stage of price negotiation. Project execution and ROW issue or land issue, I mean, won't come to us because we are only the equipment supplier. And we are in the final price negotiations closure stage for the large volume of the order. I mean we should close within next 30 days to 45 days time, and we'll announce the sale with it.

items.statement: Wind energy indigenous manufacturing plant operational in 12-14 months, margin impact after 18-24 months
items.quote: Manufacturing plant should be operational within 12 to 14 months. And there will be a real impact of that will take an other 6 months after that on the profitability. Certainly, that will be a good impact on the profitability, after 1 year, 1.5 years in the books of account.

items.statement: RMC business uses capital-light lease-based model with zero capex for plants
items.quote: Importantly, we are adopting a capital-light lease-based model that enables us to scale without significant investment in fixed assets. We believe this is the right way to build the business.

items.statement: First RMC plant at Charholi, Pune (60 cubic meter/hour) started 25 Sep 2026; Hoskote and Kalyan plants also commenced; phased rollout planned across Mumbai, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Chennai
items.quote: Our first RMC plant at Charholi, Pune commenced the operation on 25 September 2026, followed by Hoskote in Karnataka and Kalyan near Mumbai. We are progressing with a phased rollout across Mumbai, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Chennai.

items.statement: Pune RMC plant targeting 4,000-4,500 cubic meters per month
items.quote: We should anticipate volumes of almost about 4,000, 4,500 cubic meters per month from this plant alone.

items.statement: RMC segment expected to contribute to profitability from FY28; FY27 focused on plant setup and team building
items.quote: RMC segment will start contributing to the overall profitability from the coming financial year and it will contribute a good amount to the total profitability. In the current financial year, it will go towards the setting up of the new plant and establishing the team across the location.

items.statement: Receivables cycle 120-130 days; zero overdue and zero bad debt; targeting automation to reduce billing/certification cycle
items.quote: It will be the same 130 days. I mean that's breaking that cycle is not easy. I mean, that is where we are trying to bring some level of automations more, so that billing and certification works happens faster, where that cycle is only under our control.

items.statement: Using TReDS platform for MSME vendor payments; finance cost increase offset by COGS reduction from vendor discounts
items.quote: We have started paying all our vendors through the TReDS platform with a certain cost and also which is benefiting the vendor, and we are also getting an additional discount in the direct cost, there is a good impact on the gross margin at the COGS level, whatever the finance cost increase is getting offset, or we are getting more benefit in the COGS level.

items.statement: Demerger of green mobility business: NCLT hearing adjourned to 11 Nov 2026; expect completion in 2-3 months post approval
items.quote: On the demerger process, we have completed key procedural milestones and the final approval from honorable NCLT is currently awaited. And the matter is listed on 11th of November in the coming months. Subject to the necessary regulatory approval and comple tion of the remaining formalities, we expect this demerger process will get completed within next 2 to 3 months' time

items.statement: Wind energy deliveries commenced to all 3 customers: Torrent, KP Energy, Jindal; foundation erection underway per schedule
items.quote: The business continued to make steady progress during the quarter, with the delivery gaining momentum and initial supplies completed all 3 customers, Torrent, KP Energy and Jindal. Project execution is advancing across the customer side, with foundation er ection activity underway in line with the delivery schedule

items.statement: India installed wind capacity reached 59.2 GW as of Sep 2026
items.quote: As a result, the country total installed wind capacity reached 59.2 gigawatts as on September 2026.

items.statement: Monsoon impacts Q2 ash handling volumes (35,000-40,000 MT in Q2 vs 90,000 target); seasonal revenue fluctuation expected
items.quote: This Q2 was quite less. It was around 35,000 to 40,000. And volume started going up, though there in some part, there was a tsunami or the rain going on for last 1 week, but volume started going up.

name: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd

items.statement: Reiterated FY27 presales guidance of INR9,000 crores; H1 achieved ~INR2,900 crores, targeting ~INR7,000 crores in H2
items.quote: For now, we reiterate the INR9,000 crores presales guidance.

items.statement: Expects FY27 residential revenue recognition of ~INR5,000 crores with EBITDA margin 22-24%
items.quote: It should be INR5,000 crores in rough order of magnitude.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity to remain comfortably under 0.5x by end of FY27 from 0.31 currently
items.quote: consolidated debt-to- equity ratio outlook for the year post funding for projected capex commitments and business development spend is comfortable and will be well within 0.5x

items.statement: Operating cash flow for FY27 expected to be higher than FY26
items.quote: We remain confident of sustaining healthy cash flows in the coming quarters and outlook to generate operating cash flow from operations for the entire financial year higher than that of FY26.

items.statement: H2 launch pipeline of 7 million sq ft with GDV of INR7,600 crores; includes 2 large Bengaluru townships (~INR3,800 crores combined), 1M sq ft each in Chennai and Hyderabad
items.quote: We have INR9,800 crores of inventory in addition to another 7 million square feet or INR7,600 crores Gross Developmental Value (GDV) of launches planned for the second half of the financial year.

items.statement: Residential demand remains strong; IT sector job losses not impacting demand as talent shifts to GCCs; premiumization trend continues
items.quote: We've been maintaining for a long time that despite the net hiring in IT and IT sector and certain companies not being positive, it has not really impacted demand. In fact, demand has actually become more premium while also maintaining growth.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 38% in Q2 FY27 from 26% in Q2 FY26 (+1,200 bps); Real Estate EBITDA margin 24% vs 12% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated revenue for the quarter stood at INR1,250 crores with EBITDA of INR478 crores. The EBITDA margin improved to 38% compared with 26% in Q2 of FY26, an improvement of 1,200 basis points.

items.statement: FY27 Real Estate EBITDA margin expected 22-24%
items.quote: So the margin profile of the entire FY27 would -- in real estate would be in that early 20s, between 22% and 24%, which is what was there in H1 as well.

items.statement: Average realization up 29% YoY to INR13,841/sq ft driven by disciplined pricing and premium mix shift
items.quote: Average realization stood at INR13,841 per square foot, a strong 29% year-on-year improvement, driven by disciplined pricing increases in our existing projects and a sustained shift in contribution of higher-end homes in our overall product mix.

items.statement: H2 launches skewed to INR1-2 cr ticket size (sweet spot); Bengaluru projects largely INR1-1.5 cr (North) and INR2 cr; ~20% at INR3 cr
items.quote: Some of our upcoming launches are in that INR1 crores to INR2 crores range, which is a sweet spot for many customers, especially in Bangalore and Chennai.

items.statement: Office occupier base diversified across GCCs (41% of Q2 leasing), IT, BFSI, engineering, life sciences, flex operators; green certified parks capture 61% market absorption
items.quote: Our occupier base remains well diversified across GCCs, IT, ITES, BFSI, engineering, life sciences and flexible workspace operators. Occupier demand continues to reflect a flight to quality with GCCs accounting for 41% of Q2 office leasing and green certified tech parks capturing 61% of market absorption.

items.statement: Operational leasing portfolio 9.6M sq ft at 90% occupancy; 6.8M sq ft under construction including WTC & Orion Mall Hyderabad; balance capex ~INR3,350 crores
items.quote: We also completed Arcadia at Brigade Cornerstone Utopia in Bengaluru, taking our total operational leasing area to 9.6 million square feet at a portfolio occupancy of 90%.

items.statement: Office capex phasing: INR400 cr in H2 FY27, INR1,500 cr in FY28, INR1,500 cr in FY29; post-FY29 projects include WTC Hyderabad, Brigade Industrial Park, Brigade Icon commercial
items.quote: Balance capex we have to spend for the office in the remaining H2 of '27 is about INR400 crores. In '28, we are expected to spend about INR1,500 crores. And in '29, we're expected to spend another INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: Q2 collections INR1,633 cr (Real Estate INR1,115 cr, Leasing INR343 cr, Hospitality INR175 cr); INR250-260 cr milestone billed in September pending collection
items.quote: Collections for the quarter stood at INR1,633 crores. The reduction in collection number as compared to earlier quarters was primarily due to milestone that got billed in the third month of the quarter and for which collections were in progress.

items.statement: Gross debt INR5,439 cr, net debt INR2,765 cr (cash INR2,674 cr); 85% debt backed by rental/GOP; avg cost of debt 7.61%
items.quote: As of September 30, 2026, the group's consolidated gross debt stood at INR 5,439 crores, and consolidated net debt outstanding was INR 2,765 crores, adjusting for cash and cash equivalent of INR 2,674 crores.

items.quote: So this is investment which came from Bain Capital's fund in first quarter in a SPV called Vibrancy Real Estates Private Limited.

items.statement: Hospitality: ARR INR7,876 (+11% YoY), RevPAR INR5,922 (+10% YoY), occupancy 75%; Bengaluru occupancy 81%, RevPAR +12%; PAT doubled to INR22 cr
items.quote: Portfolio Average Room Revenue (ARR) grew 11% year-on-year to INR7,876 and RevPAR grew 10% year-on-year to INR5,922 at an occupancy of 75%.

items.statement: Retail: Orion Mall portfolio 94% trading occupancy; retailer sales +16% YoY; footfall steady
items.quote: Our Orion Mall portfolio delivered a steady quarter at 94% trading occupancy. Retailer sales across the portfolio grew 16% year-on-year, led by stronger electronics and restaurant sales, while mall footfall remained steady.

items.statement: Chennai launch approvals may slip to next fiscal due to government change; one of two Q4 projects at risk
items.quote: The other one, we're still working to try and get it within Q4, but that one might get pushed out into the next financial year.

items.quote: We have added about 12.5 million, 13 million square feet totally in this financial year for the first half, of which close to about 10 million square feet has come in Q2. This would approximately translate to about INR13,000 crores of GDV.

items.quote: On the sustenance sales, the large contributors were Brigade Eternia in Bangalore and Brigade Belvedere in Bangalore. We also had Brigade Insignia in Bangalore. The other projects are Brigade Gateway Hyderabad, Brigade Icon, Chennai.

items.quote: New leases that we are doing, we are re-leasing the same space at around 15% higher than what it was getting us.

items.statement: Land payments INR440 cr in Q2 split ~half Bengaluru, half Hyderabad; West & East Bengaluru focus
items.quote: It's almost half and half between Bangalore and Hyderabad.

items.statement: Office portfolio to grow from 9.5M to 12.5M sq ft operational by FY29; rental income expected ~INR1,700 cr in FY29
items.quote: By FY29, we expect that to grow to 12.4 million square feet. So if I add even the retail, there we'll be adding a smaller amount. So I would just say 12.5 million square feet, you can expect from 9.5 million to 12.5 million.

items.statement: GRESB ESG score 93.7 (4-Star) for FY26; Brigade Citrine received IGBC Net Zero Carbon (Design) certification

items.statement: Exports expected to sustain at ~7.5 lakh units per quarter

items.statement: Chetak capacity expanding to 80,000 per month by Q4 FY27
items.quote: We are expanding Chetak capacity to 80,000 per month by quarter 4, which will help us get market share and unlock new reach.

items.statement: Exports crossed 7.8 lakh units in Q2 FY27, up 41% YoY; second consecutive quarter above 7 lakh
items.quote: The BU crossed its highest ever volume of 7.8 lakh units in Q2, a growth of 41% year -on-year. This is the second consecutive quarter above 7,00,000 units.

items.statement: Input cost inflation impact 3-3.5% of revenue in Q2; cumulative H1 impact exceptionally steep
items.quote: Taken together, the impact of commodity and other input cost inflation in quarter 2 was in the whereabouts of between 3% and 3.5% of revenue.

items.statement: Calibrated pricing covered 50-60% of H1 inflation impact; balance offset by currency and cost optimization
items.quote: We have responded through calibrated pricing actions, which really have covered about between 50% and 60% of the inflationary impact over this first half.

items.statement: October price hike covers ~30% of estimated Q3 inflation; further hikes dependent on market absorption
items.quote: We have, though, taken some level of calibrated pricing earlier this month to recover a third of the inflationary impact so far.

items.quote: The industry continued to grow rapidly at 75% plus in Q2 and penetration of electric scooters is now 25% of the scooter category.

items.quote: Significantly, the Chetak portfolio profitability has moved to double digits, in fact, at an overall level, our EV business, which includes 3-wheelers and Chetak is now margin accretive at the corporate level.

items.statement: 3W market share ~90% in CNG passenger, >50% in cargo; WEGO e-auto share ~32% in September

items.statement: Spares revenue crossed INR2,000 crore for first time, up 15% YoY

items.statement: BACL AUM ~INR21,000 crore (+1.5x YoY), PAT INR243 crore (+85% YoY), RoE 26%

items.statement: Input cost inflation persists into Q3 across metals, proprietary parts, electrical components; magnitude hard to quantify

items.statement: Currency headwind if INR stays below 95; will not take pricing to cover currency moves
items.quote: if the currency were to be a bit of a headwind, we will not take pricing action to cover currency movement because we know it's a very short-term transient measure.
