We will look at the end of the year if we want to revis

items.statement: Floating rate liabilities 48% of total, floating rate assets 66% of total; structurally positioned to reprice assets with benchmark increases
items.quote: Our asset liability mix provides us flexibility to manage interest rate movements with 48% of our liabilities on floating rates and 66% of our loan portfolio on floating rates, enabling us to reprice our floating assets in response to benchmark rate increases.

items.statement: Plan to raise capital in second half of FY28 based on current growth plans
items.quote: On the capital, based on the current growth plans, we expect to raise capital sometime towards the second half of FY28. We will keep evaluating our capital position as the business grows, and we'll take a call at an appropriate time, but that's the plan as of now.

items.statement: No gold loan portfolio currently; organic gold loan business to launch in coming month
items.quote: So, Manju, we do not have a gold portfolio at this point of time. Our organic business should start in the coming month with the launch of that business. So currently, we do not have a portfolio in this.

items.statement: Mortgage business faces competition from large banks in prime segment; NIM trajectory to be managed via PLR hikes and mix changes
items.quote: you will have some impact like your mortgage business where the large banks will continue to compete in the prime segment. So, on the net, how do you see the NIM trajectory going forward in the H2 of FY '27 and '28.

items.statement: AI embedded across lending value chain: 7.8 crore documents processed, 95% adoption in personal/business loan underwriting, 70% retail applications via AI workflows, AI-powered voice/email for servicing
items.quote: In underwriting, our AI-powered credit intelligence and decisioning engines have processed over 7.8 crores documents and have achieved over 95% adoption across personal loans and business loans underwriting, resulting in meaningful improvements in productivity and turnaround times. Across operations, AI -led workflows now process approximately 70% of retail applications driving productivity gains,

items.statement: Expect to raise capital in second half of FY28, more towards Q3-Q4
items.quote: If you look at the current growth trajectory, we think we'll be required to raise capital by second half of FY28, more towards Q3-Q4.

items.statement: Motor Finance portfolio expected to stabilize in Q3 and start growing from Q4
items.quote: We expect the portfolio to stabilize in Q3 and start growing from Q4. That's the plan as far as Motor Finance is concerned.

items.statement: NIM plus fee expected to be stable in Q3 and show improving trend in Q4
items.quote: As far as our Q3 assessment is concerned, we expect the NIM plus fee in Q3 not to have any further drag. In fact, we expect it to be stable or marginally getting better, but more towards being stable. And based on all the measures which we have taken, our Q4 NIM plus fee should show an improving trend.

items.statement: AUM growth guidance maintained at 23%-25%, will not chase growth at expense of margins
items.quote: We would want to be on the guidance which we have given of 23% -25%. And while we will focus definitely on growth, but we do not want growth at the expense of margins.

items.statement: NIM dropped 10 bps in Q2 vs Q1 due to 5 bps higher cost of funds and 5 bps competitive intensity in prime home loans
items.quote: As far as NIM is concerned, we've seen a drop in Q2 compared to Q1 by about 10 basis points. This is primarily coming in because of two reasons: about 5 bps happening because of increase in cost of funds, which is also in our investor presentation. And another 5 bps impact is happening more because of competitive intensity in the prime home loans business.

items.statement: PLR increased 25 bps for Tata Capital and 20 bps for Tata Capital Housing Finance effective 1st November
items.quote: Tata Capital ALCO decided. Tata Capital Housing Finance decided to increase rates by 20 basis points, and both the increases would be effective from 1st of

items.statement: Structurally well positioned with 66% floating rate assets vs 48% floating rate liabilities in rising rate environment
items.quote: If you look at our liabilities, 48% of our liabilities are floating rate liabilities. On the asset side, 66% of our assets are floating. So structurally, we are very well positioned in a rising rate environment.

items.statement: Housing finance has 95% floating assets and 40% liabilities repricing, giving advantage from PLR hike
items.quote: In our housing portfolio, 95% of our assets are floating. And roughly 40% of our liabilities will get repriced because of the rate increase. So this will give us an advantage to our entire portfolio, this 20 basis points would give a lift.

items.statement: Expect income growth ~25% and cost growth ~15% for the year, supporting margins
items.quote: As far as the year is concerned, we expect if incomes will grow at about 25%, then cost to grow at about 15%. So that should help us.

items.statement: SME growth driven by supply chain financing and term loans, supply chain significantly better this quarter
items.quote: I would say the growth is from both term loans and supply chain, but supply chain obviously has had a better quarter significantly compared to other products.

items.statement: Retail momentum expected to pick up further in Q3 and even more in Q4 across vehicle, housing, affordable and micro housing
items.quote: We, in fact, expect retail momentum growth to further pick up in Q3 and then even more pick up in Q4. So, we are clearly on a trend where the retail business will pick up more. Same is true for our housing business in retail.

items.statement: High-margin business disbursements grew 40% and AUM grew 14%, expected to mirror overall portfolio growth by Q4
items.quote: Our high -margin business has shown a growth of 40% on disbursements and 14% on AUM growth. And this AUM growth of 14%, we expect it to increase with every quarter. And by Q4, it should be mirroring our overall portfolio growth and should start getting better from the next financial year.

items.statement: Supply chain financing diversified from 67% auto to 35% auto over 4 years
items.quote: From a stage, 4 years back where auto used to constitute about 2/3rd of our supply chain, it is now down to about 35%.

items.statement: Overall GNPA stable at 1.9% QoQ, improved YoY; Motor Finance NPA up due to book rundown and seasonality
items.quote: If you look at our overall NPAs, we have been stable at 1.9% compared to last quarter. And same time last year, we have come down. But if you look at Motor Finance, that's gone up. It looks as if it is increasing for two reasons. One, because the book is falling, the denominator is coming down. And second is the fact that it is seasonal.

items.statement: Absolute slippages in Motor Finance significantly lower in Q2 vs Q2 last year
items.quote: And if you look at the absolute slippages, they are significantly lower in Q2 compared to Q2 of last year.

items.statement: Created macro provision of INR30 crores in CV business this quarter
items.quote: We've also, in this quarter, created a macro provision of about INR30 crores in CV business, and we will monitor how it goes ahead in the future.

items.statement: Motor Finance GNPA of INR2,000-2,100 crores mostly from pre-March 2025 portfolio, predominantly Tata vehicles
items.quote: You are right. Majority of it does come from a portfolio before March '25.

items.statement: PCR increase driven by aging of Stage 3 assets and staggered ECL provisioning
items.quote: PCR is on Stage 3 assets, and it often depends on the mix or the aging of the assets which have moved into Stage 3. So we apply the ECL rate and the staggered provisioning over and above when the asset moves into Stage 3, that gives you the PCR.

items.statement: Tightened credit screens in certain SME segments due to crude price impact, monitoring drought/war impact closely
items.quote: So, in certain SME segments, we have tightened our screens, which are part of our secured and unsecured business loans.

items.statement: Insurance commission capping impact unknown pending final guidelines; working on product mix and cost mitigation
items.quote: See, we've not put out any number because we honestly don't know what the final guidelines will be and when they will be effective from. Once we have that, we will look at things. But parallelly, we've been thinking through what we can do in terms of which insu rance products, which we can sell, whether the retail product makes more sense than a group product

items.statement: Fee income up 30% YoY and QoQ driven by 58% YoY growth in assignment income; non-assignment fee income flat
items.quote: the DA income has increased by 58% on a year on year basis. So that's what's contributing, the assignment which we do. Kunal Shah: Which income, sorry. Rakesh Bhatia: The assignment income. Rajiv Sabharwal: So basically, as far as non-assignment income is concerned, it has remained at the same level as it was in Q1 as a percentage

items.statement: PLR hike of 25 bps (Tata Capital) and 20 bps (Housing) effective 1st November, reset for almost all portfolio from that date
items.quote: So this will happen for almost all the portfolio from 1st November. So , it is the date we decide to change the rates from.

items.statement: Motor Finance book proportion declined from 14.5% of total book in March 2025 to 7.7% currently
items.quote: In fact, proportion of that book used to be 14 .5% in our total book in March '25, which is now down to about 7.7%.

items.statement: De-recognition of associate generated INR186 crores gain, INR27 crores flows to PAT

That's why you have a separate line in the LODR which shows a gain of INR186 crores. But if I take out the amount which pertains to the other LPs, only INR27 crores of it flow into the PAT of Tata Capital.

items.statement: Management commits to crossing INR100 crores revenue in FY27 and expects similar growth trajectory to continue in FY28
items.quote: For now, we commit that we will surely cross INR100 crores. And let's see, if things move smoothly, then maybe more also.

items.statement: Management confident of maintaining similar growth pattern in FY28 as seen in previous years
items.quote: The graph will remain constant. It will not decline. It will remain constant. The volume will increase; the line will go straight up.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR77.42 crores with 80-90% expected to be executed by end of FY27
items.quote: Our order book stood at INR77.42 crores as of the latest reporting period.

items.statement: INR65-70 crores of current order book to be executed before end of FY27
items.quote: Out of these INR77 crores, we will be executing around INR65 crores to INR70 crores before end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Management expects good order book build-up by March 31st with many projects in pipeline and finalization stage
items.quote: By the time we are finishing this year, we will have a good order book build-up by 31st of March, for sure, because a lot of projects are in pipeline, a lot of projects are in finalization.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 23% driven by in-house manufacturing of components previously outsourced
items.quote: As you know in our object, we planned to purchase some equipment which will save a lot of money, time, and transportation for us, because we will be making -- we are making these components required for machine manufacturing in-house now.

items.statement: Management confirms 23% EBITDA margin is sustainable and expects similar or slightly better margins in H2 FY27
items.quote: Basically, you must have seen the figures from last half and this half, the EBITDA margins have definitely improved, and these are quite sustainable margins. And in H2 also, we will maintain these margins, maybe slightly better, but not less, for sure.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 estimated at INR15-16 crores split 60% plant & machinery and 40% factory building improvements
items.quote: Total capex just a moment. I have to see the figures. I think somewhere around INR15 crores, INR16 crores.

items.quote: So, and balance will be is related to the plant and machinery. So, what Mr. Longani has mentioned meaning we are doing some synergy in terms of having going for a good profit in future years.

items.statement: Nuclear sector opportunity expanding with 3-4 additional projects beyond executed INR10.62 crore order, some larger in value
items.quote: We are working on four, five projects additionally, which are not similar to this what we have executed. And some of them are even bigger than this.

items.statement: European partners shifting more work to India due to energy crisis and Chinese competition, creating tailwinds for order inflows
items.quote: Our European partners are now more inclined to giving more work in India and working with us. So, we are already working with two or three similar projects which normally were executed by our European partners.

items.statement: Developing two import-substitute products (one steel, one nuclear) launching in 3-3.5 months as game changers with better price-performance than European alternatives
items.quote: We are developing two more products currently, which will fulfill Indian market phase in Phase 1, and in Phase 2 outside India also. So, these products will soon launch in next another 3 months maybe, and they these products, once developed, they are also a game changer.

items.statement: Revenue mix expected to remain 50% steel and 50% non-steel (NDT and nuclear) for FY27
items.quote: Steel will more or less remain 50%.

items.statement: Infrastructure improvements underway including new shed, power and testing facility to support capacity expansion beyond current INR200 crore potential
items.quote: Currently, we have plans for improving our existing infrastructure. The new shed built from the power and testing facility point of view, and that is being taken care of now.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue grew 48.34% YoY to INR42.2 crores, EBITDA grew 47.62% to INR9.95 crores, PAT grew 45.91% to INR6.53 crores
items.quote: We have delivered strong year-on-year growth, with revenue from operations increasing by 48.34% to INR42.2 crores. EBITDA grew by 47.62% to INR9.95 crores, while profit after tax increased by 45.91% to INR6.53 crores.

items.statement: Nuclear and defense currently 4-5% of order book but expected to increase significantly given government target of 100 GW nuclear capacity by 2047
items.quote: Currently, in the current order book, nuclear and this defense is around-- in current order book, it is 4% to 5%. But it will but in near future, in few months, it will increase.

items.statement: Government focus on defense indigenization and nuclear capacity expansion (8.8 GW to 100 GW by 2047) creates long-term structural demand
items.quote: The nuclear power generation currently is at only 8.8 GW. By 2047, government is aiming to make it 100 GW. So, you can imagine the kind of potential we are looking at.

items.statement: Entry barriers in defense/nuclear due to lengthy government scrutiny, documentation and qualification processes across global markets
items.quote: Yes, the time taken is slightly longer than private industries because the government organizations, as you know, we have to go through a lot of scrutinies and then a lot of questions are there, a lot of documentary formalities are to be completed.

items.statement: NDT equipment supplied domestically and exported to government organizations in Brazil, Taiwan, Korea with similar long qualification timelines
items.quote: We have supplied quite a lot of equipment's in India as well as exported also. So, there are already very huge number of applications for NDT equipment's.

items.statement: Management emphasizes disciplined working capital management and timely project execution as business scales
items.quote: At the same time, we remain conscious of the importance of disciplined working capital management, timely project execution, and maintaining profitability as the business scales.

items.statement: European partners facing higher costs due to energy crisis (power, gas, petrol) making Indian manufacturing more competitive for import substitution
items.quote: Since European costs are very high, and Europe is facing their own challenges, and they have also increased their cost because of the power issue, and gas charges, and petrol, everything is expensive in Europe.

items.statement: Nuclear project timelines involve 2 quarters for materialization due to government scrutiny, agreements and commercial negotiations
items.quote: Yes, it takes about 2 quarters to materialize because being government organization, lot of scrutinies, agreements, everything is there. So, when we fulfill everything, then the things move into the commercial zone.

items.statement: Expect margin recovery from Q3 FY27 as pricing adjustments flow through
items.quote: We also expect margin to recover from Q3 FY27 onwards as pricing adjustments flow through.

items.statement: Target Mexico JV breakeven by Q3 FY27, provisional target Q4 FY27
items.quote: And quarter three, we are expecting like we are almost achieved the breakeven point. See, in our provisional, quarter four is our targeted to achieve this win-win situation, but not as we committed.

items.statement: New Gujarat plant completion targeted by October 2027
items.quote: The new Gujarat plant remains a key milestone, and its timely completion and utilization will be primary focus through 2027.

items.statement: Sustained demand for premium bags domestically and in export markets; new customer orders ahead of capacity expansion
items.quote: We saw sustained demand from our premium bags both domestically and in our export market. Importantly, we began fulfilling orders from new customers ahead of our next phase of capacity expansion.

items.statement: Dog food industry growing double digits in India; migrating customers from jute to PP woven to PLWPP to pinch bottom bags
items.quote: Dog food industry is now in India, it is increasing in double digit. So, dog food industries, we have a very good presence in all over world as well as the India. So that industry's growth, that is also our growth compared to our customers.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 16.35% down 285 bps YoY due to polymer and freight cost pressure; expect recovery from Q3 FY27
items.quote: The EBITDA margin was 16.35% against 19.25% a year ago, a decline of 285 basis points. This reflected industry-wise cost pressure. Polymer price rose with the crude oil and freight cost increased because of disruption in the Red Asia.

items.statement: Gross margin impact limited to 7% despite 26% raw material price increase in Q2; 45-50% customers on conversion cost model
items.quote: But in our gross margin, there is an impact of the 7%. Rest we have already, passed on to the customer and continuous we have already discussions So that pass on reflect in the quarter 3 majorly

items.statement: EBITDA per kg fell from INR54 in Q1 to INR45 in Q2; target to return to INR54 level in next 2 quarters
items.quote: It is a per kg is a INR55 and this month, this quarter is like a INR46, INR47 approximate. I am telling you. Ajay Kumar Dubey: You, INR54 last. Alpesh Tulsibhai Patel: INR54 and this is INR45

items.statement: Announced 3-year contract renewal worth INR150 crores per year from major international pet food customer on 2 Oct 2026
items.quote: On 2nd October 2026, we announced a new order and 3-year contract renewal worth about INR150 crores per year from an international customer, one of the largest private corporations in the world from the pet food and animal nutrition packaging, including in the United States.

items.statement: Installed capacity 42,000 metric tons annually, running at 39,000-40,000; post-expansion target 69,000-72,000 metric tons
items.quote: See, sir, very honestly, that is right now we are installed capacity is 42,000 metric tons annually. Out of that, we are almost actually like 39,000-40,000 capacity. After this expansion, our capacity reach into the 70,000, 69,000 to 72,000 in between.

items.statement: Served 2,040+ customers with 13,974 SKUs as of 30 Sep 2026; up from 2,000 customers and 13,500 SKUs at end Q1 FY27

items.statement: Revised full-year FY27 revenue growth guidance to 25%+ from earlier 20%+
items.quote: Also, on the top line, we are revising our guidance from earlier 20% plus to 25% plus for the full year.

items.statement: Maintained full-year FY27 EBITDA margin target at double-digit
items.quote: We continue to maintain our full year margin trajectory to the double-digit number.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 maintained at INR 200-250 crore
items.quote: Our capex guidance for FY 27 remains at INR 200-250 crore.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 8.2% vs 9% in H1 FY26 due to material cost impact
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 110 crore, up 21% y-o-y with a margin of 8.2% compared with 9% in Q2 FY 26.

items.statement: Expect H2 FY27 EBITDA margin of 10.5-11% to achieve full-year double-digit target
items.quote: for H2 specifically, we would be expecting a margin of, let's say, anywhere between 10.5-11% for H2.

items.statement: Order book at INR 2,580 crore with 80% LED and 11% EV programs
items.quote: Our order book is at INR 2,580 crore, and LED lighting accounts for approximately 80% of the order book, while EV (Electric Vehicle) program accounts for approximately 11%.

items.statement: 60% of order book (INR ~1,500 crore) to be delivered in FY28
items.quote: almost 60% of the order book gets delivered in FY 28, which is almost close to INR 1,500 crore revenue.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 33% y-o-y to INR 1,342 crore, outpacing industry
items.quote: The Q2 FY 27 revenue stood at INR 1,342 crore, up 33% y-o-y and 10% quarter-on-quarter (q-o-q), outpacing broader industry trends.

items.statement: LED lighting share reached 63% of H1 FY27 revenue, up 200 bps y-o-y
items.quote: LED (Light Emitting Diode) lighting, which has reached 63% of revenue in H1 FY 27, up 200 bps (basis points) y-o-y.

items.statement: Gaining wallet share with Maruti Suzuki (25-30% to 35-40%), HMSI tail lamps (<20% to ~50%), Toyota (new headlamp business 15-20%), Suzuki 2W (15-20% to 30%+), VW/Skoda tail lamps (30% to ~70%) over 2-3 years
items.quote: Currently, the wallet share at Maruti Suzuki on a headlamp, tail lamp put together is anywhere between 25-30%, and this wallet share will be increasing to anywhere between 35-40% over the next 2 to 3 years. Also, Honda Motorcycle and Scooter India, we've got a significant order win, specifically on the tail lamps, where the current wallet share was less than 20%, and we are expected to increase ou

items.statement: No wallet share decline at any OEM; Hero MotoCorp share drop due to product mix
items.quote: most of the OEMs, which I mentioned, we have either gained wallet share or we have maintained the present wallet share. There has not been any OEM where there has been a wallet share decline. Number three, specific to Hero, it is just a resultant of the product mix, whereas some of the models where we are not present, perhaps were the volume growth drivers vis-a-vis some of the models where we are

items.statement: INR 80 crore capex spent in H1 FY27; remaining INR 120-170 crore in H2
items.quote: Out of that, in H1, we have already done around INR 80 crore of capex, and the remaining will happen for the project which we are progressing in the H2.

items.statement: Net long-term debt reduced to INR 188 crore (Sep 2026) from INR 291 crore (Mar 2025); net debt/EBITDA improved to 2.2x from 3.0x
items.quote: Our net long-term debt as on 30th September 2026 stood at INR 188 crore compared with INR 291 crore as on 31st March 2025, and our net debt to EBITDA has improved to 2.2 as on 30th September 2026 versus 3.0 as on 31st March 2025.

items.statement: Crude-linked polymer prices, freight, rupee depreciation pressuring industry margins
items.quote: crude-linked polymer prices, freight, rupee depreciation remains a key monitorable, putting the industry margins under pressure.

items.statement: Company LED penetration at 63-65% (PV 55-60%, 2W/3W 75-80%); industry at 50-55%
items.quote: our estimate is that as we are close to 63-65% of LED penetration collectively, and out of that, our PV is close to 55-60% and 2-Wheeler, 3-Wheeler is in the range of 75-80%. And the market is also close to 50-55%.

items.statement: EV contribution currently 10-12% of revenue; product is powertrain agnostic
items.quote: Currently, the contribution of EV in our business is close to 10-12%. And as we mentioned, since our product is like technology and powertrain agnostic, so per se, it does not has any significant impact on our business.

items.statement: No significant disruption expected from new entrants; top 5 lighting players to control market for next 5 years
items.quote: we do not anticipate or foresee any significant changes with respect to some of the new entrants. These could be strategic players only in 1 or 2 customers or 1 or 2 models, also maybe for smaller lamps. However, the large part of the market would still be controlled by the top 5 automotive lighting companies in India, and I don't see any significant change over the next 5 years in the top 5 playe

items.statement: Czech advanced engineering centre expanding rapidly; servicing Tata Motors and M&M needs
items.quote: we also have our own advanced lighting engineering centre in the Czech Republic, and that is expanding very rapidly. A lot of the needs of the OEMs in India, specifically the likes of Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra, are being serviced from the Czech Advanced Lighting Centre.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments and energy prices could further pressure input costs and margins
items.quote: in the near term, we remain watchful of the geopolitical developments and energy prices, which could further put pressure on input costs and weigh on margins.

items.statement: Margin guidance assumes no significant further volatility from West Asia crisis
items.quote: there is a caveat that I'm hoping that there is no significant further volatility based on the ongoing West Asia crisis. If these were to continue, then I would probably have to relook at the guidance.

items.statement: Export revenue minuscule vs domestic; engagements with IPOs may yield revenue in 2-3 years
items.quote: probably in the next 2 to 3 years, we can see some export revenue to come in. But again, it will be a minuscule number compared to the domestic.

items.statement: Current capex projects for SOP by end FY27 or early FY28; 60% of order book for SOP in FY28
items.quote: the project which we are executing now and will go for SOP somewhere by end of this fiscal year or maybe early next fiscal year. So accordingly, the business will come up. And also, as we mentioned, next financial year, we see around 60% of our order book will go for SOP.

items.statement: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue ₹275 cr vs ₹210 cr, up 31%; EBITDA ₹36 cr vs ₹13 cr; PAT ₹24 cr vs ₹17 cr
items.quote: So, as far as consol revenue is concerned for September quarter, it stands at ₹275 crores versus ₹210 crores registering top line growth of 31 %. EBITDA up from ₹13 to ₹36 crores and PAT up from ₹17 to ₹24 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated H1 FY27 revenue ₹653 cr up 17%; EBITDA ₹83 cr vs ₹51 cr; PAT ₹64 cr vs ₹59 cr
items.quote: As far as first 6 months are concerned, on a consol basis, revenue stands at ₹653 crores up by 17%, EBITDA at ₹83 crores versus ₹51 crores and PAT at ₹64 crores versus ₹59 crores.

items.statement: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue ₹170 cr vs ₹155 cr; EBITDA ₹30 cr vs ₹27 cr; PAT ₹29 cr
items.quote: On a standalone basis, the revenue stands at ₹170 crores vis-à-vis ₹155 crores, EBITDA at ₹ 30 crores versus ₹27 crores and PAT at ₹29 crores.

items.statement: Standalone H1 FY27 revenue ₹411 cr vs ₹384 cr; PAT ₹57 cr vs ₹65 cr but business PAT higher
items.quote: And on a standalone basis, revenue stands at ₹411 crores versus ₹384 crores, while PAT at ₹57 crores versus ₹65 crores, but here if you look at PAT bridge, business PAT during 6 months is higher than previous year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 13% vs 6.4% despite gross margin down ~4% due to operating leverage and cost discipline
items.quote: EBITDA margin expansion as conveyed earlier, despite on a consol basis due to input cost pressure gross margin is lower by about 4%, but EBITDA margin percentage stands at 13% vis-a-vis 6.4%, one on account of operating leverage and secondly, on account of cost discipline and product mix.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin down ~2.3% but EBITDA margin almost maintained
items.quote: on a standalone basis, even though gross margin percentage is down by about 2.3%, the EBITDA margin has been almost maintained.

items.statement: Standalone H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 14.4%, up 18% YoY; expect next two quarters somewhat better
items.quote: in the first half, on a standalone basis, our EBITDA level has actually improved by 18% and EBITDA margin is at 14.4%. In the next two quarters, in fact, it should be somewhat better than this.

items.statement: BISP (Beyond India Summer Products) 51% of consolidated revenue at ₹625 cr TTM; EBITDA high-single digit, accretive
items.quote: As far as Item #3 , Beyond India Summer Products (BISP) on a consolidated basis, it contributed ₹625 crores of top line. As conveyed earlier and on a consol basis, BISP constitutes of all products and geography sales, which is not dependent on India Summer. So, basically, this is the de-risking from India Summer and that now constitutes 51% of top line on a consol basis

items.statement: Standalone BISP ₹192 cr TTM (24% of revenue), EBITDA ~10%, each category EBITDA positive
items.quote: On a standalone basis, BISP products have contributed in all ₹192 crores of top line in trailing 12 months, that is 24 % and BISP as a whole, EBITDA is around 10 % and each component of the BISP category even on a standalone basis is also EBITDA positive and accretive with minimum capital employment.

items.statement: D2C channel EBITDA and PAT positive from year 2, higher margins than traditional channel
items.quote: another channel of sales which is D2C which was nurtured over a period of last 4 to 5 years is not only generating decent contribution and gross margin but it is EBITDA positive in line with our traditional channel, in fact more than that and obviously also at a PAT level it is in line with that.

items.statement: New products (RAC, BLDC fans, air purifiers) zero capex for ACs and fans; purifier may need small capex later
items.quote: Just like our existing business , here also , we will continue following absolutely asset -light operating models. There will be outsourced business model , and as far as air conditioners and BLDC ceiling fans are concerned, there will be zero CAPEX. In air purifier, down the line, there may be a small amount of CAPEX.

items.statement: New products to follow low working capital model like coolers; buy-and-sell approach, no large inventory build-up
items.quote: This would be also a fairly low working capital model, the way we are going to approach it. So, just like in coolers where our capital employed is fairly low, these products will also fall within that same sort of philosophy. So, these should have a good return on capital employed.

items.statement: Channel inventory normalized end of Q1; fresh inventory built for summer 2027, no residual from prior years
items.quote: At the end of the previous quarter, the company inventory was also minimal, and the channel inventory was also minimal. As we speak, the company has been producing in the last quarter, and in the current quarter so far, and has been producing what is needed to prime the channel. The company's inventory hasn't built up, but the channel inventory, to some extent, has been built up, which is part of

items.statement: RAC pricing mid-premium segment, not entry-level; specs higher, priced accordingly, similar to Voltas/Samsung for like-to-like features
items.quote: Pricing for residential ACs will be in the mid-premium sort of segment. Obviously, we will not compete with the likes of Daikin or Mitsubishi or Hitachi or one of those.

items.statement: Air cooler margins ~45.9% standalone Q2, down 2.3% YoY; expect similar going forward
items.quote: as far as air coolers are concerned, the margins would be more or less what you saw so far, which are, at the moment, on a standalone basis, we ended the quarter at 45.9%, which was 2.3% less than at the same time in the previous year.

items.statement: Demand depends on temperature; clean channel inventory means even normal summer should yield good sales
items.quote: Demand to a great degree at the consumer level will depend on temperature. If the temperatures are high enough, then product will sell even if it is more expensive. If the temperature is not high enough, products will not sell even if you discount them. Th at is the nature of seasonal categories. As we sit today, because the channel is completely clean from the previous year, even modest demand sh

items.statement: Second interim dividend ₹2/share (face value ₹2), payout ~₹13 cr; total ₹3/share (~₹21 cr) so far in FY27
items.quote: Today, Board of Directors have declared second interim dividend of ₹2 per share on a face value of ₹2. In all, the payout will be about ₹13 crores. This is in addition to interim dividend of ₹1 announced post-June quarter, in all ₹3 and close to ₹21 crores of payout so far.

items.statement: Dividend policy etched in stone unless revised; no moderation expected
items.quote: It's a policy which has been adopted by the Board, informed to the shareholders. So, it's a policy. It's sort of etched in stone, unless we revise the policy, which we don't need to.

items.statement: IMPCO Mexico Q2 revenue ₹40 cr vs ₹17 cr; GSK China ₹23 cr; Australia+USA ₹46 cr vs ₹35 cr
items.quote: As far as IMPCO Mexico is concerned, the top line is ₹ 40 crores versus ₹ 17 crores. However, the summer was delayed, so in June quarter, there was a decline in sales, but in this quarter, there has been a decent increase and part of the loss of sales has been made up in the current quarter. As far as GSK China is concerned, it is ₹ 23 crores of sales. As far as Brazil and USA are concerned, of co

items.statement: New products outsourced; BLDC fan partner finalized, rollout soon; RAC sourced from China for exports
items.quote: Yes. We will be rolling out our products fairly soon.

items.statement: International ACs, heaters, fans sourced from China; air coolers mostly from India; commercial/industrial coolers from China
items.quote: Bulk of it is manufactured in India. All the evaporative air coolers that we are selling internationally, bulk of it is going from India. But then there are large-size coolers, commercial coolers, industrial coolers that are also going from China. It is a mix.

items.statement: No cannibalization of coolers by RAC; new products strengthen channel, help cooler sales at trade level
items.quote: No, not really. Because on the contrary, we believe that with all these product categories, we will also have channel expansion. We should be becoming more stronger in some of the outlets.

items.statement: International growth uncertain due to Middle East shipping issues, freight costs, tariff uncertainties
items.quote: International business will grow, but there are uncertainties. For example, current Middle East situation was a big deterrent in growth this year, wherein we had customers who wanted to buy coolers and there are cases where we have got the money in advance, but we are unable to ship. The freight costs have shot up. On the other end, these are these tariff related things.

items.statement: Existing team has AC experience from prior roles; no new hires for AC launch; incentive structure market-aligned
items.quote: We already have people with the company on the manufacturing side, on the operations side, on the sales side, who have prior experience with air conditioners, rich experience with air conditioners. We did not recruit them for air conditioners, but they were already on board for air coolers for the last few years.

items.statement: Consolidated ROCE (PBIT/core capital) 143% vs 57% YoY on TTM Sep; standalone negative capital employed, infinite ROCE, RoNW 21%
items.quote: on a consol basis stands at ₹104 crores versus ₹322 crores translating into ROCE percentage i.e. PBIT by capital employed (core capital) 143% versus 57% and return on net worth at 20%. While on a standalone basis, it is a negative capital employed during first 6 months and hence in a way academically it is an infinite ROCE and return on net worth of 21%

items.statement: Treasury ₹468 cr after repaying most Australia loans and borrowings
items.quote: Treasury now stands at ₹468 crores after repaying most of the loans and borrowings availed in Australia.

items.statement: No specific revenue targets for new categories; baby steps, EBITDA-accretive, no delusions of grandeur
items.quote: We are taking baby steps in these segments. As explained, we really have no delusions of grandeur. We do not think that we will really be amongst the top players in the country. We are going to grow these categories cautiously so that they remain EBITDA accretive. At this moment, we really do not have a specific number that we can share.

items.statement: No ad spend or launch OPEX in current quarter; measured brand investment may come summer
items.quote: We do not envisage any ad spend or launch expenses in the current quarter. Maybe come summer, we may spend something on these products. Like I said, it will be a very measured investment in brand building, not so much that it does not remain EBITDA accretive.

items.statement: Bharuch plant overall utilization expected 70-75% by year-end FY27
items.quote: I would say overall, would be between 70% to 75%.

items.statement: Bharuch SRB lines at 70% utilization, CRB lines below 60%, overall plant ~60% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: SRB lines, we have already reached 70% for the quarter, what we promised in the last quarter. CRB lines are still below 60%, I would say. So on an average, it is at 60%.

items.statement: Rail expansion at Jamshedpur and plain bearing at Bharuch on target, trial runs Nov-Dec, PPAPs to follow
items.quote: The new line would start getting into the trial runs in November and December only, then the PPAPs would start and then we'll qualify those lines.

items.statement: Rail tender delayed, committee to be set in 2-3 weeks, interim orders placed on wagon builders
items.quote: Tender was delayed and the tender hopefully should get into in terms of -- because committee has not been set yet, committee will be set and all that stuff will happen in the next 2, 3 weeks.

items.statement: Cost inflation must be passed on, industry cannot absorb; 50% of 130 bps gross margin impact from unfavorable mix, 50% from input cost timing gap
items.quote: So probably I would say 50% is because of unfavorable mix and 50% is because of input cost difference between price and cost timing difference.

items.statement: Unfavorable mix in Q2 due to low rail share (16% vs higher historical), rail tender delayed
items.quote: Rail was low in the quarter. That is the unfavorable mix because the global -- the rail tender was delayed.

items.statement: Bharuch plant revenue INR 75 cr in Q2 FY27, heavily export/intercompany, SRB lines gaining traction
items.quote: From a revenue perspective for this quarter was very close to INR75 crores.

items.statement: Amalgamation of Timken GGB Technology Private Limited with Timken India Limited progressing smoothly
items.quote: The amalgamation of Timken GGB Technology Private Limited with Timken India Limited is progressing smoothly.

items.statement: GGB FRC and metal polymer investments at Bharuch ~INR 70 cr total, asset turn 1.5-2x expected
items.quote: This Bharuch investments for GGB, what's going on for both FRC and metal polymer put together, I think INR35 crores, INR35 crores, INR70 crores of investments.

items.statement: Wind gearbox bearings currently imported from GGB, local production at Bharuch to start soon, plain bearing tech (Gen 3/4) opportunity
items.quote: We are already winning orders and supplying from our overseas by brand. We are buying from them, our GGB brand. But very soon, it will be produced here.

items.statement: Competitor being selective in wind due to low-margin main shaft business; Timken focused on gearbox carrier tapers
items.quote: Whoever has made the comment has made a valid comment. So we are also into the gearboxes and not on the main shaft generally.

items.statement: Carbides up 200%, steel, gas, fuel, labor costs rising; CI improvements insufficient to offset
items.quote: Carbides have gone 200% up. Steel is going up and then your gases have already gone up. Then if you look at the labor, labor is going up.

items.statement: Major customers understand cost pass-through; automotive delays slightly, industrial accepting
items.quote: Our major customers understand it. They are passing on. But automotive, they will kind of delay it a little bit here and there. Industry people, otherwise, on the industrial side is coming up.

items.statement: Geopolitics, trade uncertainties, supply chain realignments, global demand unpredictability
items.quote: Global industry activity continues to be influenced by geopolitics. So that is a challenge, as we all know, trade-related uncertainties are very much there and supply chain alignments are happening with every passing week.

items.statement: Targets 60% gross profit and 30% EBIT margin in core coding and marking business
items.quote: So we target about 60% gross profit and about 30% EBIT.

items.statement: Standalone COGS improved to 41.65% of operating revenue in Q2 FY27 from 42.32% in previous quarter
items.quote: On a standalone basis, the cost of goods sold is about 41.65% of the operating revenue for the quarter 2. On comparison to the previous quarter, this was 42.32% of the operating revenue.

items.statement: Standalone employee costs at 17% of operating revenue in Q2 FY27 vs 18% in prior year quarter
items.quote: Employee costs are 17% of the operating revenue Q2 of FY26-'27. Comparative period in previous year, it was approximately 18% and for the entire FY25-'26, it was 19%.

items.statement: Consolidated COGS increased to 44% of operating revenue in Q2 FY27 from 40% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: The cost of goods sold is 44% of the operating revenue. Compared to the Q2 of FY25-'26, it was about 40%.

items.statement: Coding and marking segment sees steady growth with new customers added and development in new printer, ink, cartridge technologies
items.quote: The business outlook for the coding and marking segment for the next half is exciting. With new customer base getting added to our portfolio, we are also in the midst of development in new technologies in printers, inks and

items.statement: Co-packing business in packaging division progressing with regular orders
items.quote: The co-packing business is going well. That's not a problem. I think that's definitely progressing and we've got like regular orders for that.

items.statement: Invested over INR 100 crores in Track & Trace business over last six years
items.quote: Even in the Track & Trace business, we've invested more than a INR 100 crores already so far over the last six years.

items.statement: V-Shapes next-generation machine blueprint targeted for completion by January or February
items.quote: Our target is to finish that in January or February. So we have a blueprint for the next sets of machines that we will make.

items.statement: Track & Trace pilots with top 5-10 Indian pharma companies concluding; field performance feedback expected soon
items.quote: And we've been doing some pilots for about a year and something, like I said with two -- top 10 or top 5 Indian customers. Now we are coming to the end game of those pilots, and we are going to get a feedback of how exactly the field performance is.

items.statement: Coding and marking domestic market is oligopoly; Control Print plus three others dominate ~80% market share
items.quote: And we in the domestic market of coding and marking, we are an Oligopoly. So we along with the other three players, we dominate about 80% of the domestic coding and marking.

items.statement: International subsidiary losses trending down: Q4 FY26 INR 12 cr, Q1 FY27 INR 8 cr, Q2 FY27 INR 5 cr; structural improvement but quarterly lumpiness expected
items.quote: So fundamentally, we believe that the trend is in the correct direction. But of course, quarter to quarter, there'll be variations. Sometimes especially in smaller businesses, when we book a couple of big sales or certain other things, it bumps it up and takes it down. But yeah, the overall trend is to constantly reduce those, I mean, or improve the business, improve the sales and improve the busi

items.quote: Markprint is a company which gives profit year on year. So that's probably the least of the worries for us. Middle East operations, which is CP, MEA operations, that is just recently started January 2025. And it's obviously going to pick up and we will definitely have a break even this year.

items.quote: We have already implemented certain price increase. With reduction in input costs and overheads, we feel that our profitability will definitely improve.

items.statement: Three European technology acquisitions: Markprint, Codeology, V-Shapes (patents for single-snap mono-dose packaging machine)
items.quote: all like technology acquisitions. V-Shapes was a certain set of patents. We are buying around a packaging concept, a packaging machine concept for a single snap mono dose. items.statement: Announced solar plant, filter presses, debottlenecking, and JV specialty compounds projects totaling INR 458 crores
items.quote: We are establishing a 40 MW (peak) solar energy plant in Kota for INR 145 crores and installing filter presses in our Cement plant at Kota for INR 60 crores

items.statement: Debottlenecking at Bharuch and Kota to improve energy efficiency and increase Caustic capacity at INR 120 crores
items.quote: we are debottlenecking operations at Bharuch and Kota to improve energy efficiency of our current operations and increase Caustic capacity at a project cost of INR 120 crores

items.statement: Setting up specialty PVC compounds, medical grades, and HFFR polymer compounds in JV Shriram Teknor at INR 133 crores total, with INR 50 crores equity
items.quote: we are setting up new lines for manufacture of speciality compounds of PVC, speciality medical grades and diversification into the manufacture of Halogen-Free Flame Retardant (HFFR) grades of polymer compounds in our JV Shriram Teknor Limited at a total cost of INR 133 crores. Our investment will be up-to Rs. 50 crores as Equity into the JV.

items.quote: During the quarter, we commissioned the 100 TPD Aluminium Chloride plant at Bharuch, taking the total capacity to 250 TPD along with partial commissioning of Calcium Chloride Plant taking us to 50% of the planned capacity, that is, 133 TPD out of 266 TPD.

items.statement: Commissioned 68 MW hybrid renewable power project at Kota; 58 MW hybrid renewable project at Bharuch progressing as per schedule
items.quote: We also commissioned the 68 MW hybrid renewable power project at Kota, further strengthening our structural cost competitiveness. The 58 MW hybrid renewable power project under group captive SPV at Bharuch, is progressing as per schedule.

items.statement: Caustic capacity utilisation at 89% in Q2 FY27, up from 79-80% same period last year
items.quote: Capacity utilisation during the quarter stood at 89%.

items.statement: Fenesta Aluminium Extrusion Plant phase one commissioned at Kota, phase two in installation; wooden doors facility on schedule
items.quote: During the quarter, phase one of Aluminium Extrusion Plant at Kota was commissioned, while the second phase is in the process of installation and commissioning. Work on the wooden doors facility is moving as per schedule.

items.statement: Chemicals PBDIT fell to INR 158 crores from INR 254 crores YoY due to higher input costs and absence of INR 76 crore Gujarat incentive
items.quote: The PBDIT for this quarter stood at Rs 158 crores against Rs 254 crores last year, as higher input costs more than offset the benefit of better realizations and volumes. Further, last year there was onetime positive impact of Rs. 76 crores towards incentive from the Government of Gujarat.

items.statement: Vinyl PBDIT rose to INR 51 crores from INR 12 crores YoY on higher PVC and Carbide volumes and realizations
items.quote: PBDIT was higher at Rs 51 crores as compared to Rs 12 crores last year, led by better volumes and realizations, partially offset by higher input costs.

items.statement: Sugar & Ethanol PBDIT increased to INR 62 crores from INR 33 crores YoY; prior year had INR 15.5 crore power tariff revision benefit
items.quote: PBDIT for the segment came in at Rs 62 crores as against Rs 33 crores last year. In Q2 FY26, there was a significant positive impact of Rs 15.5 crores on account of the upward revision of power tariff by UPPCL as mentioned earlier.

items.statement: Fenesta PBDIT up 15% to INR 49 crores, margins slightly lower due to product mix change, elevated input costs, and higher fixed expenses for new platforms
items.quote: PBDIT for the quarter was up 15% at Rs 49 crores, although margins were slightly lower. This was due to the change in product mix, elevated input costs and higher fixed expenses for setting up new revenue platforms for the future.

items.statement: Shriram Farm Solutions PBDIT declined to INR 78 crores from INR 106 crores YoY on lower Seed and Specialty Plant Nutrition volumes
items.quote: PBDIT for the quarter was lower at Rs 78 crores as against Rs 106 crores last year.

items.statement: Fertilizer PBDIT increased 25% to INR 25 crores driven by better margins from higher gas rates and improved energy efficiency
items.quote: PBDIT increased by 25% to Rs 25 crores, driven by better margins on account of higher gas rates and improved energy efficiency.

items.statement: Bioseed PBDIT negative INR 41 crores vs negative INR 7 crores YoY due to lower volumes, higher fixed cost burden, doubtful debt provisions in India, and seed discard in Philippines
items.quote: PBDIT for the quarter stood at negative Rs 41 crores, against negative Rs 7 crores last year. The decline reflects lower volumes, which increased the burden of fixed expenses, along with higher provisions for doubtful debts in India and seed discards in Philippines.

items.statement: Chemicals cost of production up 6-8% across chemistries, selling prices down 4-6%; only Hydrogen Peroxide margins improved due to in-house hydrogen and delinked gas prices
items.quote: the cost of production in this quarter has gone up in the range of about 6% to 8% across, the chemistries, and selling price has come off in the range of around 4% to 6%.

items.statement: Coal prices up significantly, impacting caustic business; glycerin prices volatile for epichlorohydrine downstream due to West Asia crisis and freight disruptions
items.quote: coal prices have gone up significantly and they are still going up. So probably we will keep seeing the impact of higher costs. But that cost is primarily impacting our caustic business because that is where the energy intensity is high.

items.statement: Current PVC prices in range of INR 95,000 to INR 1 lakh per tonne; demand expected to pick up post-monsoon in Q3 and Q4
items.quote: the current prices of the PVC are in the range of INR95,000 to INR1 lakh a tonne. So those are kind of prices currently prevailing PVC.

items.statement: Chemicals demand supported by domestic consumption in textiles, alumina, infrastructure; future capacity additions may create near-term supply-demand imbalances
items.quote: In India, underlying demand remained supported by domestic consumption across textiles, alumina and infrastructure. Capacity additions over last few years have been well absorbed by the markets, however future capacity additions may create near-term supply-demand imbalances and put pressure on prices and margins.

items.statement: Shriram Farm Solutions topline declined 10% YoY due to timing difference in Research wheat seed sales; portion may reverse in Q3 subject to crop conditions
items.quote: The SFS business witnessed a decline in the topline in Q2 FY 27 compared with Q2 FY 26, largely on account of the difference in timing of sales of Research wheat seed. A portion of the timing-related impact may reverse in Q3, subject to crop conditions and channel demand.

items.statement: Bioseed Kharif season challenging due to El Niño; Corn, Cotton, Paddy acreage below last year in south and central India; Cotton volumes better than last year
items.quote: The Kharif season remained very challenging for the Bioseed business due to a broader climatic pressure especially in south and central India. Despite a late recovery in rainfall, acreage under key crops such as Corn, Cotton and Paddy stayed below last year's levels.

items.statement: Fenesta order book healthy; project business at 45% causes volatility but no challenge seen
items.quote: it is still a very healthy order book, we do not see any challenge.

items.statement: Minimum Import Price of USD 766 per MT for PVC helping domestic realizations; weaker rupee further supporting prices
