items.quote: In absolute terms, our net debt as on 30th September 2026 was INR814.51 crores. Our working capital cycle has also come down to less than 100 days during this quarter from the 124 days, which we achieved in the same period in the previous year.

items.statement: State incentives received INR1.62 crores in H1 FY27 vs INR9 crores in H1 FY26, expect INR12-15 crores more in H2
items.quote: The amount should be in the range of about INR12 crores to INR15 crores.

items.statement: Privi Fine Sciences merger pending regulatory approvals, expected completion by FY27 end, 6,000 MTPA capacity ready for INR300-350 crores revenue potential
items.quote: That's correct. So Krish, to answer you specifically, yes, the capacities are already put in place. That's what Sanjeev is trying to say. So, we have about 6,000 ton s of capacity, which is there, which can possibly give us a potential revenue of about INR300 crores, INR350 crores, which we've been talking about basis the prices that is there

items.statement: ROCE 24.30% (+216 bps YoY), ROE 26.34% (+134 bps YoY), asset turnover 1.7x on fixed asset base
items.quote: As on 30th September 2026, our ROCE stood at 24.30%, an improvement of 216 basis points year-on-year, while ROE increased by 134 basis points, and we have achieved a figure of 26.34%.

items.statement: PRIGIV JV profitable in Q2 FY27: INR28 crores revenue, ~INR2 crores PBT; FY28 guidance INR225 crores revenue
items.quote: In the JV, we are looking at 2 phases of expansion. One is already underway. And based on that, we see a revenue of around INR225 crores and somewhere there, okay?

items.statement: First ever interim dividend declared: INR5 per share (face value INR10) for FY27
items.quote: Reflecting our confidence in the business and our commitment to creating value for shareholders, the Board has declared the company's first ever interim dividend of INR5 per share of face value INR10 for the financial year '26 -'27.

items.statement: Phase 2 includes maltol, ethyl maltol, cyclopentanone, furfural-based derivatives; Phase 3 adds INR450-500 crores revenue potential
items.quote: That's correct. That's furfural -based derivatives, maltol, ethyl maltol, cyclopentanone, and a couple of specialty molecules as well.

items.statement: Strong customer relationships driving reliable supply partnerships, customers helping with early payments
items.quote: Privi stands for quality on delivery time, and expectations of the customers have been so good with us that they have been helping us in ensuring that the money is paid to us on time and in some cases, maybe a few days before time

items.statement: Regulatory approvals delaying Privi Fine Sciences capacity expansion and merger completion
items.quote: We had given that guidance. So, it is waiting for some regulatory approvals. Otherwise, in terms of products, we are good, okay? But in terms of some regulatory approvals, we faced some delays, which are now nearing completion.

items.statement: Cash generated from operations INR445 crores in H1 FY27, significant improvement YoY
items.quote: Our cash generated from operations for the first 6 months was INR445 crores, showing remarkable improvement over previous year, mainly on account of higher profits earned during this year.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of INR750 crores with healthy orders in hand and delivery scheduled for H2
items.quote: As for the current year, we remain on track with our revenue target of FY27 of INR750 crores with a healthy orders in hand and delivery scheduled for the second half of the year.

items.statement: Targeting INR1,000 crores sales for FY27-28 and INR1,250-1,500 crores for FY29
items.quote: Yes. So like I said, for FY27, '28, our sales target will be INR1,000 crores. And the export mix, I cannot say anything right now because that depends on the situation, but our focus is on export as well as domestic.

items.statement: Targeting EBITDA of INR225-250 crores for FY27-28 with higher absolute profit despite potentially lower margin percentage
items.quote: But coming year, we are targeting more than INR200 crores of EBITDA. It can be INR225 crores, INR250 crores. So percentage may be lower, but the value terms, it will be higher, and that's what we are targeting.

items.statement: Phase 3 expansion adding 6,500 MVA capacity progressing as per plan with commissioning expected April 2027
items.quote: On the project front, expansion Phase 3, which will add 6,500 MVA of capacity is progressing as per plan, with commissioning expected in April '27.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 80-90%, expected to reach 100% in Q3 and Q4 FY27
items.quote: I can tell you very confidently that right now, last quarter, we have utilized almost 80% of our installed capacity. And going forward in Q3, Q4, I think it will be almost 100%.

items.statement: Total capacity will reach 14,000 MVA after Phase 3 commissioning, driving growth from FY28 onwards
items.quote: This will take our total capacity to 14,000 MVA and drive the next leg of growth from FY28 onwards.

items.statement: Order book of more than INR550 crores as on date with 60-40 domestic-export mix
items.quote: So we have an order book of more than INR550 crores going forward. So like I said earlier in my opening remarks that we are on track to achieve more than INR750 crores of sales, which was projected in the beginning of the year. And the export domestic will be in ratio of around 60% to 40%, 60% domestic, 40% export, which is likely to improve in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Orders in hand executable over next 6 months, with new orders also coming for Q1 FY28
items.quote: Yes, yes. Very much. Like I said, we have orders in hand of almost INR550 crores, and we are getting new orders also. And this first half, I think we have done about INR330 crores in sales. So even if we do additional say, INR500 crores, we'll reach to almost more than INR800 crores. I mean we have started getting orders for even the Q1 of next year.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 20.8% from 16.4% in Q1, expected to improve further in Q3 and Q4 with higher export share
items.quote: On profitability, our EBITDA margin improved to 20.8% in Q2 from 16.4% in Q1. We expect conditions for export to improve further in the near future. This should translate d irectly into higher export share in our revenue mix and in turn, a further improvement in margin over the coming quarters

items.statement: Export EBITDA margins significantly higher than domestic margins, with export margins maintained at previous year levels
items.quote: No. I think export margins are pretty much same what we did in previous years.

items.statement: Raw material prices have stabilized at current levels, new orders priced at prevailing market rates with pass-through to customers
items.quote: The RM prices have stabilized. Again, it is not as what it used to be. And I don't think that it will completely stabilize till all the Middle East crisis and other things gets concluded. But all the orders what we are getting now is as per the market price, as per the current raw material price.

items.statement: Sales prices have increased to partially offset higher raw material costs, but raw material prices unlikely to decrease
items.quote: Frankly speaking, I don't think that the raw material price will come down. But you never know. I mean nobody can give that very accurately. But like I said earlier, that with these higher raw material costs, our sales price has also gone up now.

items.statement: Power consumption expected to double in 3-4 years driven by AI/data centers, renewables, and transmission expansion, creating sustained demand for transformers
items.quote: And if you see certain government data, our power consumption will be doubled in next 3 to 4 years. The AI investment and the data center will require a lot of power. The renewable also, government is targeting more and more gigawatts every year. So this all will create a demand for not only transformer, but all the power equipment.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 export-domestic mix at 40-60, with US contributing 40-60% of export sales, Europe minimal but efforts underway
items.quote: And the export domestic will be in ratio of around 60% to 40%, 60% domestic, 40% export, which is likely to improve in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: US demand strong across data centers, distribution, and substations after 50% tariff withdrawal in February, lead times 1-1.5 years for higher kV class
items.quote: Yes. So I mean, demand from U.S.A. is quite good right now. In between our supply to U.S.A. went down mainly because of the 50 % tariff imposed on Indian product, but that has been withdrawn in February. So after that, we have started getting orders steadily, and that orders have now increased.

items.statement: Higher receivables and financial assets due to LC structure where customers bear interest for 180-day LCs, company earns interest on working capital
items.quote: So higher asset is basically because of the investment what we are doing for the new project. And like I said, once again, the receivable is not actually a receivable. So just to give you an example, we provide a 60 days credit through LC to one of our customers, but we established LC for 180 days with interest borne by them.

items.statement: No margin pressure expected for at least 2-3 years despite industry-wide capacity additions due to strong demand growth
items.quote: Not for at least another couple of years. I don't think because there is enough demand. After 2 or 3 years, I'm not sure. But like I said, the power consumption is very high. The power demand is going to grow, and I think that will drive the demand of all the electrical products

items.statement: 220 kV class transformer approvals to be applied after new plant commissioning, expected 3-6 months with verbal commitments from existing customers
items.quote: Yes. So we don't have any approval. Once this plant will function, only then we can apply for the approvals of 220 kV class transformers. But I have said earlier that in the same plant, we start manufacturing the lower kV class transformer till we get the approval for higher kV class, and we start getting orders. But a lot of our customers to whom we supply the transformers right now, they also re

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue INR192.61 crores, up 43% QoQ and 12% YoY; EBITDA INR40.06 crores at 20.8% margin; PAT INR32.98 crores at 16.5% margin
items.quote: For Q2 FY27, Shilchar Technologies reported revenue from operation of INR192.61 crores, up 43% over Q1 FY27 and up 12% over Q2 FY26. EBITDA, excluding other income, stood at INR40.06 crores with an EBITDA margin of 20.8%. Profit after tax for the quarter stood at INR32.98 crores with a PAT margin of 16.5%.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue approximately INR330 crores, targeting INR225-230 crores per quarter in H2 to achieve FY27 target
items.quote: And going forward, like I said that we are on the road to achieve our original target of INR750 crores sales for the entire year, meaning that we will be able to -- we will be doing more than INR225 crores, INR230 crores every quarter going forward.

items.statement: Majority production is renewable transformers, minimal distribution transformers, new 220 kV capacity to add 6,500 MVA out of 14,000 MVA total
items.quote: Distribution transformer, we hardly make. We make in very less quantity. So major is all renewable transformers.

items.statement: Exploring diversification and acquisitions in related fields under NDA, will disclose when progressed
items.quote: Yes, we are exploring.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation in Middle East and global political factors create uncertainty for export conditions and freight costs
items.quote: I mean, of course, we would like to maintain the same higher EBITDA, but the market situation, the world political situation, a lot of things are dependent.

items.statement: New capacity requires trained manpower and quality systems, ramp-up will take time beyond just plant commissioning
items.quote: No, it's not possible because it's not that we turn on the machine and the transformers are being produced. I mean there is a lot of things which are involved. First is the approval, the trained manpower, the quality system, all those things. So it takes time.

items.statement: FY27 AUM guidance maintained at Rs 50,000 crore; PAT expected around Rs 1,600 crore
items.quote: So FY'27 guideline in terms of AUM, we are maintaining guidance at about Rs. 50,000 crores. Since we have already reached about Rs. 44,000 crores AUM, we may slightly do better, but we are maintaining guidance of achieving Rs. 50,000 crores AUM. And as far as the profit after tax is concerned, I think we will be about Rs. 1,600 crores.

items.statement: FY28 AUM target Rs 65,000 crore; RoE 19-21%; RoA 4.2-4.7%
items.quote: We are on the track to achieve an AUM of Rs. 65,000 crores by FY '28 with return on average equity in the range about 19% to 21% and return on average assets of 4.2% to 4.7%.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM Rs 43,878 crore, up 62% YoY and 9% QoQ
items.quote: Our consolidated AUM stood at Rs. 43,878 crores, reflecting a robust 62% year-on-year growth and 9% quarter-on-quarter growth.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM Rs 21,000 crore, up 102% YoY and 10% QoQ
items.quote: AUM saw robust growth to Rs. 21,000 crores, a sequential increase of 10% quarter-on-quarter, led by steady customer demand and productivity gains.

items.statement: MSME AUM Rs 7,016 crore, up 25% YoY; disbursements Rs 560 crore, up 36% YoY
items.quote: Our MSME AUM grew to Rs. 7,016 crores, up 25% year-on-year, and disbursement stood Rs.560 crores for Q2 FY '27, up 36% year-on-year.

items.statement: Housing AUM Rs 8,325 crore, up 39% YoY
items.quote: Our housing AUM stood at Rs. 8,325 crores, delivering a year-on-year growth of 39%.

items.statement: Construction finance AUM Rs 7,503 crore, up 51% YoY across 304 projects
items.quote: Our construction finance AUM saw healthy growth of 51% year-on-year to Rs. 7,503 crores, spread across 304 active projects.

items.statement: Co-lending AUM Rs 9,083 crore, up 60% YoY and 12% QoQ, now 21% of total AUM
items.quote: Our co-lending AUM for Q2'FY27 surged 60% year-on-year and 12% quarter-on-quarter to Rs. 9,083 crores, now accounting for 21% of total AUM.

items.statement: Blended yield 17.5%, spread 8.3% in Q2 FY27; NII Rs 812 crore, up 69% YoY
items.quote: Our blended yields and spreads on net advances increased in the quarter to 17.5% and 8.3% respectively, driven by increasing share of high-yield products and leveraging competitive cost of funds. Our net interest income for Q2 FY '27 stood at Rs. 812 crores, up 69% year-on-year.

items.statement: Gold loan yield improved to 19% in Q2 FY27; management confident yields will not decline significantly
items.quote: And with this combination, our yields have improved to 19% in Q2’ FY27. Going forward, even while the competition is increasing, we are quite confident that our yields will not go significantly lower, and we will always maintain an equilibrium between yield s, growth and asset quality

items.statement: Non-interest income Rs 273 crore, up 34% YoY, contributing 25% of net total income
items.quote: Non-interest income grew 34% year-on-year to Rs. 273 crores, contributing 25% on our net total income for the quarter.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved to 41% in Q2 FY27 from 44% in Q1 FY27 and 49% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Yet the cost-to-income ratio improved to 41% in Q2 FY '27 from 44% in Q1 FY '27 and 49% in Q2 FY '26, reflecting our continued focus on operating efficiency.

items.statement: Pre-provision operating profit surged 84% YoY to Rs 636 crore; PAT Rs 418 crore, up 77% YoY
items.quote: As a result of margin expansion, operational efficiency improvement, and strong traction in fee income, our pre-provision operating profit surged 84% year-on-year to Rs. 636 crores for the quarter. Further, we continued our strong profitability momentum in Q2 FY '27, delivering a robust profit after tax of Rs. 418 crores, up 77% year-on-year.

items.statement: Consolidated GNPA 1.2%, NNPA 0.8%; gold loan Stage-2 spike Rs 1,266 crore due to shorter-tenure products, expected to normalize next quarter
items.quote: Our consolidated gross Stage-3 ratio spiked by 22 basis quarter-on-quarter to 1.2% due to spike in gold loan at around similar levels. Housing loan Stage-3 remained steady at 1.2%, and construction finance Stage-3 improved significantly, dropping to 0.02% level on account of wr ite-offs and recoveries as mentioned earlier. The net Stage-3 ratio stood at about 0.8%, up 22 basis points sequentially

items.statement: Credit cost 0.8% in Q2; expected sustainable range 0.6-0.9%
items.quote: Our credit costs for the quarter stood at 0.8%, and we expect to maintain credit costs in the range of 0.6% to 0.9% level on a sustainable basis going forward.

items.statement: Added 176 branches in Q2 (154 gold loan, 22 non-gold); total network 1,609 branches; target 500 gold loan branches in FY27
items.quote: So this year we intend to add about, as per the board, board has given us approval for 600 branches. We are going to add about 500 branches this year in the gold loan alone. Besides that, we will add more branches in the MSME and affordable housing.

items.statement: Gold loan branch productivity Rs 18.2 crore per branch vs Rs 19.2 crore; mature branches (18+ months) at ~Rs 20 crore
items.quote: aggregate branch productivity continues to remain resilient and now stands at Rs. 18.2 crores per branch versus Rs. 19.2 crores per branch, which is function of rapid network expansion and addition of new branches during the quarter

items.statement: Raised $300 million via maiden USD senior secured bond under GMTN in H1 FY27; Rs 500 crore CP + Rs 1,271 crore NCD/CP in Q1
items.quote: Yet I am delighted to share that Capri Global raised $300 million through its GMTN program during H1 FY '27 via a maiden U.S. dollar senior secured bond issue. As part of liability diversification journey, we further raised Rs. 500 crores via commercial papers in addition to Rs. 1,271 crores raised in Q1 FY '27 through a combination of NCD and CP.

items.statement: RBI revised gold loan guidelines (effective April 2026) led to shorter-tenure products causing technical delinquencies; schemes discontinued
items.quote: Following the RBI's revised gold loan guideline with effect from April 2026, which required accrued interest to be factored into LTV ceiling for bullet loans, most major gold loan lenders moved towards shorter tenure products. We similarly introduced monthly and bi-monthly repayment frequency loans in Q1 FY '27. These shorter cycles led to technical delinquencies driven by repayment convenience re

items.statement: IRDAI consultation paper impact: expect RoE decline ~1% in FY28-29; potential beneficiary of higher remuneration in underserved markets
items.quote: Therefore, if implemented, the new draft guidelines, while FY '27 may not likely see much impact, we expect return on average equity for FY '28 and '29 to decline by about 1% at consolidated level. Also, the consultation paper puts forth the framework that could allow higher remuneration for distribution in the underserved m arket, including rural areas, smaller towns, smaller cities, thereby ince

items.statement: Self-employed non-professional customers now 76% of housing AUM; focus on smaller ticket, higher yielding loans
items.quote: From a product and customer segment perspective, we will continue to focus on smaller ticket loans and higher yielding business with increased emphasis on self-employed non-professional customers, which now contributes 76% to our AUM.

items.statement: Gold loan focus on sub-Rs 3 lakh ticket size to defend yields; average ticket size Rs 2.14 lakh
items.quote: So, what we mean that our ticket size is still at less than Rs. 3 lakhs, and if you see, some of the competition which are doing gold loan s above Rs. 5 lakh ticket size, the interest rate there is very low in terms of net realizations. So, our focus will continue to remain in the below Rs. 3 lakh ticket size where yields are better

items.statement: Digital payments penetration 91.2% in MSME/housing (Sep) vs 90.7% (Jun); Capri loan app 17 lakh transactions, Rs 594 crore value in Q2
items.quote: Digital penetration across our MSME and housing businesses continues to demonstrate sustained momentum, with 91.2% of the inbound payment received digitally in September compared to 90.7% in June. Our Capri loan application facilitated over 17 lakh transactions aggregating approximately Rs. 594 crores during Q2.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance for FY27 lowered to 7-9% from earlier 9-11%
items.quote: We now expect revenue growth of 7% to 9% in FY27 compared with our earlier guidance of 9% to 11%.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected broadly in line with FY26 vs earlier 50-100 bps expansion
items.quote: We expect FY27 EBITDA margin to be broadly in line with FY26 compared with our earlier expectation of 50 to 100 basis points of expansion.

items.statement: Confident of returning to 9-11% revenue growth in FY28
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain confident in our ability to return to 9% to 11% revenue growth in FY28, supported by our new digital-first platforms, enhanced marketing capabilities and greater operational efficiency.

items.statement: Retail volumes grew ~2% driven by strong demand for lower price point items
items.quote: Retail volumes grew approximately 2%, driven by strong demand for our lower price point items.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded ~197 bps to 65.5% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Gross margin expanded by approximately 197 basis points to 65.5%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined to 8.1% in Q2 FY27 from 10% a year ago
items.quote: EBITDA was INR76.2 crores, down 13.5%, with a margin of 8.1% compared to 10% in Q2 last year.

items.statement: Digital share target of 50% of B2C revenue by Q4 FY27
items.quote: With the transition complete, we expect digital to return to its earlier growth trajectory, and we continue to work towards our target of digital share at 50% of B2C revenue by Q4 FY27.

items.statement: INR36 crores capex for U.K. warehouse migration in Q2 FY27
items.quote: the main part of this capex related to the U.K. warehouse migration. The commentary, we mentioned the 4 different premises and 2 studios migrate in a single premises to improve the efficiencies and order club bing, which will result in benefit in the coming years, but that was necessary change and easy to operate in a single premises. So that we have invested around INR36 crores over there

items.statement: Completed migration of all retail websites to Shopify Enterprise and consolidated U.K. 4 sites into single headquarters
items.quote: During the quarter, we completed 2 of the major operational projects. The migration of all our retail websites to Shopify Enterprise and the consolidation of our U.K. 4 different sites into single headquarters.

items.statement: Revenue impact of Shopify migration ~USD2.8 million or 2.8 percentage points of growth
items.quote: Based on our internal assessment, the revenue impact in the quarter was approximately USD2.8 million or around 2.8 percentage point of growth.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamond share rose to 12% of total retail revenue from ~10% a year ago
items.quote: In-house brands contributed 57% of B2C revenue and the lab-grown diamond share rose to 12% of total retail revenue from about 10% a year back, strengthening our differentiation and pricing.

items.statement: Lifestyle products ~40% of B2C revenue, medium-term target 50%
items.quote: Lifestyle products contributed approximately 40% of B2C revenue, and we continue to work towards a medium-term objective of 50% share.

items.statement: 360,000 new customers acquired over trailing 12 months, 38% retention, avg 23 pieces per customer per year
items.quote: Under our 4R framework, we reached more than 127 million household s with approximately 687,000 unique customers on a trailing 12 -month basis and 360,000 new customers acquired over trailing 12 months, 38% retention and an average of 23 pieces per customer buying per year

items.statement: Inventory buildup ~INR100 crores YoY for festive season readiness, expected to moderate by Q3-Q4 to 200-220 days inventory
items.quote: We have roughly around INR100 crores inventory buildup compared to the last year same time, mainly related to the readiness of festive season and the uncertain environment across the world. So some readiness that we have in terms of inventory for upcoming festive season time. But normally, we see that inventory build in that time, and we're expecting by Q3 and Q4, it will moderate that and the inv

items.statement: Net cash INR186 crores as of Sep 30, 2026 vs INR279 crores Mar 2026, reduction due to seasonal inventory and U.K. capex
items.quote: As of September 30, 2026, our net cash stood at INR186 crores compared to INR279 crores of March '26. This reduction is mainly related to seasonal inventory buildup and capex related to U.K. warehouse migration of INR36 crores.

items.statement: Second interim dividend of INR1.5 per share declared, Board to consider buyback after building cash for acquisitions
items.quote: The Board has declared a second interim dividend of INR1.5 per equity share, following the first interim dividend of INR1.5 per share in Q1 FY27. Our capital allocation approach continues to balance investment in growth, shareholder returns and balance sheet strength.

items.statement: Board decided to continue dividend tradition, will deploy additional cash for buyback after building cash for future acquisitions
items.quote: Board has decided to continue our tradition of the dividend paying company. And the dividend is relatively modest. It's not a very large dividend. We want to build up some cash for future acquisitions or future strategic moves. And after we have built the cash, we will definitely deploy any additional cash for buyback.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on digital-first transition and customer acquisition cost payback within 6 months
items.quote: We want to acquire a customer that can become profitable for us within 6 months. So we don't want to overinvest into acquiring a new customer so that we get hit by the profitability within the quarter or the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: U.S. constant currency revenue declined 4.1% YoY in Q2 FY27 while units grew 4.8% and ASP fell 8.4%
items.quote: In U.S., revenue grew 4.3% to INR500 crores in rupee terms and declined 4.1% in constant currency. The shift towards value is clearest here. Unit rose 4.8%, while the average selling price was 8.4% lower as consumer moved to lower price point

items.statement: U.K. constant currency revenue declined 7% YoY in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The U.K. had a most challenging quarter. Revenues grew 2.3% to INR257.2 crores in rupee terms, but declined 7% in constant currency.

items.statement: Europe ex-U.K. revenue grew 18.3% YoY in rupee terms, 8% in constant currency
items.quote: Europe, excluding U.K., delivered the strongest underlying growth. Revenue rose 18.3% to INR110 crores and 8% in constant currency terms, led by 11.5% in units growth.

items.statement: B2B revenue grew 32.4% YoY to INR70.9 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our B2B business delivered another strong quarter with revenue up 32.4% to INR70.9 crores.

items.statement: U.S. midterm election contentiousness may divert eyeballs from programming, factored into guidance
items.quote: At this time, we see some possibility of contentiousness there, which might take eyeballs away from our programming. Therefore, we included that as one of the factors influencing our guidance.

items.statement: U.K. consumer headwinds: inflation 3.5%, consumer confidence sharpest fall since 2020, discretionary spending dispersed
items.quote: U.K. inflation rose to 3.5% in September, driven by a higher fuel cost, non-food retail sales were almost flat. And in October, consumer confidence recorded its sharpest monthly fall since 2020. As households held back ahead of autumn budget, discretionary category such as our field dispersed.

items.statement: India launch planned after Germany reaches robust profitability, potential e-com acquisition for FY30 target
items.quote: Down the road, first, we want to get Germany to robust profitability before we get into a new country. But definitely, India is on the cards.

items.statement: Sustainable effective tax rate 18-20% for next 2-3 years due to Germany loss carryforwards and FTC credits
items.quote: Sustainable basis remains 18% to 20% range in mid-term like for next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Upgraded Prestige & Above volume growth target to 30% for FY27 and maintained EBITDA margin guidance of around 20% for the year
items.quote: Looking ahead, we have upgraded our Prestige & Above volume growth to 30% in FY27, and we remain confident of sustaining an EBITDA margin of around 20% for the year.

items.statement: Luxury portfolio on track to meet 25% value growth guidance for FY27
items.quote: See, we have done a turnover of Rs. 475 crores last year and we are well in course of meeting our guidance of 25% growth in terms of value.

items.statement: Prestige & Above volume grew 36% YoY in Q2 FY27 to 5.28 million cases, driven by vodka structural shift and Karnataka policy changes
items.quote: The Prestige & Above category continued its strong upward trajectory, recording highest ever volume of 5.28 million cases at 36% volume growth.

items.statement: Vodka category share of IMFL reached 6.3% in Q2 FY27, up from 4.5% in 2026 and 3.7% in 2025, driven by Gen Z, women, and flavored vodka
items.quote: In 2025, it was 3.7 %; in 2026, it became 4.5 %; and this quarter Q2, it is 6.3 %.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 440 bps YoY to 48.0% in Q2 FY27, driven by premiumization (+510 bps) and price increases (+85 bps), partially offset by packaging cost volatility (~Rs. 27 cr impact)
items.quote: Gross margin during the quarter is 48 .0%, representing a 440 basis point expansion on year-on-year basis and 109 basis point compression on quarter -on-quarter basis.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 462 bps YoY to 20.4% in Q2 FY27, reflecting premiumization, operating efficiencies, and cost discipline
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 20.4%, expanding by 462 bps on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Packaging material volatility impacted gross margin by ~Rs. 27 crore (155-160 bps) in Q2 FY27; grain price inflation mitigated through higher stock build; FCI ethanol allocation at 72 lakh metric ton expected to stabilize prices from Novemb
items.quote: This was offset to a certain extent by the recent volatility in the packaging material prices which resulted in approximately Rs. 27 crores of financial impact.

items.statement: Glass bottle, PET resin, and laminate prices impacted by West Asia conflict; freight rates increased tremendously affecting export margins
items.quote: On packaging material, there has been an impact on account of the West Asia war, and particularly on the glass bottle and the PET resin prices and also some laminate prices.

items.statement: Prestige & Above now 75% flavored vodka; vodka 30% of volume, whisky 40-45%, brandy/rum/gin remainder; non-vodka P&A grew ~20% YoY
items.quote: Vodka is 30% of our volume, whisky is about 40%, 45%, and rest is brandy and rum and gin is still very small because it's only at the extreme top end.

items.statement: Karnataka premium volumes grew >100% YoY after duty reduction and free pricing; Maharashtra P&A returned to growth in Q2; Tamil Nadu volumes up 20% with new digital payment rule for brands above Rs. 1,000
items.quote: Karnataka has led the way, and we have really seen after the reduction in the duties and free pricing. To give you an example, say Radico in the current quarter, we have grown more than 100% of our premium volumes there.

items.statement: Export shipments to West Asia bounced back after initial disruption; freight rates up significantly, partially absorbed by customers and consumer price increases; present in 70 duty-free locations targeting 100
items.quote: We are currently in around 70 duty -free locations, and our objective is to get to 100.

items.statement: DRI investigation on Scotch imports under HSN 2208; company asserts compliance, no change in import code; matter being studied by Ministry of Commerce and DRI with inputs from stakeholders
items.quote: The Scotches which we were importing from last 10 to 20 years, are in the same HSN code as 2208. And after 15th July also, we are importing it in the same code.

items.statement: UK FTA provides 8-10% reduction in BIO duty; luxury portfolio priced above BIO, mainstream portfolio well below BIO, so minimal competitive impact
items.quote: We are seeing about close to 8% to 10% reduction in the BIO. And if you see our portfolio, whether it's Rampur or Virasat, it's a single malt, and it is already priced higher than the existing BIO.

items.statement: Deliberate working capital investment in Q2 to support premium growth, new launches, and secure raw/packaging materials amid volatility; expected to normalize in H2 FY27
items.quote: During the quarter, we made a deliberate investment in working capital to support the strong growth in our premium portfolio, new launches and secure key raw material and packaging material amid price volatility.

items.statement: ROE and ROCE improved in Q2 supported by higher operating profit and better asset utilization; expect further improvement as premium portfolio expands
items.quote: Both ROE and ROCE improved during the quarter, supported by higher operating profit and better asset utilization.

items.statement: Capex directed towards maintenance, operational efficiencies, and essential capacity optimization; disciplined capital allocation approach maintained
items.quote: We remain disciplined in our approach to capital allocation , with capex directed towards maintenance, operational efficiencies and essential capacity optimization.

items.statement: Dilip Banthiya elevated to Executive Director & CFO; Saket Somani elevated to Deputy CFO with expanded mandate across strategy, financial planning, IR, and digital transformation
items.quote: Effective today, Dilip Banthiya joins the Board as Executive Director and CFO, bringing his deep financial, capital allocations and alcobev industry experience to the Board.

items.statement: IMFL volume over 10 million cases in Q2 FY27, up 7% YoY; Regular volume degrowth due to Andhra base effect and Maharashtra/Karnataka policy changes
items.quote: During Q2 FY27, we delivered a strong all -round performance , with total IMFL volume s of over 10 million cases, reflecting a 7% year -on-year growth.

items.statement: IMFL business margin ~24%+ in Q2 FY27; non-IMFL business margin ~9.5-10%
items.quote: So, the IMFL business margins because of the luxury and the vodka being major share , it is approximately 24% plus, and non -IMFL business is around 9.5% to 10% for this quarter.

items.statement: Pricing improved 85 bps overall in Q2; realization up 2.2% QoQ and ~12% YoY mainly from mix shift (P&A +36%, Regular -15%); normal mix difference 5-6%, annual price increase 100-125 bps
items.quote: Whatever price increase we have got in 7, 8 states, right? And on quarter -on-quarter basis, the realization improved by 2.2%. On a year -on-year basis, the improvement is much higher, around 12%.

items.statement: Industry price hike process starts November ahead of February excise policies; inflation absorbed currently, relief expected at next revision
items.quote: At this point of time, it will start from November onwards in various excise by the industry representatives.

items.statement: Spirit of Kashmyr matter subjudice in court; no comment at this time
items.quote: Yes. So, I think the matter is subjudice in the court, and I don't want to comment on that at this point of time.

items.statement: Uttar Pradesh elections not expected to slow business; liquor revenue ~Rs. 60,000-65,000 crore, system well set
items.quote: It does not slow down during election.

items.statement: Vodka growth driven by Flavours of India innovation (Mango, Jamun, Aam Panna); 1-2 more flavors planned; international flavored vodka only 25% vs India 75%, but Indian palate favors flavors
items.quote: Our flavored vodka would be about close to 75%. And as we said, we have been innovators in making this category grow.

items.statement: After Dark relaunched in 10 states with positive traction; grew ~60% last year; Virasat Indian Single Malt seeing tremendous response across states; Jamun and Aam Panna generating high tertiary interest
items.quote: Now, after the new pack change, we ha ve entered in 10 states as of now, and we are getting the positive traction of the brand.

items.statement: Technology spending directed at engineering-led programs connecting silicon, software, and connected devices; customers consolidating vendors for larger integrated scope
items.quote: Technology spending is increasingly directed at engineering-led programs that connect silicon, software, and connected devices, which is where our capabilities sit. Customers are consolidating vendors and looking for partners who can take on larger, more integrated scope.

items.statement: Total contract value signed in Q2 was $47 million, up 66% YoY; $25 million new bookings, rest renewals; annual contract value $34 million
items.quote: Our total contract value signed during the quarter was $47 million of which $25 million Q2 & H1 FY27 Concall Transcript represented new bookings and the rest was renewals. TCV increased by 66% over the same quarter last year. Annual contract value for orders won in the quarter was about $34 million

items.statement: EBITDA margin 12.9% (+330 bps QoQ, +700 bps YoY); EBIT margin 8.9% (+250 bps QoQ, +660 bps YoY); PAT margin 8% (+8.8% QoQ, +143.8% YoY)
items.quote: As we benefit from operating leverage, EBITDA for the quarter was Rs.41 Crores, translating into an EBITDA margin of 12.9%, an improvement of 330 basis points sequentially, and 700 basis points year-on-year. EBIT for the quarter stood at Rs.29 Crores, with an EBIT margin of 8.9%, up 250 basis points sequentially, and 660 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Software services expected to deliver single-digit sustained growth above industry average for mid/small tier; product solutions targeting $12-14M/quarter run rate for 10-12% EBITDA margins
items.quote: However, going forward, I think we would be moderating that growth to above industry average, particularly for the mid tier or small tier companies. So we should be delivering single digit growth on a sustained basis, at least for the foreseeable future.

items.statement: Headcount grew 7% QoQ; LTM attrition lowered to 9.3%; utilization improved to 86%
items.quote: At the close of Q2, the head count grew by 7%, with LTM attrition lowering to 9.3% and utilization improving to 86%.

items.statement: Software services revenue Rs.252 Cr (+34% YoY, +14.6% QoQ); product solutions Rs.69 Cr (+2.4% YoY, -42% QoQ) due to memory/component pressures
items.quote: Software services revenue was Rs.252 Crores, up 34% year-on-year and 14.6% sequentially. Product solutions revenue moderated to Rs.69 Crores, up 2.4% year-on-year, and reducing by 42% sequentially, as volumes were impacted by ongoing pressures relating to memory availability and component pricing.

items.statement: Inventory spike due to memory and components backed by firm customer orders; zero risk on inventory holding
items.quote: That is correct. It is a combination of largely memory and other components which are required to deliver to customers where there are supply chain issues. Rajiv Mody: But these are all backed by firm customer orders. So there is zero risk on us holding on to the inventory

items.statement: Cash and investment position of Rs.399 Crores at quarter end; strong balance sheet maintained
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong. We close the quarter with a cash and investment position of about Rs.399 Crores.

items.statement: CSAT at 4.5/5, well above industry benchmark of 3.75
items.quote: Our CSAT stands at 4.5 out of 5, well above the industry benchmark of 3.75.

items.statement: European telematics multiyear program (3-4 years) with leading automotive OEM; revenue recognition started in Q2, full ramp-up achieved by Oct 1, 2026

Yogesh Rathi: Yes, thanks. So, whatever deal we have won, so we have achieved already the full ramp up as on October 1, 2026

items.statement: Sasken Silicon revenue split roughly equally between consulting/design services and IP licensing; IP royalties expected in coming years as products reach manufacturing and sales
items.quote: Our revenue right now is on a very rough basis, split equally between two types of deals. items.statement: 90-95% of H2 service revenues tied up from signed orders; confident on achieving full year numbers; targeting sustained momentum into FY28
items.quote: I think on your first question, I think we would have about 90% to 95% of our revenues tied up for the second half and all efforts are also on for winning more business in Q3 and Q4, that should add. So overall, we are fairly comfortable, confident on achi eving our overall yearly numbers

items.statement: Focus on financial discipline and prudent capital allocation while remaining flexible to invest in capabilities and opportunities
items.quote: Emphasis remains on financial discipline and prudent capital allocation while remaining flexible to invest in capabilities and oppor tunities that support the business

items.statement: Product solutions quarterly volatility due to shipment schedules, product lifecycles, memory/component pricing; better evaluated annually
items.quote: Product solution, on the other hand, can have a quarter-to-quarter variation depending on program milestones, shipment schedules, and product life cycles. We therefore believe product solution is better evaluated over a longer period rather than through the moment in any single quarter.

items.statement: Annual salary revisions implemented across levels in July per established commitment to people
items.quote: reflecting our focus on disciplined execution, even as we implemented annual salary revisions across levels in July, keeping with Sasken's established commitment to its people.

items.statement: Automotive peers facing stagnation and client-specific issues; Sasken navigating via technology closeness, semiconductor partner relationships, and AI-driven high-performance compute investments

One is of course the geopolitical one and second is the technological one. items.statement: 60x4x3 plan (Rs.240 Cr revenue target) may be delayed by 12 months; focus remains intense using organic and inorganic means
items.quote: I think on the first one we are on the on the task and like I said last time maybe I think we may be delayed by 12 months or so but our focus is intense to see how we achieve that goal objective and both using organic, inorganic means, and ensure that we meet our objectives.

items.statement: Launched Juniper Alta device developed end-to-end and shipped within 18 months; demonstrates concept-to-commercialization capability
items.quote: During the quarter, we also launched Juniper Alta, a new device developed end-to-end and brought to shipment within 18 months. The program demonstrates our ability to take products from concept through engineering and commercialization.

items.statement: AI priorities: internal efficiency, AI-enabled delivery, customer-facing AI capabilities, organizational readiness; measured by customer value and operating performance improvement
items.quote: Our four priorities are internal efficiency, AI-enabled delivery, customer facing AI capabilities, and organizational readiness. We will measure progress by value delivered to customers and the improvement in our operating performance.

items.statement: FY27 screen opening target of 90-100 screens, mostly in H2 under capital-light formats
items.quote: We remain on track to open up 90 to 100 new screens in FY2 7 with the bulk of the openings in the second half, mainly under capital-light formats

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance of INR 300-330 crores
items.quote: In terms of the capex, this year, we will do around INR300 crores to INR320 crores, INR330 crores in that range, overall capex.

items.statement: FY28 capex expected above INR 350 crores due to higher screen additions
items.quote: And next year will be higher as we mentioned that the screen additions will be more than current year. And therefore, the capex are likely to be more than INR350 crores, plus/minus depending on how the pipeline and fit-outs and the execution gets going on the ground.

items.statement: Depreciation to reduce by INR 35-40 crores annually due to useful life extension
items.quote: Accordingly, the useful life has been increased and the depreciation, therefore, is now lower between INR35 crores to INR40 crores a year.

items.statement: Target net screen additions of 150-175 per year from next fiscal
items.quote: 150, 175 is a number that we could achieve from next fiscal every year, could be even more.

items.statement: Capital allocation policy: 30% of annual surplus cash flow to shareholders via dividends/buybacks
items.quote: Third, from the surplus that remains, we expect to return around 30% of our annual surplus cash flow to shareholders through dividends, buybacks or a combination of the two, with the timing and quantu m at the Board's discretion

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA to remain within 0.5x after distributions
items.quote: Second, we will keep the balance sheet strong with net debt-to-EBITDA remaining within 0.5x after any distribution.

items.quote: Industry gross box office collections reached INR 4,433 crores, the highest quarterly collections on record and the first time the industry crossed INR4,000 crores in a single quarter.

items.statement: PVR INOX footfalls up 4% YoY to 46.3 million in Q2 FY27
items.quote: We welcomed 46.3 million guests during the quarter, up 4% year-on-year as occupancy rose to 30.4%.

items.statement: Hindi box office incremental growth muted due to high base; strong Q3-Q4 slate expected
items.quote: But wait till you have Q3 and Q4, you will see, without making any forward-looking statements for PVR INOX, but at the industry level, we are confident that in Q3 and Q4, you will see a big jump in incremental numbers even for Hindi box office.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 420 bps YoY to 22.3% on Ind AS 116 adjusted basis
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded around 420 basis points to 22.3%, driven by strong operating leverage.

items.statement: F&B gross margins at 77-78% with headroom; 60% of SPH growth from value increase
items.quote: There is a fairly good headroom to grow because if you look at our F&B, I don't think we've shared that information, but 40% of this growth has happened actually through the volume increase and about 60% of the SPH growth has happened through the value increase.

items.statement: ATP and F&B SPH each grew 14% YoY to INR 298 and INR 153 respectively
items.quote: Average ticket price and food and beverage spend per head each grew 14% year-on-year, reaching INR 298 and INR 153, respectively.

items.statement: SMART Cinema pipeline of ~100 signed locations for next 12-18 months
items.quote: And then we have a pipeline of about another 100-odd that we have signed, which should come up in the next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Value offers: weekday morning shows at INR 99, Friday first shows at INR 149, front row seats from INR 79
items.quote: Value offers such as weekday morning shows at INR99, Friday first shows at INR149 and front row seats from INR 79 are bringing in more price-sensitive moviegoers.

items.statement: F&B discounted offers (free refills on weekends) driving volume upgrades to larger packs
items.quote: So discounted F&B is basically on weekends when we do free refills of large category of Pepsi and popcorn, and that's been a very successful initiative.

items.statement: English films grew 87% YoY to INR 1,024 crores; Spider-Man: Brand New Day highest grossing English film at INR 608 crores
items.quote: English language cinema had a standout quarter with collections growing 87% to INR 1,024 crores, crossing INR1,000 crores in a quarter for the first time. Spider-Man: Bran d New Day became India's highest grossing English movie ever at INR608 crores of box office

items.statement: Regional blockbusters: Jana Nayagan (Tamil) INR 200 crores, Toxic (Kannada) INR 296 crores
items.quote: Regional cinema also witnessed a strong box office growth with star-led spectacles like Jana Nayagan in Tamil and Toxic in Kannada grossing INR 200 crores and INR296 crores, respectively.

items.statement: 85% of cinema visitors now consume F&B; personalized offers driven by consumption database
items.quote: Today, we have a scenario where close to about 85% of the people who walk in eat something or the other at the cinema, and that's a fairly healthy number.

items.statement: H1 FY27 free cash flow INR 604 crores; debt repaid INR 259 crores
items.quote: During H1, we generated INR604 crores of free cash flow and repaid INR259 crores of debt.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR 141 crores as of September 2026, up from INR 81 crores in June
items.quote: Even after this payout, we ended September with net cash of INR 141 crores, up from INR81 crores in June.

items.statement: Maiden share buyback of INR 300 crores completed in September 2026
items.quote: We returned part of surplus capital to shareholders in September through our maiden share buyback of INR 300 crores, while retaining sufficient capital for growth.

items.statement: Return on capital employed improved to 16.5% on trailing 12-month basis from 10.2% in FY26
items.quote: Our return on capital employed has improved from 10.2% in FY26 to 16.5% on a trailing 12-month basis, above the pre-COVID benchmark of around 13%.

items.statement: No discussions on ticket price caps in Southern states
items.quote: No conversations at all.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-25% y-o-y, targeting around INR 6,000 crore
items.quote: And hence, for the full year, we should be anywhere between a 20-25% growth on a full-year basis on the revenue. So, looking at perhaps close to a INR 6,000-odd crore, given that growth number.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 maintained at around INR 300 crore including greenfield expansions
items.quote: The guidance for the year continues to remain around INR 300 crore, including the new greenfield expansion in the Mechatronics, Advanced Plastics and Alternate Fuels divisions, which is expected to begin the SOP (Start of Production) in the H2 of financial year.

items.statement: Long-term 20% revenue CAGR from FY25 to FY31 maintained, targeting INR 11,000 crore by FY31
items.quote: In the long term, our compass remains our 20.20.20.20 North Star, aiming for a 20% revenue CAGR between FY 25 through FY 31 and inching closer to a 20% EBITDA margin over the next 5 to 7 years. By FY 31, we aspire to more than double our current revenue base to around INR 11,000 crore.

items.statement: Order book grew to INR 1,879 crore at end of Q2 FY27, up from INR 1,600 crore at end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: Coming to the order book, it has grown to INR 1,879 crore at the end of Q2, up from INR 1,600 crore at the end of Q1 FY 27, providing a healthy visibility for the business going forward.

items.statement: Order book execution timeline: 14% in FY27, 59% in FY28, 27% in FY29
items.quote: Of this order book, approximately 14% is expected to be executed in FY 27 itself, 59% in FY 28 and the remaining 27% in FY 29.

items.quote: At its meeting on 24th October, 2026, the Board approved the setting up of a new Mechatronics manufacturing facility at Manesar in Haryana, with a capital outlay of around INR 150 crore to be funded through a mix of debt and internal accruals.

items.quote: The facility will manufacture advanced electronic components such as the Body Control Module (BCM) for leading OEMs (Original Equipment Manufacturers). items.quote: At Lumax Greenfuel Energy Solutions, we are pleased to report that the Nashik facility has commenced production in Q3 FY 27, the ongoing quarter, supplying ferrule-less tubes and fittings and receptacles to Mahindra & Mahindra.

items.statement: Chakan IV facility in SOP phase, product launch expected December-January
items.quote: Just to discuss the point Mr. Anmol Jain said, the Chakan IV facility is in the SOP phase, but the product launch will actually happen more towards December, January.

items.quote: By powertrain, EV (Electric Vehicle) and CNG (Compressed Natural Gas) together accounts for 29% of the order book, with CNG at 20% and pure EVs at about 9%, while new future technologies account for 22% of the total order book.

items.statement: H2 FY27 capex expected to be similar to H1 at around INR 90 crore each half

items.quote: Analytics and automation grew 5% sequentially and 27% year-on-year, more than twice the company's growth rate. The business now has an annual revenue run rate of about USD 109 million and accounts for approximately 20% of revenue.

items.statement: Utilization declined slightly to 74.9% in Q2 from 75.5% in Q1
items.quote: Utilization in Q2 is 74.9% compared with 75.5% in Q1.

items.quote: Headcount increased 3.4% compared with revenue growth of 1.5%. Utilization declined slightly to 74.9%, while attrition rose to 23.4%.
