items.statement: CAMSPay expected to grow late 20s to 30% annually for next 2 years
items.quote: Our public statements have be en that CAM SPay should grow in a fair manner by about 30-odd percent for the next 2 years

items.statement: Yield decline expected around 3% year-on-year and less than 1% quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: We have always guided that you will see -- some quarters, you will see a 3% to 3.5% drop in yields. But I think quarter-on-quarter, we've done much better. The drop in yield is less than 1%.

items.statement: Expense growth target kept below 10% for the year
items.quote: We had guided in the initial part of the year that we will try to keep it less than 10%.

items.statement: Non-MF revenue target to reach 20% of total within next couple of years
items.quote: We are at the 16%, almost non-mutual fund proportion of sales. And as we said, our target is to get to 20% within the next couple of years.

items.statement: No large customer discounts given or expected in near term
items.quote: There is no large customer discounts given or no renewal discounts that are given in the numbers that you're seeing.

items.statement: Equity AUM grew 15.5% year-on-year, ahead of industry 15.2%
items.quote: Equity AUM grew 15.5%. So ahead of industry, industry was 15.2%.

items.statement: SIP collections grew 16.5% year-on-year vs industry 12.4%
items.quote: SIP collections grew 16.5% year-on-year. This is against the industry 12.4% number.

items.statement: CAMS share of equity net sales upwards of 70% over last year
items.quote: Our share in equity net sales was upwards of 70%.

items.statement: Live SIPs and investor base both grew in share and ahead of industry
items.quote: Live SIPs and investor base, both of them grew in share and grew ahead of industry.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 140 bps to 46% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded 140 basis points to 46%.

items.statement: Non-MF business margin upwards of 18%, close to 19%
items.quote: The non-mutual fund profitability is upwards of 18%, right? So which means it's a very good development from a profitability perspective.

items.statement: Payments business margin at 20%, KRA very profitable, AIF stable at 20% margin
items.quote: Payments has been growing at a profitability level, which exceeded our expectations. So to have a card business mix and then still continue to have a margin of 20% is good.

items.statement: Non-MF steady-state margin target 25%+ in 3 years, aim for 30%
items.quote: I think a steady-state margin of 25% plus is very much on the cards in the 3-year period that we're talking about. Our aim will be to get closer to 30%.

items.statement: SIF AUM at INR20,000 crores with 12 AMCs launched, ~1 lakh investors
items.quote: SIF new product class, almost 12 of our AMCs have now launched SIFs. Overall AUM at INR20,000 crores.

items.statement: GIFT City retail funds AUM crossed INR1,500 crores with 5 launches, 2-3 more in current quarter
items.quote: GIFT City retail funds continue to scale with 5 launches that have happen, 2 more, 2 to 3 more will happen in the current quarter. So the AUM crossed INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: InCred AMC appointed CAMS as MF RTA, taking client count to 32 of 64 licensed AMCs
items.quote: InCred AMC appointed CAMS as its MF RTA, a fairly significant win for us. So we get with this from a client count perspective to 32 out of 64 licensed AMCs.

items.statement: ASK Investments and Carnelian went live with maiden funds; Oaklane and Neo expected in Q3
items.quote: ASK Investments and Carnelian, these 2 went live with their maiden funds during the quarter. And Oaklane and Neo are expected to go live in the coming quarter, which is 3Q.

items.statement: Rearchitecture project ~30% done; legacy utility sunset planned by March-April
items.quote: FUNDSNet is really the face of the RTA utility because this is how the transactions, millions of transactions every day come in. This has all gone live. We are planning to sunset the legacy utility by March, April.

items.statement: Headcount reduced by 250-300 over last 12 months to ~8,200
items.quote: When we started the year, we had around 8,450 was the headcount. I think we are ending the quarter around 8,200. So there's been a 250 reduction in the headcount.

items.statement: Employee productivity rising due to AI and new platform; headcount decline trend to continue 3+ years
items.quote: We believe that this has happened after 30% or approximately 30% of the work on the new platform is done. That is perhaps a trend which will last at least the next 3 more years.

items.statement: Yield drop <1% QoQ, ~3% YoY due to asset mix shift (debt to passive) and telescopic pricing
items.quote: If you see the remaining asset classes, you've seen debt falling down by X percentage, and you've seen the passives going up by the same percentage. So in my asset mix, what you have seen is whatever the yield is given the same absolute number, whatever the yield was contributing by debt, which is, say, a little more than 2, 2.25 bps, has been replaced by passiv es, which is probably 0.5 bps

items.statement: SIF pricing mirrors regular equity fund rates; no yield difference
items.quote: The pricing of the SIF broadly mirrors what we do for the usual funds. So if it is an equity kind of a fund that we have, you will see the same rates that we are charging effectively for equity and regular schemes to be charged for SIF.

items.statement: Repository crossed 1.5 crore demat policies; Bima Central broker module driving growth
items.quote: We crossed 15 million, 1.5 crores demat policies. The important thing is that Bima Central now has a module for brokers.

items.statement: CAMS won all target AMC logos in last 3-4 years; 32 of 64 licensed AMCs now clients
items.quote: In the last 2, 2.5 years, we have flattened that completely. So 32 out of 64 licensed AMCs. And if you reflect on the logos in the last 3 to 4 years, we continue to believe that we have won everything that we wanted to.

items.statement: Insurance digitalization directionally positive; CAMS positioned as 'sold product' with servicing layer
items.quote: There is directionally a possibility that this industry may go heavily into a digital format. We will continue to remain a sold product, a significantly sold product, not a sought product.

items.statement: Account aggregator new pricing model remunerating SIPs expected; regulatory wins may shape future
items.quote: in the account aggregator market, although it remains a smal l business, a new pricing model, remunerating SIPs, etcetera, is about to come in

items.statement: Cash position INR900 crores after INR160 crores dividend paid; INR3.25 interim dividend declared
items.quote: From a cash position, we ended the quarter with a very comfortable INR900 crores cash position. This is after paying around INR160 crores of dividend during the quarter for the earlier 2 quarters. And we've also declared INR3.25 dividend as an interim dividend.

items.statement: MF AUM grew 12.5% YoY to INR58.5 lakh crores; 67% market share maintained
items.quote: CAMS MF AUM, as I said, grew about 12.5%, got to about INR58.5 lakh, 67% market share.

items.statement: AI/headless architecture not a near-term threat; building core systems via LLMs still distant
items.quote: Just taking a large LLM or just building a more intelligent SLM on top of it, giving it some instructions and getting the software built is still some distance away.

items.statement: AMC in-sourcing unlikely; global benchmarks show 90-95% outsourcing intact; scale benefits at INR60 lakh crores AUM
items.quote: Show me 1 example where anybody is able to condense all their operating costs to 7 or 6 or 5 or 4 bps, there will be no one. There will absolutely be no one.

items.statement: Management targets 80-100 new restaurant openings annually in future, up from 50-70 previously
items.quote: CapEx as well, helps us expand from building what we were building in the past, 50 to 70 restaurants, to potentially go up to 80 to 100 restaurants in the future.

items.statement: Approved primary capital infusion of ~130 crore rupees for Indonesia asset upgrades, to be deployed in tranches based on milestones
items.quote: We've set that money aside for for improving the quality of asset. That's that's literally the plan. And, you know, obviously we've taken the approval for the entire money that could go in.

items.statement: India store count reached 619 as of call date, with 12 openings in October alone
items.quote: We have a very strong pipeline to continue to take this journey forward for growth. As Raj earlier mentioned, we are already at 619. This month, we've already opened 12 stores.

items.statement: India restaurant EBITDA margin at 13%, company EBITDA margin at 7.8%; target to reach 15% restaurant EBITDA via volume leverage
items.quote: We had a very strong 13% levels now over last few quarters. But if we look at it from the perspective over last year, a very clear 2.5% improvement in profitability at a restaurant level.

items.statement: Gross margin dipped slightly by ~0.4% due to chicken cost headwinds; supply chain efficiencies and scale expected to improve it
items.quote: We have a slight drop in our gross margins of about 0.4%, but not a very significant amount, and most of those efforts have been through a fantastic work our supply chain is doing.

items.statement: India SSSG of 14% in Q2 FY27, 14th consecutive quarter of positive dine-in traffic growth
items.quote: It's the second consecutive quarter with a very strong SSSG growth of 14% for the quarter, with an ADS of 1,31,000, similar to what we achieved in quarter one.

items.statement: Launching 'Families' pillar in November with kids program and Avengers co-branded premium products to drive traffic and check
items.quote: The Families program is what we're launching this month, this in November, and you will start to experience over the next several months the efforts around our Family program.

items.statement: Peri-Peri LTO delivered 30% higher volumes than Korean Season 2, which was 30% higher than Korean Season 1
items.quote: Korean Season 2 that came in quarter one this year was 30% better volumes than Korean Season 1, and Peri-Peri helped us deliver 30% better volumes than Korean Season 2.

items.statement: Energy costs rising but spending reduced via solar, efficient equipment, lighting; fully offsetting utility inflation
items.quote: As energy costs are going up, we're actually bringing down the energy spending, and that's thanks to all the work that he's doing over there.

items.statement: Supply chain efficiencies from cluster approach and scale (600 to 800 restaurants) lowering distribution costs and improving gross margin
items.quote: As we build these restaurants, and we've got, you know, a whole bunch of openings that will be coming this quarter and the next quarter, these will bring down transportation costs.

items.statement: App frequency up 7% YoY in Q2; CRM engine live on app driving Dine-In Crazy App Deals
items.quote: App frequency is up about 7% year-over-year in Q2. You will find a lot of the digital elements again shared by Kapil as he speaks about the business there.

items.statement: Navratri impact minimal due to balanced veg/non-veg menu; traffic growth overcame any seasonal dip
items.quote: We have a very balanced menu with veg and non-veg, and so we don't see that big a dip during Navratri. We see a small, you know, receding, but this year I can tell you that that the impacts have been minimal.

items.statement: Indonesia Burger King 'Super Hemat' value program added 35-40 transactions per day per restaurant since late September launch
items.quote: We have added about 35 to 40 additional traffic per day per restaurant with just this program. And we're extremely excited about this.

items.statement: Indonesia Burger King restaurant EBITDA turned positive (INR 8M) vs negative last year; Popeyes still a drag with sliding ADS (64k) and losses
items.quote: At a restaurant level, obviously we were closer to break-even, a little higher than break-even, with a marginal INR 8 million restaurant EBITDA that we made, which is still a big shift because last year during the same quarter we were negative.

items.statement: Cash and liquid investments ~1,000 crore; additional ~450 crore from warrants; no plan to use for India expansion currently
items.quote: The total amount that we have on our balance sheet is close to 1,000 crores. And and then obviously there is another warrants that are to that that could give us another 450-odd crores of cash.

items.statement: Indonesia asset upgrade program (HVAC, kitchen equipment, lighting, signage, washrooms) to complete over next 6+ months
items.quote: Asset upgrade is a pillar that's going to be there in Indonesia for the next 6 months, maybe even slightly longer. And what we're doing, what we're doing over there is, again, some of the equipment, energy efficient equipment that's going in there

items.statement: Indonesia target: improve ADS from ~19-20M IDR to 25M IDR (+5M IDR/day/restaurant) and restore 15% restaurant EBITDA margin
items.quote: The target that that I had set with the with the team over there before I came in, full honest, you know, sharing with you, is is to improve every restaurant on a daily basis by 5 million IDR per day per restaurant.

items.statement: Sumit Zaveri promoted to CEO India Business; Sandeep Dey leads Indonesia; Deepa joined supply chain team recently
items.quote: You just heard Sumit Zaveri assigned to a new role. He's been promoted to lead the business here in India. Sandeep is also on the phone, who leads the business in Indonesia.

items.statement: Popeyes Indonesia under active discussion with brand owners to resolve persistent losses and declining ADS
items.quote: We are in active discussion with the brand owners as well to find a suitable answer as far as Popeyes is concerned.

items.statement: Inflation impact on labor (minimum wages) fully baked into annual planning; utilities inflation fully offset by efficiency investments
items.quote: We do reasonably kind of plan for inflation on the labor side, especially minimum wages, because we've seen the trends, so there's absolutely fully fully taken care of.

items.statement: Promoters invested in July; capital allocation strategy for excess funds (new brand vs acquisition) under formulation, to be shared later
items.quote: The promoters just came in in July, and, you know, the the entire, you know, capital, so there's some capital to come in as well with the warrants, so so we we are working together with the promoters.

name: Home First Finance Company India Ltd

items.statement: Targets 25% AUM growth to reach Rs. 20,000 crore by March 2027
items.quote: We are working towards a 25% growth target, which effectively means that we have to hit a Rs. 20,000 crore number by Mar 2027.

items.statement: Targets exit ROE of 15% for FY27 and 16% for FY28
items.quote: Our target is 15% exit for this year and 16% exit for next year.

items.statement: Commits to maintaining 5.0% to 5.2% spread on floating rate book
items.quote: We are running a fully floating rate book, and we are committed to maintaining a 5.0% to 5.2% spread, which is what we have always articulated.

items.statement: Targets 10 bps annual reduction in opex to assets ratio
items.quote: On opex, our commitment is to reduce by 10 basis points every year. So, opex to assets, we would like to push that down by 10 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Spread excluding co-lending at 5.2%, NIM at 6.0%, cost of borrowing at 7.8%, incremental borrowing cost at 7.5%
items.quote: Consequently, our spread, excluding co-lending, remained healthy at 5.2%, while net interest margin remained at 6.0%.

items.statement: Insurance distribution fee draft circular impact ~35 bps on ROA; expects ~10 bps concession, net 20-25 bps to offset via LAP mix, assignment income, pricing
items.quote: The final impact on our ROA is about ~35 basis points. So, we have to basically make up for the 35 bps. We are hopeful that out of that 35bps, about maybe 10 bps will eventually come back as a concession from the insurance authorities.

items.statement: AUM Rs. 18,010 crore, up 27% YoY and 6.3% QoQ; disbursements Rs. 1,705 crore, up 32.2% YoY and 4.7% QoQ
items.quote: At the end of September 2026, AUM stood at Rs. 18,010 crore, up 27% year-on-year and 6.3% sequentially. Quarterly disbursement reached Rs. 1,705 crore, an increase of 32.2% year-on-year and 4.7% sequentially.

items.statement: Co-lending disbursements Rs. 1.8 crore in Q2, portfolio Rs. 593 crore (3.3% of AUM); expects uptick in Q3
items.quote: Co-lending disbursements stood at Rs. 1.8 crore during the quarter, taking the co-lending portfolio to Rs. 593 crore or 3.3% of the AUM.

items.statement: Direct assignment transactions of Rs. 281 crore executed in Q2
items.quote: During this quarter, we executed direct assignment transactions of Rs. 281 crore.

items.statement: Gross Stage 3 improved 10 bps QoQ to 1.7%; 1+ DPD 4.7%, 30+ DPD 3.2% unchanged QoQ; credit cost 40 bps
items.quote: Both early delinquency indicators were unchanged sequentially, with 1+day past due at 4.7% and 30 + days past due at 3.2%. Gross Stage 3 improved by 10 basis points sequentially to 1.7%.

items.statement: Stage 3 provision coverage 23.6%; total coverage including management overlays 46.4%
items.quote: Including these overlays, total provision coverage to Stage 3 was 46.4% as of Sept'26.

items.statement: Balance transfer outflows reduced to ~4.5% from 5-6% range; expects 4-6% range going forward
items.quote: We used to be at about 5% to 6%. We have brought it down to about 4.5%. We don't want to read too much into it at this point of time. Broadly, we want to convey that balance transfers will be in the 4% to 6% range.

items.statement: ECL assumptions recalibrated every quarter
items.quote: We are now recalibrating the ECL assumptions every quarter.

items.statement: Added 6 branches in Q2, network at 181 branches and 379 touch points; plans 20-25 branches/year, 10-15 more in H2 FY27
items.quote: Branch additions, we normally do at a run rate of about 20 to 25 branches a year. So, broadly at the same pace. At the moment, we have added about 10 this year. So, about 10 to 15 will get added in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Individual housing loans 84% of portfolio; LAP within 20% guardrail, currently ~15%; apartments 30%, self-construction 30%, plots 1-2%, repair/renovation 1%
items.quote: Individual housing loans accounted for 84% of the portfolio, while origination yield, excluding co-lending, was 13%.

items.statement: LAP share can increase by 5% for 6-7 bps spread benefit; holding as headroom for later use
items.quote: We do keep LAP as a kind of headroom that we have, we can increase it by another 5%. So, an increase of 5% in LAP can give us maybe a spread increase of 6 to 7 basis points.

items.statement: Origination yield ex co-lending 13%, disbursement yield 13%; book yield fell 10 bps QoQ due to past rate pass-through
items.quote: Both portfolio yields, excluding co-lending, and disbursement yields stood at 13%, reflecting consistency in pricing discipline and quality customer acquisition.

items.statement: Demand good across board; H1 strong, expects momentum to continue in H2; tariff issues in Gujarat/Tamil Nadu resolved post Oct 2025
items.quote: Demand is good across the board. And as you mentioned, we have tale of 2 halves. We have conveyed that, let's say, 3 quarters back, there were some external issues like the tariffs, etc, which impacted some of our markets.

items.statement: No significant drought impact on portfolio; customers in manufacturing/services in urban areas, not agriculture-dependent
items.quote: Our business is basically serving customers in the manufacturing and service-related segments. So, our customers don't have too much of an overhang or involvement or any dependence on the agricultural sector.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu team stabilized, leadership in place; expects growth reversal in Q3-Q4; UP scaling on track
items.quote: In Tamil Nadu, the teams are in place now. Last year, there were a couple of regions where there was no leadership, etc, but leadership has been put in place.

items.statement: Bounce rate higher in Oct due to calendar day (4th falling on weekend); better than last year's Oct
items.quote: The bounce rate figure is also a function of which day the particular 4th of the month falls in. So, if it is a Saturday or Sunday, then the bounce rate is slightly higher.

items.statement: Funding mix: banks 58%, NHB 14%, assignment/co-lending 20%, balance NCDs/ECBs/NBFCs; ECB hedging cost 3-3.5% via cross-currency swaps
items.quote: Cross-currency swap is something that we use to hedge our positions. The cost of hedging fluctuates from time to time, and is currently in the range of 3% to 3.5%.

items.statement: Capital adequacy 39.8% (Tier 1 39.4%), net worth Rs. 4,665 crore, book value Rs. 446/share
items.quote: Capital to risk-weighted assets was 39.8%, with Tier 1 capital at 39.4% compared to 42.6% and 42.2% at the end of June.

items.statement: CEO term until July 2028, intends to seek reappointment; no board-level role change discussions
items.quote: My current term as CEO extends until July 2028, and I intend to remain available for reappointment beyond that, subject to the requisite approvals.

items.statement: Team stability improved over 12-18 months, lower attrition driving growth momentum
items.quote: It is a reflection of the stability in the teams that we have in most of the states. Whatever we had put in place over the last 12 to 18 months is kind of bearing fruit.

items.statement: ROA 4.2%, ROE 14.9% (+40 bps QoQ); cost-to-income 30.8% (from 32.7%), opex to assets 2.6% (from 2.8%)
items.quote: Return on assets remained healthy at 4.2%, while return on equity improved by 40 basis points to 14.9%.

items.statement: AI deployment across lending lifecycle (Cue, ClariFi, BankLens, DocIQ); moving to shared data platform over 18 months
items.quote: Over the next 18 months, we will move from these point solutions to one shared data and decision platform and exte nd AI into sourcing, collections and servicing in phases

items.statement: Raised ₹150 crore via NCD public issue in Oct 2026, oversubscribed at ₹166.49 crore
items.quote: On 28th September 2026, we filed our Prospectus for a public issue of secured, rated, listed, redeemable, non-convertible debentures of ₹1,000 face value each, with a base size of ₹75 crore and a green shoe option of up to another ₹75 crore, for a total of ₹150 crore.

items.statement: Broking DP AUA rose to ₹1,66,737 crore, up ~17% from March 2026
items.quote: Our broking client base, including StoxKart, grew to 14.2 lakh as of September 2026, and broking DP AUA rose to ₹1,66,737 crore, up about 17% from March 2026.

items.statement: Mutual fund AUM at ₹4,711 crore with 91,145 running SIPs; wealth AUM/AUA grew ~25% in H1 to ₹1,464 crore
items.quote: Mutual fund AUM stood at ₹4,711 crore with 91,145 running SIPs, and our wealth AUM/AUA grew about 25% in the half year to ₹1,464 crore.

items.statement: NBFC AUM at ₹1,031 crore as of Sep 2026; disbursements ₹323 crore in H1 FY27
items.quote: Our AUM stood at ₹1,031 crore as of September 2026, with disbursements of ₹323 crore in the first half, through 41 branches across 7 states.

items.statement: Micro-LAP AUM rose to ₹172 crore from ₹121 crore; gold loans to ₹74 crore from ₹66 crore since March 2026
items.quote: Within this, our focus products are growing, micro-LAP AUM has risen to ₹172 crore from ₹121 crore in March 2026, and gold loans to ₹74 crore from ₹66 crore.

items.statement: NBFC NIM improved to 7.8% in H1 FY27 from 7.3% in FY26
items.quote: NIM improved to 7.8% in H1 FY27 from 7.3% in FY26, and the NBFC earned a profit after tax of ₹23.3 crore in the first half, close to the ₹24.6 crore it earned in the whole of FY26.

items.statement: NBFC capital adequacy ratio strengthened to 46.1%
items.quote: Our capital adequacy ratio strengthened further to 46.1%, giving us ample headroom to grow.

items.statement: Expect NBFC AUM of ₹1,125-1,150 crore by end FY27, below earlier ₹1,300 crore target
items.quote: So, AUM by the end of the year, we expect to be around Rs. 1125 to Rs. 1150 crores. But the rundown for the discontinued products, you need to understand that could have been higher in the next year, which has been shifted to this year.

items.statement: StoxKart targets >₹100 crore revenue in FY27; no break-even this year; plans ₹50 crore additional investment
items.quote: We at least aim for more than Rs. 100 crores revenue this year and good increase next year also. So, to fund this high growth, we need to keep investing in the technology and marketing. Hence, I do not see break even coming this year, but we will maintain the same level of bottom line.

items.statement: Plan to invest ₹50 crore more in StoxKart, primarily to grow MTF book
items.quote: So, we expect to invest Rs. 50 crores more in StoxKart, which will primarily be used for our increase in MTF business. We want to increase our book size in MTF.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 19.1% in Q2 FY27, stable vs 19.2% YoY; PAT margin 5.3% up 50 bps
items.quote: For the quarter ended September 2026, consolidated operational income stood at Rs. 532.5 crores, a growth of 20.9% YOY and 3.4% quarter-on-quarter. EBITDA was Rs. 101.6 crores up 20.4% YOY with an EBITDA margin of 19.1%, broadly stable as compared with 19.2% in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: H1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin 19.9%, PAT margin 6.2% up 30 bps YoY
items.quote: For the first half, consolidated operational income stood at Rs. 1047.5 crores up 21.1% YOY. EBITDA was Rs. 208.4 crores up 13.0% with a margin of 19.9% and profit after tax was Rs. 65 crores up 27.6% YOY. The PAT margin improved by 30 basis points to 6.2%.

items.statement: NBFC segment EBIT rose 43% YoY to ₹37.6 crore in Q2 FY27 on higher yields and lower cost of funds
items.quote: The Financing or NBFC segment recorded strong growth with revenue increasing by 33.6% YOY to Rs. 62 crores and segment EBIT rising by 43% to Rs. 37.6 crores supported by higher portfolio yields and a lower cost of funds.

items.statement: Expect ~20 bps increase in borrowing cost from RBI repo hike; >90% borrowings floating rate; negligible NIM impact due to yield improvement
items.quote: So, we expect 20 basis point increase in our cost gradually as and when the reset gets due. Our more than 90% of the borrowing is at floating rate. So, definitely, the borrowing cost will go up by around 20 basis points. However, as I said earlier, there has been increasing yield on our loan book as we are shifting the portfolio to more retail granular book. As explained earlier, our yields have g

items.statement: Plan to reduce unsecured loan book below 15% in ~1 year, maintain at 10-15% long term
items.quote: So, we plan to reduce the unsecured loan book further from current level. So, we expect it to be, you know, below 15% in about a year or so. And we want to maintain it, you know, at 10 to 15% level.

items.statement: Q2 brokerage revenue fell sequentially due to SEBI CAS changes from Aug 3 reducing turnover; treasury income hit by lack of arbitrage
items.quote: But since some changes in regulatory changes by SEBI, CAS, that has been introduced in August 3rd. And this was a bigger change for options and happened to closing May. And people, investors had suffered losses. And by that time, this could not be understood. And there were so many anomalies that people can manipulate the closing price. So, people suffered the losses. And in due course, people sta

items.statement: IRDAI consultation paper on insurance distribution economics is draft; impact uncertain until final guidelines
items.quote: So, as far as the consultation paper is concerned, it is a draft consultation paper, which has been open to the public and the stakeholders for their comments. So, since it is only a draft consultation paper at this point of time, we should not be able to comment on the impact of revenue and the product till the final proposal is out.

items.statement: Consolidated debt-equity 1.63x; NBFC CAR 46.1%; ratings ICRA A1+ short-term, ICRA A and CRISIL A stable long-term
items.quote: Our balance sheet remained strong. The consolidated net worth stood at Rs. 1,358 crores as of September '26 with a debt-equity ratio of 1.63x. At the NBFC level, our capital adequacy ratio was 46.1%. Our ratings stand at ICRA A1 plus for short-term borrowings and ICRA A and CRISL A with a stable outlook for long-term borrowings.

items.statement: Broking client base 14.2 lakh; online penetration 75% vs 72% end FY26
items.quote: Our broking client base, including StoxKart, grew to 14.2 lakh as of September 2026, and broking DP AUA rose to ₹1,66,737 crore, up about 17% from March 2026. Online penetration of our client base increased further to 75%, from 72% at the end of FY26.

items.statement: SMC and StoxKart fully live on new exchange Closing Auction Session and realigned pre-open from day one
items.quote: These changes improve price discovery and market integrity. They also required every broker to re-engineer trading systems at short notice, and I am pleased to say SMC and StoxKart were fully live for all clients from day one.

items.statement: Insurance gross premium H1 FY27 ₹1,598 crore; 5.78 lakh policies via 16,916 POS agents and 387 MISPs
items.quote: Gross premium for H1 FY27 stood at ₹1,598 crore, with 5.78 lakh policies issued through a network of 16,916 POS agents and 387 motor insurance service providers.

items.statement: Insurance segment aims to achieve budgeted numbers if no adverse regulatory changes
items.quote: So, we are hopeful if nothing changes or if some impacts are done, we shall be able to achieve our budgeted numbers.

items.statement: No current plan for scale-up, partnership or exit across 11 business lines; open to strategic equity investors if suitable
items.quote: Mr. Sumit, no such plan is there as of now. We can always welcome for some equity strategical investors if that is suitable to us. And that increase our credibility and capital and which suit to us. Otherwise, we are fine. We are doing well in all our vertical. We have sufficiently capitalized. So, we do not find any urgency for doing that.

items.statement: RBI repo rate hike 25 bps in Oct may pressure borrowing costs; pace of transmission and lender repricing uncertain
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are mindful that the RBI's 25 basis point repo rate hike in October may put some upward pressure on our borrowing costs, depending on the pace of transmission and lender repricing.

items.statement: Gift City market share >25%; International Gold Exchange restarted with quota system; other exchanges doing reasonably well
items.quote: You can see our market share more than 25% in gift city. So, we are doing much better.

items.statement: Full-year advances growth guidance of 30% to 35% and exit ROA of approximately 1.4% to 1.5% maintained
items.value: 30% to 35% advances growth; 1.4% to 1.5% exit ROA
items.quote: We remain focused on the full -year objective of 30% to 35% advances growth and an exit RO A of approximately 1.4% to 1.5%, while continuing to assess developments in the operating environment

items.statement: Medium-term book mix target of 45-55% between inclusive finance and retail assets maintained
items.quote: We may not be reaching 45-55 by the end of the year, but as we had stated in our earlier calls, 45-55 is the kind of a mix that we would like to maintain in the medium term.

items.statement: Gross NPAs declined to 2.9% from 6.5% in June supported by INR387 crores CGFMU claims and INR596 crores write-offs/OTS
items.quote: In line with the strategy adopted by the bank, which played out during the last credit cycle, gross NPAs de clined to 2.9% from 6.5% in June, supported by the receipt of INR387 crores of CGFMU claims in July and write-offs and OTS of INR596 crores of legacy stressed assets

items.statement: Current bucket collection efficiency for inclusive finance at 99.3% in Q2 FY27 versus 99.2% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Current bucket efficiency for IF in Q2 FY27 stood at 99.3% versus 99.2% in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: INR1,000-1,100 crores exposure in drought-affected districts of Karnataka and Maharashtra; no significant collection change in September-October
items.quote: We have around INR1,000-odd crores to INR1,100-odd crores of exposure in these affected areas. And we've not seen any significant change. Well, there's been a change over a period of last couple of quarters. September and October have not shown any significant change as of now.

items.statement: CGFMU cover for FY27 disbursements not yet opened; INR40-45 crores provisioned in H1 for premiums; full portfolio till March 2026 covered
items.quote: For the current financial year, the CGFMU cover has not opened yet. We are expecting that with the due clearances from various authorities. It should open up. We don't have any information otherwise. However, as you would know, we will make a provision of around closer to 1% to 1.5%, is around approximately closer to INR70 crores to INR80 crores for CGFMU fees.

items.statement: NIM improved 28 bps year-on-year to 7.2% in Q2 FY27 aided by growth in paying book share
items.quote: Our net interest income for the quarter stood at INR368.8 crores, a growth of 42.8% year-on-year, and NIM improved 28 basis points year-on-year to 7.2%, aided by growth in the share of our paying book.

items.statement: PSLC income dropped to INR8 crores in Q2 from INR45 crores in Q1; CLOU convenience fees increased by INR14 crores offsetting the decline
items.quote: We made around INR8-odd crores of PSLC income in Q2. My sense is that we would be making around INR5-odd crores of PSLC income in Q3, because typically the market is very modest in Q3. And I think in so far as the convenience fee from the CLOU business is concerned, we will continue to see some amount of growth in that.

items.statement: Gross advances including IBPC at INR14,972 crores, up 34.6% year-on-year; disbursements at INR3,096 crores, up 27.4% year-on-year
items.value: INR14,972 crores gross advances; INR3,096 crores disbursements
items.quote: Gross advances including IBPC stood at INR14,972 crores, representing a year-on-year growth of 34.6%. Disbursements during the quarter were INR3,096 crores, an increase of 27.4% over the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Raised INR200 crores Tier 2 capital in October improving CRAR by 1.8%; another INR200 crores planned by December or Q4 FY27
items.value: INR200 crores raised; INR200 crores planned
items.quote: The INR200 crores that we have raised in the first week of October will improve our CRAR by about 1.8%. We plan to raise another INR200 crores well before the end of the year, all things going well and the rates stabilizing.

items.statement: CRAR at 19.37% in Q2; Tier 1 comfort zone revised to 18.5-19% from earlier ~20%
items.quote: We while our comfort range for Tier 1 is approximately around 20, because understand the entire INR300 crores profit we are likely to kind of which you called out and guided. We also get to the capital adequacy in terms of CRAR, and we will also be doing I think now I'm going to instead of 20 probably to 19 and 18.5 would be the comfort zone.

items.statement: Adding 50 branches in next 4-5 months; 10 already opened; expected to add INR30 crores monthly disbursements by February
items.quote: We are adding a few branches, we'll be adding around closer to 50 branches in the next 4 months or 5 months. We already opened around 10 at this point of time, so there will be an increase contribution approximately of at least around INR50 lakhs to INR60 lakhs per branch. Around INR30 crores is likely to come from branches once their operations say probably by February.

items.statement: CASA ratio dipped to 19.4% year-on-year but CASA balances grew 26.8% year-on-year in absolute terms; retail deposits at 84.5% of total deposits
items.quote: While our CASA ratio dipped a bit year -on-year and stood at 19.4%, our CASA balances have grown 26.8% year -on-year in absolute terms. We remain focused on building a granular and sustainable deposit base supported by our branch network, customer acquisitio n efforts, and digital channels

items.statement: Cost-to-income adjusted for digital expenses at 68.7% in H1 FY27 versus 72.9% in H1 FY26; CGFMU expenses expected to remain stable as MFI share stable
items.quote: Our pre-POP has grown significantly on year-on-year basis to INR145.5 crores, with our CTI adjusted for digital expenses at 68.7% in H1 FY27 versus 72.9% in H1 FY26.

items.statement: Inclusive finance at 41% and retail assets at 59% of advances; mortgage and CV growing at 36% YoY; CLOU digital credit scaling exponentially
items.quote: We are encouraged by the quality and composition of this growth, with both inclusive finance at 41% and retail assets at 59% contributing to the expansion of our franchise.

items.statement: Over 14 lakh customers targeted under CLOU program; over 2 lakh customers onboarded via digital deposit channels
items.value: 14 lakh CLOU customers; 2 lakh digital deposit customers
items.quote: Over 14 lakh customers have been targeted under the CLOU program, and the said count is expected to increase substantially in the forthcoming quarters. Similarly, deposits mobilized digitally through various platforms, the key engine for acquiring customer s, and over 2 lakh customers have been onboarded via this channel

items.statement: Drought in Karnataka and Maharashtra may have lagged impact on collections; cautious onboarding new customers in affected districts; no material adverse impact seen yet
items.quote: While the drought conditions across Karnataka and Maharashtra have not thus far resulted in any material adverse impact on the portfolio performance or asset quality. Our bank continues to maintain a prudent approach and closely monitor the evolving situation.

items.statement: INR200 crores Tier 2 raised in October; board approved additional INR100 crores; total INR400 crores Tier 2 planned for FY27
items.quote: We have recently raised INR200 crores of Tier 2 capital as well, right? So, how would that impact your CRAR in Q3 numbers? And when can we expect the balance INR200 crores?

items.statement: CGFMU scheme renewal pending central government notification; first 10-year tenor completed; portfolio till March 2026 fully covered
items.quote: the bank. T he central government needs to notify the renewal of the program, and hence it is with the ministry, and that's what we are waiting for. Once the program gets notified again, we will make payment of our premium and continue the cover as we have done in the past

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; Senthil Kumar and Sasidhar Vavilala participated in Q&A alongside CEO, ED, CFO
items.quote: Senthil if you want to add on this. Senthil Kumar: Yes. Thanks. Right. Yes. As of now we have not seen much impact, but yes, probably we would expect some impact specifically in Marathwada area and also probably in the south of Karnataka area.

items.statement: SFB transition on track for Q1 FY28 go-live per Slide 12 timeline
items.quote: As we captured across on Slide 12, currently, as we speak, we are tracking on that kind of schedule and timetable, okay?

items.statement: First year SFB disbursal target around INR 2,000 crores in first 12 months of operations
items.quote: We are looking at anywhere around INR 2,000 crores odd, kind of, disbursal, which will be happening across the portfolios and the secured product, which we are looking at.

items.statement: Medium-term loan book target INR 8,000-10,000 crores over 3-4 years post SFB launch
items.quote: We are looking at around INR 8,000 crores to INR 10,000 crores book over a period of 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Capex of INR 120-150 crores over 1-1.5 years for SFB transition, mainly technology
items.quote: We are anticipating anything between INR 120 crores to INR 150 crores of capex over a period of 1 year to 15 months from now in terms of transitioning into SFB, the first year of SFB operational.

items.statement: Plan to open ~40 liability branches and 25-30 asset centers in first year of SFB operations
items.quote: We are also planning to open approximately 40-odd branches, liability branches and around 25 to 30 asset centers in the first year of operations.

items.statement: Loan referral disbursals INR 762 crores in Q2 FY27, up 286% YoY; H1 FY27 INR 1,390 crores surpassing full FY26
items.quote: Total disbursals in Q2 w ere INR 762 crores, up by 286% on a year -on-year basis. While for H1'27, disbursals stood at INR 1,390 crores, already surpassing full -year levels of FY26, which stood at INR 1,285 crores.

items.statement: CMS throughput grew 13% sequentially and 12% YoY to INR 20,511 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our B2B business, CMS throughput grew 13% sequentially and 12% on a Y-o-Y basis to INR 20,511 crores.

items.statement: Regaining B2B alliance volumes after Q1 dip; CMS and alliance numbers show recovery
items.quote: In Q1 FY27, our B2B and Alliance business had reduced due to skepticism of an event, which had happened. Now in Q2 and more, we are indeed working towards regaining the market share in this alliance and B2B space as seen in the CMS and alliances numbers, which I ju st stated earlier.

items.statement: Net revenue margin 38.1% in Q2 FY27, up 100 bps YoY but down 450 bps sequentially; H1 FY27 40.3% vs 35.2% YoY
items.quote: Our net revenue margin was around 38.1%, which is 100 basis points higher than the last year's net revenue margin. And however, it is lower by 450 basis points sequentially.

items.statement: Cost of funds 1.4% in Q2 FY27; expect ~4% post SFB conversion, retaining 250-300 bps advantage over traditional SFBs
items.quote: Our cost of funds for Q2'27 was 1.4%, giving Fino a structural cost advantage. Further, we expect our cost of funds to be around 4% even after SFB conversion, retaining an advantage of roughly around 250 to 300 basis points over the traditional SFBs.

items.statement: CASA contributes 52% of revenue; renewal income record INR 74.6 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: CASA segment contributed INR 174 crores or 52% of our revenue, including a record renewal income of INR 74.6 crores, which we see as one of the biggest indicators of sustainable retail income.

items.statement: CASA base 1.91 crore accounts as of Sep 2026; 8.2 lakh new accounts opened in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our CASA base is inching towards a 2-crore mark, having reached 1.91 crore as at September 2026. This quarter saw 8.2 lakh new accounts open, averaging roughly 1 new account being opened every 10 seconds.

items.statement: Digitally active customers 64.9 lakh in Sep 2026; 87.9 lakh for Q2 FY27
items.quote: Digital engagement also continues to deepen as digitally active customers in September'26 stood at 64.9 lakhs, while for the entire second quarter of FY27, it stood at 87.9 lakhs.

items.statement: Pricing competition in B2B alliances impacting take rates; focus on volume and network engagement
items.quote: Competition in this segment continues to weigh on pricing, hence our focus remains on volume and network engagement and reinstatement of our earlier B2B partners.

items.statement: Corporate BC business exit part of SFB transition plan; will be executed before RBI application
items.quote: In terms of sort of exiting the corporate BC business, it's part of our SFB transition plan, and it will be executed as per the plan before we apply to the Reserve Bank of India.

items.statement: Strengthened leadership with four senior executives for branch banking, liabilities, credit risk, MSME lending
items.quote: On the people front, we strengthened our leadership team with four senior executives who will drive branch banking, liabilities, credit risk and MSME lending.

items.statement: Average total deposits grew 12% YoY to INR 2,794 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Average total deposits grew by 12% on a Y -o-Y basis to INR 2,794 crores, continuing its growth momentum.

items.statement: 90% of deposit balances remain core/sticky per management observation
items.quote: And what we have also observed from that behavior 90% of our deposits remain as a core balance, which is very critical from a lending point of view.

items.statement: No medium-term guidance for revenue growth, EBITDA margins, ROA; FY27 treated as transition year
items.quote: We are not providing any guidance right now. We are focusing on building a strong liability franchise. So, our growth in CASA, which will be the cornerstone for our SFB launch and our loan referral business, which is a testimony to say that there is a demand for credit in our target segment, which we are dealing with.

items.statement: Relaunch of UPI B2B P2M segment on track for Q4 FY27
items.quote: On digital business front, we had indicated the relaunch of our UPI B2B P2M segment during the year, and I'm happy to share that we are on track and shall be resuming these services of this product by Q4 FY27.

items.statement: Credit risk strategy: target own customers/merchants with 3-4 years transaction history; leverage CMS network collecting INR 6,500+ crores monthly for collections
items.quote: Currently, if you see one of our business verticals is a cash management system where we currently collect around more than INR 6,500 crores every month. And 60% of these collections are for the NBFCs and the banks or the MFIs in the rural India.

items.statement: Operating cost grew 5.8% YoY and 4.5% sequentially in Q2; H1 operating cost INR 180 crores, up 1.6% YoY; cost-to-income 27.6% in Q2 vs 28.7% in Q1
items.quote: For the first half, the operating cost was around INR 180 crores, up only 1.6% year-on-year. Our cost-to-income ratio improved to 27.6% in Quarter 2 versus 28.7% in Quarter 1.

items.statement: Food and FMCG EBITDA margin guided at 3-4% for FY27; medium-term aspiration to reach high single-digit margins from FY28 onwards
items.quote: In food and FMCG, quarterly revenue grew 32% year-on-year to INR2,216 crores with an EBITDA margin of 3.2% in line with our FY27 guidance range of 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Edible oil EBITDA per MT guided at INR 4,000-4,500 for FY27 with mid-single-digit volume growth and gradual market share uptick
items.quote: In edible oil, we continue to guide on mid-single-digit volume growth, gradual uptick in market share and maintaining EBITDA per ton within our guided range of INR 4,000 to INR4,500 per metric ton.

items.statement: Industry Essentials EBITDA guided at INR 3,000-3,500 per MT; Q2 delivered INR 4,300 per MT due to better product mix
items.quote: Industry Essentials delivered EBITDA of INR4,300 per metric ton, well ahead of our guidance range of INR3,000 to INR 3,500 per MT.

items.statement: Consolidated FY27 revenue run-rate suggests INR 85,000 crores with EBITDA near INR 2,600 crores (~3% margin)
items.quote: If this run rate continues the way it is, I think we should be close to INR85,000 crores of revenue. And with the kind of rate which we are looking at as far as the EBITDA is concerned, we are there with the guidance. I think EBITDA margin, right now it is at 2.6% and maybe full year also we can be close to 3% kind of number we can look at.

items.statement: Urban demand grew faster than rural in Q2/H1; rural demand under pressure from rainfall deficit and high food inflation (~7.5%)
items.quote: See, for us, the urban grew better than rural, fact number one. But the difference between both is not that staggering. I mean, rural grew little less than urban for us. So, yes, there is some kind of pressure which we saw on the rural number one.

items.statement: Expect mid-to-high single-digit volume growth in H2 FY27 supported by festive demand despite rural sluggishness
items.quote: I feel while we have delivered H1 11%, I think full year we should be there at 8%, 9% kind of number.

items.statement: Edible oil Q2 EBITDA ~INR 4,100/MT within guided INR 4,000-4,500 range
items.quote: In edible oils, EBITDA stood at approx INR4,100 per MT during the quarter, again in line with our guided range of INR 4,000 to INR4,500 per MT.

items.statement: Branded exports grew 72% YoY in Q2; LTM branded export revenue crossed INR 800 crores
items.quote: Our HoReCa business grew 22% with LTM revenue crossing INR800 crores, while branded export delivered strong growth of 72% year-on-year.

items.statement: Investing heavily in modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce channels for food and FMCG distribution expansion
items.quote: We are investing quite heavily on this channels. We are also investing on urban towns where these products are been bought more.

items.statement: Direct retail reach at 9.7 lakh outlets; total retail reach ~26 lakh outlets; focus on improving throughput and outlet productivity
items.quote: Our direct retail reach now stands at 9.7 lakh s outlets, while our total retail reach remains at around 26 lakhs outlet.

items.statement: Finance cost increase from inventory funding recovered through pricing; profitability not impacted
items.quote: Most of the finance cost which increase, we recover it in our pricing part. And therefore, in spite of increase in finance cost, you will see that profitability has not been impacted as such.

items.statement: Standardized pack sizes mandated from September favorable for branded players; eliminates grammage wars and boosts volumes
items.quote: Yes, the standardized pack is always favorable for branded companies like us because then you have a value level playing field across. And standardized pack will also to some extent increase the volumes for us.

items.statement: Industry Essentials: Oleochemicals and specialty chemicals now 45% of segment revenue, driving margin upside
items.quote: Oleochemicals and specialty chemicals now contribute around 45% of segment revenue, reflecting the increased importance of this business.

items.statement: Tops (GD Foods) growing 25%+ post-acquisition; expanding from North to East and Central India over next 1-1.5 years
items.quote: We have been able to leverage AWL distribution and of course the growth is significantly good there. We have been growing at plus of 25% in GD Foods.

items.statement: Brand equity allows sustaining prices despite commodity volatility; import duty cut impacts unbranded players more
items.quote: It will not impact the profitability as such because of the fact that we have a brand in front of us and it impacts to usually the players where who do no t have a brand equity in the

items.statement: Inventory increased INR 6,000 crores in H1 due to sluggish September and sunflower supply chain disruption; funded via working capital lines; expected to normalize in Q3 (OND)
items.quote: So, because of that the inventory buildup, actually inventories have gone up by INR6,000 crores, not INR600 crores and that is primarily been then funded through our working capital lines. And that's why the lines which funded this INR 6,000 crores is more of a funded lines and therefore gone into cash flow presentation into the financing part of it. And therefore, the cash flow from the operation

items.statement: Trade credit of INR 8,500 crores is non-funded supplier LCs for imports; not included in net debt calculation
items.quote: See this 8,500 of trade credit is nothing but a suppliers credit which we obtain for our imports. Okay, and its not a basically a fund based. Fund based line which we have used for the money. I think for calculating net debt, this 8,500 should not be considered.

items.statement: Inventory buildup funded through working capital lines increasing finance cost; cost recovered via pricing
items.quote: And that's why the lines which funded this INR 6,000 crores is more of a funded lines and therefore gone into cash flow presentation into the financing part of it. And therefore, the cash flow from the operation is shown as negative.

items.statement: Rainfall deficit 12-13% nationally, >30% in key wheat states may impact Kharif harvest and Rabi sowing; rural demand already weaker than urban
items.quote: Number two, with this deficit in rainfall of 12%, 13% across overall India and then couple of territories experiencing deficit more than 30%, 35%, 40% also and with the wheat growing areas of like Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab where deficit I understand is more than 30%. So, therefore, this may have some impact on the Kharif harvest and the Rabi sowing.

items.statement: Food inflation at 7-7.5% and headline CPI near 6% may dampen demand; festive season expected to offset some pressure
items.quote: The inflation is again another spoil factor which is going on right now, which is sitting at a very high with headline CPI touching close to 6% as we speak today. And within that CPI, 6% food inflation is already at 7%, 7.5% kind of level.

items.statement: Food and FMCG revenue grew 32% YoY to INR 2,216 crores in Q2; H1 volume growth 24%, revenue growth 27%
items.quote: Our food and FMCG business remains a key growth driver, delivering 32% revenue growth and crossing INR2,200 crores in quarterly revenues.

items.statement: Edible oil volume grew 5% in Q2; market share maintained via domestic oils (mustard, groundnut, cottonseed)
items.quote: Moving to edible oils, the business delivered a 5% volume growth during the quarter. Despite a challenging operating environment, we maintained our market share supported by growth in domestic oils, particularly mustard, groundnut and cottonseed oil.

items.statement: Industry Essentials volume grew 25% in Q2; oleochemicals & specialty chemicals 45% of revenue; FY growth guided at high single to low double digit
items.quote: Industry Essentials delivered another strong quarter with volume growth of 25% supported by continued momentum in oleochemicals and specialty chemicals.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 revenue growth guidance 18-20%, EBITDA margin 40-45%, PAT margin 25-30%
items.value: 18-20% revenue growth, 40-45% EBITDA margin, 25-30% PAT margin
items.quote: The growth in revenue will continue to be in the range of 18% to 20% with EBITDA margins in the range of 40% to 45%, and PAT margins in the range of 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin 40% including Ascent, 45.8% excluding Ascent; target full-year average 40%
items.quote: EBITDA margins for Q2, excluding Ascent were 45.8%, and including Ascent were 40%. That is the aim that we are targeting that we will end the year including Ascent with a consolidated EBITDA margin of 40%.

items.statement: International pipeline at ~US$47 million, up from ~US$20 million 12 months ago; six deals over $4-5 million TCV
items.quote: The pipeline itself currently stands at roughly US$ 47 million dollars. Now, that used to be roughly around 20 million about 12 months back.

items.statement: 18 new international clients in transition, expected to go live in coming 1-2 quarters
items.quote: We have added 18 new clients, which are in the transition and they are expected to go live into the coming quarter to two, depending upon the transition timelines.

items.statement: Issuer solutions targeting 20%+ year-on-year growth for FY27; Jio Platforms IPO completed 12 hours ahead with <40ms latency
items.quote: On the issuer solutions, I think, we are looking at a 20% total year-on-year growth. And again, with a little bit of luck from the market and depending upon how some of the other larger IPOs are also around the corner, including the Jio one, of course, I believe that we should get to a 20% plus top-end growth.

items.statement: Pensions grew 42% YoY vs industry 12-13%; AIF/wealth revenue and yields grew despite flattish AUM due to mark-to-market
items.quote: Pensions too, entire of last year, we grew 3x of the pace of the industry. Industry grew at about 12. KFin grew at 36. This year, we have grown faster than that, I think 42% as against similar 12% to 13% growth of the industry.

items.statement: Aria.AI generative AI platform beta live, public launch later this month; FinEx mutual fund platform ~30-35% deployed, full rollout by end Q4 FY27
items.quote: We have launched a couple of very important platforms in the mutual fund space. Aria.AI is India's and probably world's first generative AI intelligence platform, not just for purchase and redemption and commercial transactions, but also for all non-commercial transactions.

items.statement: Issuer solutions, pensions, wealth next-gen AI/cloud platforms going live by January; GFS international replatforming underway
items.quote: So, we will be live with the issuer solutions, pensions, and wealth in the next three months. So, by January we should have gone live with many of these next generation AI native, cloud native platforms.

items.statement: Ascent EBITDA margin improved from -12% YoY to ~8% in Q2; targeting double-digit EBITDA in next couple of quarters, ~20%+ next fiscal year
items.quote: But again, thanks to some really wonderful work by the business development teams. In each of the operating geographies, we continue to grow 30% plus on Ascent. And again, with a committed focus on cost optimization, the margin profile continues to expand. We hope to hit double-digit EBITDA numbers in the next couple of quarters or so.

items.statement: MF yield expanded ~2% sequentially; ~50% from pricing discipline, ~30% from AMC mix, rest from asset mix; pricing expected to remain consistent
items.quote: So, I will take the first one in terms of the yield and it is in a marginal expansion, roughly about 2% sequentially. As I always say, there are three important factors. If I were to put a weightage, the weightage may change depending upon quarters and times of the year. But roughly about half of the reason in terms of the instability or otherwise is owing to the pricing discipline, and about 30-o

items.statement: Overall AUM for KFin clients grew 15% vs industry 13%; SIP market share ~37%, expecting 100bps bridge over 3-5 years
items.quote: The overall AUM for KFin Tech clients this quarter had grown at 15%, whereas industry grew at 13%. So, that is very heartening. Now, it is also, however, true that the share of the passives for our clients seem to be on the higher side as compared to that of industry.

items.statement: Market share >33% overall, equity inching to 33%; 6 of 10 fastest-growing AMCs are KFin clients
items.quote: Overall market share has grown in the last two quarters for KFin Tech in the form of overall moving beyond 33% and the equity inching close to 33% as well. Our market share on the SIPs, which I continue to believe is the bellwether in terms of where long-term averages could be at, continues to be close to about 37%.

items.statement: Healthy cash and equivalents ~Rs 550 crore after dividend payout; H1 FY27 diluted EPS Rs 10.12
items.quote: We maintain healthy cash and equivalent situation of about Rs. 550 crores after the dividend was paid out. And the diluted EPS at the end of H1 stands at Rs. 10.12.

items.statement: Ascent gap to cash positive ~Rs 3.5-4 crore; expected to turn EPS positive in coming quarters
items.quote: The overall gap from turning cash positive is roughly about Rs. 3.5 crores to Rs. 4 crore, which isn't substantial and something that we should be able to turn EPS positive as well to the coming quarters.

items.statement: Plan to move international business to GIFT City for 20-year tax holiday; process initiated but will take time
items.quote: We are looking at moving over a period of time to the GIFT City, which should give us the advantage of 20 year tax holiday. So, it is a process that has been initiated, but it will take some time.

items.statement: Headcount rationalized across KFin and Ascent; finance, HR, tech functions consolidated; finance now managed from India
items.quote: For example, much of the finance function is managed by Amit Murarka, who sits in India. And likewise, aspects around tech and HR, and even certain aspects on operations also given Ascent has its operations in India, in Hyderabad, in Mumbai, so on and so forth, many of the locations that we are ever since organically be part of.

items.statement: Buffers for market downturn include deferring discretionary spend (transformational IT, automation, geography expansion, product launches) to protect margins
items.quote: Now, these are obviously for the future benefit. So, transformational items, discretionary IT projects, discretionary automation, discretionary expansion of probably a particular geography, which we have planned for so on and so forth, or even launch of certain products, which cost certain amount of business development dollars.

items.statement: Q2 revenue up 13% QoQ, expenses up only 3% QoQ; 18.7% sequential EBITDA growth, 32% YoY; H1 EBITDA up 13.4% YoY
items.value: 13% QoQ revenue growth, 3% QoQ expense growth
items.quote: Sequentially, expenses have gone up only by 3% quarter-on-quarter, while the revenue quarter-on-quarter went up by about 13%. And we believe that this will continue to play out in Q3 and Q4 as well.

items.statement: Cloud/compute costs doubled/tripled, offsetting productivity gains from AI/RPA; benefit expected if AI trade slows and costs decline
items.quote: Of course, there had been compensatory offsetting because of cloud costs, infra costs, as we all know, the memory and the compute space, and energy and all of these costs have doubled and tripled.

items.statement: Ascent integration on track; rationalization of duplicate functions completed; replatforming onto KFin proprietary platform underway
items.quote: Our acquisition of Ascent and its integration is one of the most strategically important initiatives that we have embarked on. Happy to inform you that we continue to grow the business again, against an extremely challenging macro.

items.statement: Ascent growing 30%+ in each operating geography despite Middle East headwinds (25% of revenue); growth offset by Americas and Singapore
items.quote: In each of the operating geographies, we continue to grow 30% plus on Ascent. And again, with a committed focus on cost optimization, the margin profile continues to expand.

items.statement: 80-90 AIF funds contracted but not yet launched; net retention rate higher than ever; Q3/Q4 typically stronger for Ascent
items.quote: But we have, even today, a little around 80 plus funds, 80 or 90 funds, which have been already contracted, but the fund manager is yet to launch and or is expected to launch in the coming weeks or a month or so.

items.statement: Value-added services now 7.5% of total revenue; targeting double-digit VAS share in 3-4 quarters for revenue predictability
items.quote: It is now 7.5% of the total revenue of the organization. Again, I remember probably three or four quarters back talking about one of the other internal goals, sub-goals we have is to get the value-added solutions to double-digit figure in the next three to four quarters.

items.statement: Confident estimates unchanged despite recent market correction; enough buffers to cushion tactical downturn unless protracted
items.quote: And so far, this quarter gives us a lot of heart that strategy had been on the right path. And even as I look at our upcoming forecast for this quarter and the subsequent quarter, despite the headwinds, I am still confident that we do not have to change any of the estimates at this point in time, unless there is a continual protracted downturn from here on as well.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected slightly better than historical 18-19%
items.quote: we would continue to kind of consider the growth for this financial year slightly better than our historical growth of 18%.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin target 38-40% as new businesses ramp up
items.quote: our sense is that over the next few years, we should be in the range of 38% to 40%, which has been our historical EBITDA margins, once these business units start to contribute in the overall business.

items.statement: Effective tax rate guided at 24-25% for rest of FY27 and FY28
items.quote: So, the tax rate would be in the range of 24-25%.

items.statement: Capex guidance Rs 50-60 crore each for FY27 and FY28, total Rs 100-120 crore
items.quote: for this year and the next year, we expect around Rs. 50-60 crore each every year, the CapEx, which is in the tune of Rs. 100-120 crores.

items.statement: Unit-I utilisation 75%, Unit-III 55%, Unit-II (oral solids) 21%, Unit-IV (injectables) 5%
items.value: Unit I stood at 75% and Unit III at 55%. And I mentioned earlier that Unit II is 21% and Unit IV is 5%
items.quote: the utilization for Unit I stood at 75% and Unit III at 55%. And I mentioned earlier that Unit II is 21% and Unit IV is 5%.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 gross margin 76.2%, down ~400 bps YoY due to higher raw material prices and product mix
items.quote: Gross margin for Q uarter 2 FY ‘27 stood at 76.2%, contracting by approximately 400 basis points on year-on-year basis, primarily due to higher raw material prices and changes in the product mix

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 33.0% vs 33.2% YoY; ex-new facilities ~37.8%
items.quote: For H1 FY '27, EBITDA margins remained fairly stable at 33.0% compared to 33.2% in H1 FY '26, despite the contraction in gross margins.

items.statement: Expect full-year margin recovery via revenue growth, cost optimization, inventory management and renewable energy benefits
items.quote: However, on a full-year basis, we expect to recover the margin impact to an improvement in revenue coupled with effective cost optimization measures and optimum inventory management.

items.statement: Injectables facility: several large customer audits completed, contracts expected to materialize in H2 FY27
items.quote: in the last couple of months, we have had several inspections or audits by our potential customers and we continue to engage with them. So, things are progressing quite well on that front, and we are quite optimistic that in, as we have mentioned in the past as well, that in H2 we should see some of these contracts materializing.

items.statement: Injectables TAM ~Rs 5,000 crore; targeting ~Rs 300 crore revenue in 3-4 years from domestic/export markets
items.quote: I would say that the TAM for the injectable products that we do is close to around Rs. 5,000 crores, of which we have kind of built in around Rs. 300 crores top line over the next 3 to 4 years from the domestic/export markets.

items.statement: API:Formulation revenue mix steady at ~80:20; gross margins expected to revert to historical levels as input costs normalize
items.quote: for the 6 months, it is around 80-20. So, it has been pretty much in line with what we have, which is the 80/20 split and

items.statement: No pricing pressure; gaining customers by offering competitive pricing due to fermentation scale and productivity advantages
items.quote: we haven't seen any pricing pressure when it comes to Concord, but yes, we have been able to gain customers because of the price reduction compared to their current existing suppliers.

items.statement: Raw material cost increases (solvents) viewed as temporary; addressing via R&D and productivity improvements rather than pass-through
items.quote: When it comes to raw material pricing, it is quite challenging, I would say, to pass on some of the costs that we have incurred to the customers. I think, we would rather try to address these issues through R&D and through productivity improvements rather than passing these.

items.statement: Broad-based 25% YoY revenue growth in Q2 FY27 across all product categories and geographies; immunosuppressants high double-digit, oncology nearly doubled
items.quote: Revenues for Q2 FY '27 grew 25% year-on-year. For the first half of the year, the 6 months ended 30th September 2026, revenue grew 26% over the same period last year.

items.statement: Anti-infectives, antifungal, oncology driving recent growth; Nystatin, Mupirocin, Fusidic acid, Fidaxomicin, Romidepsin, Everolimus seeing traction
items.quote: the growth over the last 6 months has been significantly in the anti-infectives, antifungal and the oncology. So last year, like around a year and a half back, we had commercialized Nystatin and as I had mentioned earlier also, we continue to gain traction there.

items.statement: Added several new customers in anti-infectives, antifungal, oncology; key markets US, Latin America, Japan; immunosuppressants gaining wallet share and second-source conversions
items.quote: We have added quite a few customers as new product additions are happening, particularly in the anti-infectives, antifungal segments.

items.statement: USFDA inspection of Unit-II (Valthera) completed successfully; ANVISA approval received for Unit-III (Limbasi)
items.quote: We successfully completed the USFDA inspection of our Unit-II formulation facility at Valthera, Ahmedabad. We also received ANVISA approval for our Unit-III facility at Limbasi.

items.statement: ANDA approvals received for Tofacitinib and Mycophenolate Mofetil Oral Suspension; US DMF filed for Fidaxomicin
items.quote: We received AND A approvals for Tofacitinib and Mycophenolate Mofetil Oral Suspension which strengthen our formulation portfolio. We also filed a Drug Master File for Fidaxomicin in the US

items.statement: API business historical growth 18-19%; expect slightly higher going forward plus injectables, CDMO, formulations as additional drivers
items.quote: Historically, we have grown at around 18-19% and I think it would be safe to kind of build on assuming our historical growth numbers. Of course, beyond that, there are contributors like the injectables, like the CDMO and the finished formulations.

items.statement: CDMO: one commercial project ~$2 million annual revenue; several development-stage projects; exclusive manufacturer for an NCE product
items.quote: the $2 million that we mentioned was more so from an annual perspective because currently we have one project where we are commercial.

items.statement: Zero-debt balance sheet maintained; cash and equivalents ~Rs 445 crore as of Sep 30, 2026
items.quote: Concord continues to maintain a zero-debt balance sheet with cash and cash equivalents of around Rs. 445 crores as of September 30, 2026.

items.statement: 1:1 bonus issue approved by shareholders, to take effect in coming weeks
items.quote: board recommendation of 1:1 bonus issue has been approved by shareholders and will take effect in the coming weeks.

items.statement: Launched Inspira dermatology division targeting eczema, anti-infectives, antifungal, acne; India TAM ~Rs 5,000 crore; aim Rs 400-500 crore revenue in 4-5 years
items.quote: Of course, going to the levels of close to Rs. 400-500 crores, I would say it would take at least four to five years to kind of start building, having a significant market share in these products.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties and supply chain disruptions driving solvent price increases; viewed as temporary
items.quote: primarily driven by an increase in raw material prices, particularly the solvents, amidst ongoing geopolitical uncertainties and broader supply chain disruptions. We believe these pressures are temporary in nature.

items.statement: Stellon Biotech (US front-end) ramping up; meaningful revenue contribution expected in H2 FY27 as products gain traction
items.quote: we should start seeing meaningful contributions coming from Stellon in the second half of the year because the first half of the year has been more about providing them the quantities and them trying to get traction with the customers.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of around INR170 crores
items.quote: So, we have said that it will reach up to INR170 crores.

items.statement: Current order book of INR133 crores, expected to reach INR170 crores soon
items.quote: At present, we have got for this year the order book of around INR133 crores, and more and more containers, basically we are negotiating more orders. So, we expect very soon this will be around INR170 crores.

items.statement: Order book comprises 50% innovative containers developed in last 7-9 months
items.quote: And basically, the order book is almost 50% comprises the innovations we did in last 7 months, 8 months, 9 months, and 50% is the normal containers.

items.statement: Rewari facility at 70-80% utilization (5,400 TEUs of 7,000 TEU capacity); Shivlakha facility has 10,000 TEU container capacity and 2,400 wagons/year
items.quote: Rewari facility has got around 7,000 TEUs capacity. Last year, we manufactured around 5,400 TEUs. So, we are using almost a 75% to 80% of the capacity available at Rewari. The Shivlakha facility is this integrated facility. Present capacity is around 10,000 TEUs. Along with that, we have got capacity for wagon manufacturing, which is around 2,400 per year.

items.statement: INR100 crore debt sanctioned from HDFC Bank; INR1,400 crores estimated for 100,000 TEU capacity expansion
items.quote: And then we have got sanctioned of around INR100 crores debt from HDFC Bank. Whenever required, we will use that also.

items.statement: Container manufacturing PAT margin 10-11%; ICD/rail terminal EBITDA margin 25-30%; wagon manufacturing lower value addition (60-70% bought-out)
items.quote: So basically margins in the container activity will remain around 10% to 11% PAT I'm telling, not that big a PAT. And ICD operations and trade terminal operations and margin EBITDA, there we can discuss a bit, there will be around in the range of 25% to 30%.

items.statement: New innovative containers: stainless steel (tare weight 6.5t to 4t), foldable, two-wheeler (72-90 bikes), open-top dwarf for steel, wide 20ft open-roof (33t wheat vs 26-27t), 40ft super high-cube for cotton (200 bales/34t)
items.quote: We have decreased the payload to the tare weight of this container from 6.5 ton to 4 ton so that you can load 2.4 ton -- 2.5 ton extra in these containers. And then in that series, we have innovated a very new type of containers, that is foldable containers.

items.statement: New customers added: JSW Ports (~1,500 containers), Indian Navy, Central Warehousing Corporation (INR30 crores orders); not dependent on single customer
items.quote: This period has been Pristine Logistics, JSW Ports, Western Carrier, Central Warehousing Corporation, Indian Navy, Container Corporation, Amba Coach Builders, Rail Connect, and HTPL. So, basically, you will appreciate every time our customer keeps on changing.

items.statement: Government approved INR10,000 crore container manufacturing scheme; company expects to qualify as brownfield with 25,000 TEU capacity; guidelines awaited
items.quote: In fact, let me tell you, basically, I think we all have to have the patience to keep the patience for that because these are all the government policies. Which means the government will issue the guideline, detailed guidelines and all regarding this.

items.statement: New foundry investment of INR80-90 crores planned for next financial year after wagon orders stabilize
items.quote: The new foundry that has to come, that is now that means, it will it may start in the next financial year, it will not be there in this financial year. Because once we stabilize production, then we will think of, because that is a big investment, maybe INR80 crores to INR90 crores.

items.statement: Target to expand container capacity from 17,000 TEU to 25,000 TEU for scheme eligibility; 60 acres reserved for potential 100,000 TEU facility
items.quote: We have to increase our capacity, present capacity is around 17,000 TEUs with us. We have to take this capacity to around 25,000.
